topics.title: New and existing connections when FortiNAC-F is unreachable – keep access up with a backup RADIUS server and fallback VLAN
topics.summary: DescriptionWhat happens to new and existing endpoint connections when FortiNAC-F cannot be reached, and how to keep network access available. It covers FortiNAC-F down, an HA failover in progress, a FortiNAC-F port or interface down, and a fault in the network path (link, routing, firewall policy).ScopeFortiNAC-F (all versions), standalone or HA (Layer 2 or Layer 3). FortiGate with FortiAP (Wi-Fi) and managed FortiSwitch (wired); FortiOS version notes are given in the steps where behavior differs. RADIUS-based access (802.1X with any EAP method and MAC authentication) and VLAN steering via SNMP/CLI.SolutionIdentify the failure condition:Every failure below looks the same to the FortiGate or FortiSwitch: FortiNAC-F does not answer.FortiNAC-F appliance or its services are down.An HA failover is in progress. Failover takes approximately 10 to 15 minutes, and only the node in control answers RADIUS.The FortiNAC-F port1 interface is down, or its service access (allowaccess) is missing.The network path is broken: link, routing, or a firewall policy blocking RADIUS (UDP 1812/1813), SNMP or SSH.The FortiGate tries the primary, then the secondary, then the backup RADIUS server. The backup server answers only when neither FortiNAC-F node does.Expected behavior of existing and new connections:FortiNAC-F only acts when an endpoint connects, re-authenticates or changes state. Existing sessions are therefore not dropped when FortiNAC-F goes away; what fails is the next authentication.Access methodExisting connectionsNew or re-authenticating connectionsWi-Fi 802.1X (PEAP, EAP-TLS, any EAP method)Stay connected until the client disconnects, roams without a cached key, or re-authenticatesFail. WPA-Enterprise cannot fail open, because the client key comes from the RADIUS Access-AcceptWi-Fi RADIUS MAC authenticationStay connected until the client reconnectsNot authorized until a RADIUS server answersWired 802.1X / MAB on managed FortiSwitchStay authorized. If the re-authentication timer expires while the server is down, the client stays in its VLAN in state SERVER_TIMEOUTFail, unless a RADIUS timeout VLAN is configured on the portWired VLAN steering through SNMP/CLIPorts stay in their current VLANStay in whatever VLAN the port has (often registration or isolation). FortiNAC-F cannot move them, and its captive portal, isolation DNS and DHCP are unavailableFor all methods, no FortiNAC-F policy, registration, VLAN change, CoA or Persistent Agent update is processed until FortiNAC-F is reachable again. The longer the outage, the more existing sessions reach a re-authentication and fail.Configure RADIUS server redundancy on the FortiGate:Define both FortiNAC-F nodes by their physical IP addresses (not the HA Shared IP), and a backup RADIUS server (FortiAuthenticator or NPS) as the tertiary server. The same RADIUS object serves FortiAP SSIDs and managed FortiSwitch 802.1X policies. Use IPv4 addresses, not FQDNs.config user radius edit "FNAC-RADIUS" set server "10.10.10.11" set secondary-server "10.10.20.11" set tertiary-server "10.10.30.11" set timeout 5 set status-ttl 300 next endFailover to the next server happens only when a server does not respond. An Access-Reject is a response and does not trigger failover.Prepare the backup RADIUS server:Import the same root and issuing CA used for client certificates (EAP-TLS), or join the same directory (PEAP). Add the FortiGate as a RADIUS client with its own shared secret.Return a default or restricted VLAN in the Access-Accept (Tunnel-Type, Tunnel-Medium-Type, Tunnel-Private-Group-Id), or no VLAN to use the SSID or port default. This choice sets the fail-open or fail-closed posture of the site. FortiNAC-F policies, registration and CoA are not applied while the backup server answers.Optionally, pre-stage a disabled emergency WPA2/WPA3-Personal SSID that administrators enable manually during an extended outage.Configure a RADIUS timeout VLAN on managed FortiSwitch ports:For wired 802.1X, a managed FortiSwitch can place the port in a timeout VLAN when the RADIUS server does not answer. This is a true fail-open option for wired access.config switch-controller security-policy 802-1X edit "FNAC-8021X" set user-group "FNAC-RADIUS-GRP" set authserver-timeout-vlan enable set authserver-timeout-period 10 RADIUS -> Configuration. When it is Enabled, the HA health check fails and FortiNAC-F fails over.Confirm which condition is present:Test the RADIUS object from the FortiGate. Failed (no response) means no server answered. A plain failed means a server answered with Access-Reject, so FortiNAC-F is reachable.FGT # diagnose test authserver radius FNAC-RADIUS pap testuser authenticate 'testuser' against 'pap' failed(no response), assigned_rad_session_id=562149323 session_timeout=0 secs idle_timeout=0 secs!Check the reachability state of each server (0 = Unreachable, 1 = Reachable, -1 = Undetermined):FGT # diagnose test application fnbamd 6Collect the fnbamd debug while a client connects:FGT # diagno

topics.title: FortiManager purges YouTube video filters after FortiGate is upgraded from FortiOS 7.2 branch to 7.4.2 or above
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiManager may attempt to purge YouTube video filters during the first Policy Package installation after a managed FortiGate is upgraded from FortiOS 7.2 to FortiOS 7.4.2 or above. This article describes the cause of the issue and provides workarounds.ScopeFortiGate 7.4.2, FortiManager 7.4SolutionIn FortiOS 7.2 branch, YouTube video filters are configured under "config videofilter youtube-channel-filter", as shown in the example below:config videofilter youtube-channel-filter edit 1 set name config entries edit 1 set comment "Fortinet YouTube channel" set action allow set channel-id "UCJHo4AuVomwMRzgkA5DQEOA" next end next endAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.2 or above, due to video filter customization and control enhancements, YouTube video filters are moved under "config videofilter profile", as depicted below:config videofilter profile edit config filters edit 1 set comment "Fortinet YouTube channel" set type channel set channel "UCJHo4AuVomwMRzgkA5DQEOA" set action allow next edit 2 set comment "Automatically generated during upgrade." set type channel set channel "any" set action block next edit 3 set comment "Automatically generated during upgrade." set type category set category "any" set action block next end next endIf you install a Policy Package after upgrading a managed FortiGate to FortiOS 7.4.2 or above, FortiManager may attempt to purge all YouTube video filters. This is shown in the Install Preview example below:=== Preview result === config videofilter profile edit config filters purge end next endSolutionTo overcome this issue, two solutions are proposed:Perform a "retrieve config" and then an "Import Configuration"Create a CLI script containing the whole "config videofilter profile" section from the FortiGate unit running FortiOS 7.4.2 or above and then run it in the Policy Package or ADOM Database

topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the newly introduced HA cluster failover health check mechanism and compares it with the legacy failover process.ScopeFortiNAC version 7.6.7+.SolutionPreviously, the failover mechanism relied on a series of ping checks to determine the status of the primary node. With the default settings, a failover would be triggered after five consecutive ping failures, each occurring at 30-second intervals.Starting with firmware version 7.6.7, a new mechanism is introduced:fnacf-prim # diagnose system health-check display cluster ===================== Primary Check Interval (s) 10 Primary Check Max Retries 10With the default settings, this health check runs 10 times at 10-second intervals before a failover decision is made:fnacf-sec # diagnose tail -F output.processManager 2026-11-27 11:08:21.344 +0100 [main] INFO yams.CampusManager - fnacf-sec.eb.eu(Secondary) status: Primary In Control Idle(false) In Control(false) Max Memory (KBytes) 1,048,576 Free Memory (KBytes) 895,989 Threads: 45 Up Time: 2 Days 23 Hours 16 Minutes 57 Seconds Time Zone: CET (UTC+0100) 2026-11-27 11:08:21.668 +0100 [cluster-health-check-2] INFO c.b.s.s.s.t.ClusterHealthCheckTask - node FNVXCATM26000001 connectivity failed, mark as reconnecting, currentFailedCount=1, maxRetry=10 2026-11-27 11:08:21.668 +0100 [cluster-health-check-2] INFO c.b.s.s.s.t.ClusterHealthCheckTask - node FNVXCATM26000001 failed is unhealthy, mark as warning, currentFailedCount=1, maxRetry=10 . 2026-11-27 11:10:11.882 +0100 [cluster-health-check-2] INFO c.b.s.s.s.t.ClusterHealthCheckTask - topics.title: Unable to delete a local certificate ('The entry is used by other X entries' / Return code -23) when replacing a wildcard certificate
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to resolve the CLI error The entry is used by other 1 entries (Command fail. Return code -23) when attempting to delete an incorrect local wildcard certificate from a FortiGate before uploading the correct certificate.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionWhen an incorrect wildcard certificate is uploaded to a FortiGate, uploading the replacement certificate can fail if the existing entry conflicts with it. FortiOS prevents deleting any certificate that is still referenced by another configuration object (such as an SSL/SSH inspection profile, admin GUI settings, or SSL VPN).Note: Make sure that the certificate is not applied to the configurationExample in GUI:Navigate to Security Profiles -> SSL/SSH Inspection.Edit the referenced profile.Change the CA Certificate or Server Certificate away from the incorrect wildcard certificate and select OK.Commands to delete the certificate:config vpn certificate local delete " " endUpload the new certificate and it should be uploaded successfully.

topics.title: FortiGate NP7: Checking NP Port and PHY Status Information
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to check NP7 network processor port information, link status, and physical layer configuration on FortiGate devices using NP7.The commands covered in this article provide details about NP port connectivity, link status, speed, auto-negotiation, FEC configuration, and link-recovery statistics.ScopeFortiGate devices using NP7FortiGate 1800F / 1801F and other supported NP7 platformsSolutionUse the following command to display NP port information:FortiGate-1801F # diagnose npu np7 np-port NP_port SerDes Lane Link Swid Port LP_link LP_speed LP_AN LP_FEC_s LP_FEC_a Link_chg Link_rcvr Rcvr_busy Link_err Update PktGen ------- ------ ---- ---- ---- ---- ------- ------- ----- -------- -------- -------- --------- --------- --------- --------- --------- np0_0 0 0 Up 1 41 Up 100000 On CL91 CL91 1 0 17 0 310760 0 np0_4 1 0 Up 1 45 Up 100000 On CL91 CL91 1 0 21 0 310756 0 ------- ------ ---- ---- ---- ---- ------- ------- ----- -------- -------- -------- --------- --------- --------- --------- --------- Total : 2 Rcvr_alarm : 50 * Link_chg: Link change count. * Link_rcvr: Link-recovery count. * Rcvr_busy: Link-recovery busy count. * Rcvr_alarm: Threshold of link-recovery failure message.Field DescriptionFieldDescriptionNP_portNP7 port identifierSerDesSerDes identifierLaneSerDes lane numberLinkNP port link statusSwidSoftware interface identifierPortAssociated software port informationLP_linkLink partner link statusLP_speedLink partner speedLP_ANLink partner auto-negotiation statusLP_FEC_sLink partner FEC settingLP_FEC_aLink partner FEC advertised or active informationLink_chgLink change countLink_rcvrLink-recovery countRcvr_busyLink-recovery busy countCorrelating NP Port Information with ISF Port DetailsThe NP port information can be correlated with the ISF port details using the following command:fnsysctl cat /proc/net/bcm/statsThis command provides additional ISF port statistics, including the software port information.It can be used in conjunction with diagnose npu np7 np-port to correlate the NP port information with the corresponding ISF and software port details.Checking NP7 PHY StatusUse the following command to display the NP7 PHY status:diagnose npu np7 phy-statusThis command displays the ISF port attachment configuration, link speed, auto-negotiation status, FEC settings, and link-training information.FortiGate-1801F # diagnose npu np7 phy-status SerDes FEC_s FEC AN_s AN PMA_mode_s PMA_mode PCS_mode_s PCS_mode AN_LT_Done AN_in_prog AN_retry LT_retry AN_done_waitAN_poll_us AN_poll_delay_ms ------ ----- ----- ---- ---- ---------- -------- ---------- -------- ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------------- np0-0 On On On On 25G 25G 100G 100G Yes No 10 30 2000 100000 100 np0-1 On On On On 25G 25G 100G 100G Yes No 10 30 2000 100000 100 ------ ----- ----- ---- ---- ---------- -------- ---------- -------- ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------------- * AN: Auto-negotiation. * PMA_mode: {25G|10G}. * PCS_mode: {4X10G|4X25G|40G|100G}. * AN_LT_Done: Auto-negotiation. & link-training done. * xx_s: Initial settings of link parameters. * AN_in_prog: AN in progress. * AN_retry: Number of of AN retry. * LT_retry: Number of link-straining retry. * AN_done_wait: Wait time after AN-LT done(msecs). * Command to customize paramters: * echo > np7/phy_list.Field DescriptionFieldDescriptionSerDesSerDes port identifierFEC_sInitial FEC settingFECCurrent FEC statusAN_sInitial auto-negotiation settingANCurrent auto-negotiation statusPMA_mode_sInitial PMA modePMA_modeCurrent PMA modePCS_mode_sInitial PCS modePCS_modeCurrent PCS modeAN_LT_DoneIndicates whether auto-negotiation and link training are completeAN_in_progIndicates whether auto-negotiation is in progressAN_retryNumber of auto-negotiation retriesLT_retryNumber of link-training retriesAN_done_waitWait time after auto-negotiation and link-training completion, in millisecondsThese commands can help identify port connectivity issues, link instability, auto-negotiation problems, FEC mismatches, and link-training failures on NP7-based FortiGate platforms.

topics.title: How to cancel a stuck FortiGate federated firmware upgrade
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen attempting to cancel an existing FortiGate federated firmware upgrade by modifying the federated-upgrade status directly, the error "Federated upgrade cannot be configured directly. Please use 'execute federated-upgrade ...' to configure" may be encountered.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms:A scheduled firmware upgrade is displayed in the FortiGate GUI under System -> Firmware & Registration, even though automatic firmware upgrade is disabled under FortiGuard settings.When checking the FortiGuard configuration, the following observations may be made:Automatic firmware upgrade is disabled under 'config system fortiguard'The FortiGate is not a member of Security FabricFederated upgrade is initialized with the source configured as forced-upgrade, similar to the following configuration example:config system federated-upgrade set status initialized set source forced-upgrade set upgrade-id 4 set ha-reboot-controller "FGTAWSXXXXXXXXXXXX" config known-ha-members edit "FGTAWSXXXXXXXXXXXX" next edit "FGTAWSXXXXXXXXXXXX" next end endAttempting to modify the federated-upgrade status directly results in the following error:Federated upgrade cannot be configured directly. Please use 'execute federated-upgrade ...' to configure. object set operator error, -39 discard the setting Command fail. Return code -39Additionally, executing the recommended cancellation command fails with the following error:The existing upgrades cannot be cancelled. Command fail. Return code 1Root cause:Starting with FortiOS 7.4.8, 7.6.4, and 8.0.0, a new behavior has been introduced on unlicensed or expired-support FortiGate devices. If support is not valid, the FortiGate will automatically schedule a firmware upgrade to the latest patch in its current minor version. This is managed through the CLI under 'config system federated-upgrade', where the upgrade schedule becomes visible. However, this scheduled upgrade cannot be cancelled, only postponed for up to seven days using the command 'execute auto-upgrade delay-installation'.Resolution:As a workaround, changing the central-management type on FortiGate to FortiManager and subsequently reverting it to none successfully terminates the existing federated-upgrade process on FortiGate.Change the central-management type to FortiManager on FortiGate:config system central-management set type fortimanager endThis immediately terminates the existing federated-upgrade process/schedule on FortiGate.Revert the central-management type to the default setting on FortiGate:config system central-management set type none endVerify the federated-upgrade status:show system federated-upgradeAfter applying the workaround, the following outputs will be observed:config system federated-upgrade set status disabled endThe scheduled federated-upgrade will be disabled and the previously seen upgrade configuration will no longer be visible.

topics.title: HA out-of-sync on firewall service objects with different UUIDs after upgrading from FortiOS 7.2 to 7.4
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to identify and fix an HA out-of-sync condition caused by different UUIDs on firewall service objects between cluster members after upgrading from FortiOS 7.2 to 7.4.ScopeFortiOS, FortiGate, FGCP HA.SolutionRecognize the symptom.After the upgrade, both units boot and the cluster passes traffic normally, but the secondary unit remains out-of-sync. The heartbeat interfaces are up and show no errors.This behavior was observed on a two-member FortiGate 101F active-passive cluster without VDOMs, upgraded from FortiOS 7.2.14 to 7.4.13 following the recommended upgrade path.The following do not resolve the condition:diagnose sys ha checksum recalculate. execute ha synchronize startRebooting only the secondary unit.The HA synchronization debug (hasync and hatalk) shows no configuration synchronization error that explains the mismatch.Locate the mismatched tables.Compare the checksums of the cluster members:diagnose sys ha checksum clusterIn this scenario, the global checksum matches and the root checksum differs. Run the following command on each member to find the affected tables:diagnose sys ha checksum show rootThe mismatched tables are "firewall.service.custom" and "firewall.service.group". To access the secondary unit from the primary unit, use, for example, "execute ha manage 1 admin", adjusting the member index and the administrator name.Compare the checksums object by object.Run the command on both members, and repeat it for "firewall.service.group:"FGT-A # diagnose sys ha checksum show root firewall.service.custom ALL: 3f9a0c51e2b74d6aa81c0f5e7d2b9e14 HTTP: 8c21d4e7a90b3f6c5e1d72a04b8f9c33 HTTPS: 1b7e5a2c9d0f48e3a6c2b1f7e0d95a48 ... TCP_8080: 6d0c3b9a2e7f41d58a9c0e3b7f1a2d65 FGT-B # diagnose sys ha checksum show root firewall.service.custom ALL: a74e19c2f05b3d8e6c1a9f20b7d4e391 HTTP: 05d8f3a1c6e29b7d4f0a3e8c1b6d2f97 HTTPS: e2c94b7a1d05f83c6a9e2d0b4f7c1a52 ... TCP_8080: 9b3f6e0d2a8c47f1b5e3d9a0c7f2e148All service objects and all service groups have different checksums between the members, including both the default objects and the ones created by the administrator.Confirm that the UUID is the only difference.Collect the configuration from both members:show full-configuration firewall service custom show full-configuration firewall service groupRemove the "set uuid" lines and compare the two outputs with a text comparison tool. In this scenario, there is no other difference.Example, where FGT-A is the primary unit and FGT-B is the secondary unit (output shortened):FGT-A # show full-configuration firewall service custom config firewall service custom edit "HTTP" set uuid d7504c80-f1f9-51f0-52e6-269ef2a74de4 set proxy disable set category "Web Access" set protocol TCP/UDP/SCTP set helper auto set tcp-portrange 80 ... next ... end FGT-B # show full-configuration firewall service custom config firewall service custom edit "HTTP" set uuid 47aa9e00-f1f9-51f0-6513-0c5ca6a3a450 set proxy disable set category "Web Access" set protocol TCP/UDP/SCTP set helper auto set tcp-portrange 80 ... next ... endIf anything other than the UUID differs, correct that difference first. The procedure below does not apply to it.Understand why the UUIDs differ.The "uuid" setting of "config firewall service custom" and "config firewall service group" is not listed in the CLI Reference of FortiOS 7.2.0, 7.4.0, or 7.4.1. It is listed starting from FortiOS 7.4.2, where the value is assigned automatically.In the affected cluster, the UUIDs of each unit carried a timestamp matching that unit's own reboot during the upgrade, about four minutes apart, including objects created long before the upgrade. This indicates that each member generated its own values while converting the configuration, and the HA synchronization did not reconcile them afterwards.6. Allow manual UUID setting on the secondary unit.The fix is based on the article Technical Tip: Manually setting the UUID of an object, listed at the end. That article suggests trying an HA failover or a sequential reboot first. In this scenario, rebooting only the secondary unit did not change the checksums.The changes below are made on the secondary unit, and the primary unit keeps processing traffic. Access the secondary unit and run:diagnose sys uuid allow-manual-set enableNote: Starting from FortiOS 8.0.1, manual UUID setting can no longer be enabled, so this procedure does not apply. Open a ticket with Fortinet TAC in that case. On a unit with VDOMs, the command must be run in each VDOM that has mismatched UUIDs.Copy the UUIDs of the primary unit to the secondary unit.Obtain the values on the primary unit:show firewall service custom show firewall service groupOn the secondary unit, set the UUID of the primary unit on each mismatched object. Example with two services and one service group:config firewall service custom edit "HTTP" set uuid d7504c80-f1f9-51f0-52e6-269ef2a74de4 next edit "TCP_8080" set uuid d7e8e300-f1f9-51f0-128b-892fd23f0824 next end config firewall servic

topics.title: IPSec over IPSec between two FortiGates
topics.summary: DescriptionConfiguring IPSec over IPSec between two FortiGates when IPSec over IPSec is terminated on the same VDOM or the same device.ScopeFortiOS 7.4.x, 7.6.x, 8.0.xSolutionFortiOS does not support IPSec over IPSec terminated on the same VDOM or same device if no VDOMs are configured. When it is necessary to configure an IPSec over IPSec between two FortiGates, the only way to do it is using VDOMs where the first "underlay" IPSec will be between the frontend VDOM and the second "overlay" IPSec will be terminated on the backend VDOM.For this article, the following diagram is used :Both FortiGates are configured with two separate VDOMs.On the root_vdom, the " underlay " IPSec tunnel is configured. On backend_vdom, the " overlay " IPSec tunnel is configured.The connection between root_vdom and backend_vdom is via VDOM links.The IPSec on the backend_vdom is terminated directly on loopback.TheIPSec configuration on root_vdom / FortiGate_1: edit "main_ipsec" set interface "port1" set ike-version 2 set peertype any set net-device disable set proposal aes256-sha256 set dhgrp 20 21 set remote-gw 10.109.22.220 set psksecret * nextFirewall rule set which allows the overlay IPSec from the root_vdom to the backend_vdom on FortiGate_1; this firewall rule set is needed in both directions for IKE/ESP, NAT-T can be added as well if there is NAT.config firewall policy edit 1 set name "ipsec_over_ipsec" set uuid 66456b14-d2d7-51f1-1825-a631c7f26dee set srcintf "main_ipsec" set dstintf "vdomlink0" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "IKE" "ESP" next edit 2 set name "ipsec_over_ipsec_2" set uuid a0be0562-d2d7-51f1-57e5-a5b513172df0 set srcintf "vdomlink0" set dstintf "main_ipsec" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "IKE" "ESP" next endStatic routes for the remote overlay IPSec peer and local IPSec peer via the vdom link are needed.Output from the routing table of FortiGate_1 root_vdom:Routing table for VRF=default(0) S* 0.0.0.0/0 010/0] via 10.109.31.254, port1, 00:32:14, 11/0] C 10.109.16.0/20 is directly connected, port1, 00:32:14 C 192.168.40.0/30 is directly connected, vdomlink0, 00:32:14 S 192.168.60.0/24 /10/0] via main_ipsec tunnel 10.109.22.220, 00:32:14, 11/0] S 192.168.70.0/24 /10/0] via 192.168.40.2, vdomlink0, 00:32:14, 11/0]IPSec configuration on backend_vdom:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "overlay_ipsec" set interface "loopbac_ipsec" set ike-version 2 set peertype any set net-device disable set proposal aes256-sha256 set dhgrp 20 21 set remote-gw 192.168.60.1 set psksecret * next endBackend_vdom FW rule is needed: Loopback VDOM link in both directions and a third rule for the actual IPSec traffic, which is passing via the overlay IPSec tunnel:config firewall policy edit 1 set name "fw_rule" set uuid ce0137b2-d2da-51f1-e5c6-83ecc4948cd3 set srcintf "loopback" set dstintf "loopbac_ipsec" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "ALL" next edit 2 set name "fw_rule2" set uuid e1370d34-d2da-51f1-22cb-13f50c835929 set srcintf "loopbac_ipsec" set dstintf "vdomlink1" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "ALL" next edit 3 set name "IPSec_overlay_rule" set uuid 5979f32e-d2db-51f1-2cad-ed5ef1e0f7cc set srcintf "loopback" set dstintf "overlay_ipsec" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "ALL" next endRule No. 3 allows traffic between the loopback and remote encryption domain, as the source interface is loopback, which is local for backend_vdom. The destination interface is the IPSec overlay.Routing table FortiGate_1 backend_vdom get router info routing-t Codes: K - kernel, C - connected, S - static, R - RIP, B - BGP O - OSPF, IA - OSPF inter area N1 - OSPF NSSA external type 1, N2 - OSPF NSSA external type 2 E1 - OSPF external type 1, E2 - OSPF external type 2 i - IS-IS, L1 - IS-IS level-1, L2 - IS-IS level-2, ia - IS-IS inter area V - BGP VPNv4, E - BGP EVPN, L - Leaked, D - Directly leaked * - candidate default Routing table for VRF=default(0) C 192.168.40.0/30 is directly connected, vdomlink1, 00:43:31 S 192.168.60.0/24 /10/0] via 192.168.40.1, vdomlink1, 00:43:31, 31/0] C 192.168.70.1/32 is directly connected, loopbac_ipsec, 00:43:31 C 192.168.71.0/24 is directly connected, port2, 00:43:31 C 192.168.100.1/32 is directly connected, loopback, 00:43:31 S 192.168.100.2/32 /10/0] via overlay_ipsec tunnel 192.168.60.1, 00:43:31, 31/0]FortiGate_2 root_vdom IPSec configuration:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "main_ipsec" set interface "port1" set ike-version 2 set peertype any set net-device disable set proposal aes256-sha256 set dhgrp 20 21 set transport udp set remote-gw 10.109.23.4 set psksecret ENC xxx next endFortiGate_2 root_vdom firewall rule set and routing table:config firewall policy edit 3 set name "ipsec_over_ipsec" set uuid 814f5686-d2d7-51f1-d02e-27005

topics.summary: DescriptionWhy the FortiView sessions are not showing any results and how to view them on a 6k Chassis FortiGate.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionOn a 6K Chassis FortiGate, incoming traffic is initially received and processed by the MBD (Management Board). topics.title: Add FortiAIOps to FortiManager under Deployment Mode and troubleshoot connection issues
topics.summary: Descriptionhow to connect FortiAIOps to FortiManager using the Security Fabric connector in FortiManager deployment mode, and how to troubleshoot the case where the connector stays Disconnected, stays Pending authorization, or connects but does not sync. It is useful when onboarding FortiAIOps so that it can read the FortiManager inventory, or when the connector status does not change to Connected and Authorized.ScopeFortiManager.FortiAIOps.SolutionRequired ports from FortiAIOps to FortiManager:TCP 8013 (Fabric connector)TCP 443 (HTTPS / JSON API)Part 1: Follow the steps in this document to Enable Fabric Management in FortiManager and configure deplpyment mode on FortiAIOps.Part 2: Approve FortiAIOps on FortiManagerOn FortiManager, a notification 'FortiAiOps Connector Request' appears (bell icon), showing the FortiAIOps serial number.Go to Fabric View -> Fabric Connectors and open the FortiAiOps connector (or click the notification).The status shows 'Pending Authorization'. Review the serial number, IP address and certificate, select the ADOM scope (All ADOMs or Specify), and click Allow.Make sure the 'Connector to FortiAiOps' toggle is on.Part 3: Verify in FortiAIOpsOn FortiAIOps, Security Fabric -> Fabric Connectors should show:Troubleshooting StepsSymptom 1: Status shows Disconnected in FortiAIOps.Confirm that TCP 8013 and 443 are allowed between FortiAIOps and FortiManager, in both directions, and that FortiManager has a route back to FortiAIOps.Run a sniffer on FortiManager:diagnose sniffer packet any 'host ' 4Example of the failing case (SYN on port 8013, immediate RST from FortiManager)4.868617 10.x.x.x.58860 -> 10.x.x.x.8013: syn 1441875670 4.868663 10.x.x.x.8013 -> 10.x.x.x.58860: rst 0 ack 1441875671SYN with no reply: network or firewall problem.SYN followed by RST: FortiManager is reachable but refusing the connection. Check Part 1 (fabric access on the interface and Fabric Management enabled).Complete handshake followed by a RST after the first data packet: the daemon is rejecting the session; see step 3.Example of topics.title: Technical Tip: How to download FortiClient offline installer
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to download the FortiClient offline installer. Note: Registration of the FortiClient owner is required to proceed with this process. Scope FortiClient. Solution Download the FortiClient Offline installer using these steps: Go to Support and log in. Navigate to Support -> Firmware Download -> Firmware Images Under Select Product, select FortiClient. Select Download to obtain the offline installer. Choose the desired OS and download the offline installer. For example, if the desired Operating System is Windows, follow the steps below: Select Windows: Select the desired version (i.e., v7.00): Select the desired version (i.e., '7.4'): Select '7.4.3' (or the latest available version): Note: If FortiClient is intended only for SSL VPN/IPsec connections, select the HTTPS option on the right; otherwise, refer to the option specified in the license details. Reminder: 'Pop-ups' must be allowed in the web browser; otherwise, the download will not work. For more information, refer to: Technical Tip: Cannot download firmware image from Support Portal Related articles: Technical Tip: How to download different or old versions of FortiClient and FortiClient EMS from the Fortinet Support Site Technical Tip: How to uninstall FortiClient on macOS Technical Tip: How to uninstall unlicensed FortiClient on Windows when the shutdown FortiClient button is greyed out Technical Tip: How to silently uninstall FortiClient from command prompt remotely Technical Tip: How to download FortiClient and FCRemove.exe

topics.title: Verifying IP Ban Enforcement on FortiGate
topics.summary: Description Firewall drops for IP bans are intentionally not verbose. You can verify if traffic was dropped as a result of an IP ban using a variety of tools, including debug flow, Forward Traffic logs, and the Quarantine widget. Expected debug output before and after an IP ban is provided below. Scope FortiGate. Solution FortiGate administrators can administratively ban a source IP address to prevent traffic from that address from being forwarded through the FortiGate, see IP ban. FortiGate security profiles and FortiAnalyzer "Compromised Host" verdicts can also trigger a ban if the FortiGate is configured to do so.The Quarantine widget displays banned IP addresses and the source of the ban. For information about viewing, adding, and removing banned IP addresses, refer to Managing banned IP addresses on FortiGate.The following sections detail a controlled example to verify traffic handling before and after a client IP address is administratively banned. Verifying traffic before applying the IP banBefore applying the administrative IP ban, verify that traffic from the client is successfully forwarded through the FortiGate. The following debug flow output shows the ICMP request being allowed by firewall policy 2 and source NAT being applied. Debug flow output:id=65308 trace_id=5 func=fw_forward_handler line=1003 msg="Allowed by Policy-2: SNAT" id=65308 trace_id=5 func=__ip_session_run_tuple line=3567 msg="SNAT 192.168.1.110->10.10.2.1:5118"The Allowed by Policy-2 message confirms that the traffic matched firewall policy 2. The subsequent SNAT entry shows the source IP address translated from 192.168.1.110 to 10.10.2.1. The following firewall policy configuration shows the settings associated with policy 2:config firewall policy edit 2 set name "LABCLIENT_INTERNET_ACCESS" set uuid be160e1e-e535-51f1-de7b-9ac8479d9456 set srcintf "internal" set dstintf "wan1" set action accept set srcaddr "LABCLIENT01" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "ALL" set utm-status disable set logtraffic all set nat enable next endFor steps to apply a debug flow trace, see Using the debug flow tool. Forward Traffic log before applying the IP ban:date=2026-11-20 time=15:38:45 eventtime=1795217924737549697 tz="-0800" logid="0000000013" type="traffic" subtype="forward" level="notice" vd="root" srcip=192.168.1.110 identifier=1 srcintf="internal" srcintfrole="lan" dstip=8.8.8.8 dstintf="wan1" dstintfrole="wan" srccountry="Reserved" dstcountry="United States" sessionid=14659991 proto=1 action="accept" policyid=2 policytype="policy" poluuid="be160e1e-e535-51f1-de7b-9ac8479d9456" policyname="LABCLIENT_INTERNET_ACCESS" service="PING" trandisp="snat" transip=10.10.2.1 appcat="unscanned" duration=63 sentbyte=240 rcvdbyte=240 sentpkt=4 rcvdpkt=4The action="accept" field indicates that the traffic was accepted. The packet and byte counters confirm that traffic was successfully transmitted and received through the firewall policy.The built-in packet sniffer confirms that the client's ICMP echo request was forwarded from the internal interface to the outgoing interface. The corresponding echo reply was received on the outgoing interface and forwarded back to the client. Packet sniffer output before applying the IP ban:2026-11-20 15:37:44.677916 internal in 192.168.1.110 -> 8.8.8.8: icmp: echo request 2026-11-20 15:37:44.677978 wan1 out 10.10.2.1 -> 8.8.8.8: icmp: echo request 2026-11-20 15:37:44.681711 wan1 in 8.8.8.8 -> 10.10.2.1: icmp: echo reply 2026-11-20 15:37:44.681756 internal out 8.8.8.8 -> 192.168.1.110: icmp: echo reply Verify the administrative IP banAfter the administrative IP ban was applied, the FortiGate was checked to confirm that the client's source IP address was added to the banned IP list.Banned IP list:NETSCOPEXCORE # diagnose user banned-ip list src-ip-addr created expires cause 192.168.1.110 Fri Nov 20 15:40:39 2026 Fri Nov 20 16:10:39 2026 AdministrativeThe output confirms that 192.168.1.110 was added to the banned IP list with the cause shown as Administrative. The entry also displays its creation and expiration times. The Quarantine widget provides a GUI view of the banned IP entry. It displays the source IP address, ban source, and expiration time. Quarantine widget: The widget confirms that 192.168.1.110 appears as a banned IP address with the source identified as Administrative. Its expiration time matches the entry displayed in the CLI output. Verify traffic after applying the IP banAfter confirming that the client's source IP address was administratively banned, ICMP traffic was generated again from the client. topics.title: VPN Report generated by FortiManagement Cloud Portal shows "n/a" as the username for IKEv1 IPsec Dialup VPN
topics.summary: DescriptionThe VPN Report in FortiManagement Cloud version 26.4.0 (formerly FortiGate Cloud) shows "n/a" as the Username for IPsec dial-up users when the eapuser field is missing or n/a.ScopeFortiManagement Cloud 26.4.0SolutionFortiManagement Cloud 26.4.0 was released in early November. Portals that have upgraded automatically to this version will have reduced information displayed in VPN Report if users are connecting to IKEv1 Dialup IPsec VPNs.This is because IKE version 1 Dialup users use XAUTH instead of EAP for user authentication, and the "eapuser" and "eapauthgroup" do not appear in VPN event logs related to these users.Sample FortiOS VPN event log for an affected user:devname=XXX device_id=XXX date=2026-11-25 time=09:20:10 eventtime=1795620009953153529 tz="-0600" logid="0101037139" type="event" subtype="vpn" level="notice" vd="root" logdesc="IPsec phase 2 status changed" msg="IPsec phase 2 status change" action="phase2-down" remip=XXX locip=XXX remport=4500 locport=4500 outintf="wan1" srccountry="United States" cookies="XXXX/YYYY" user="192.168.0.200" group="N/A" useralt="N/A" xauthuser="USER1" xauthgroup="GROUP1" assignip=X.X.X.X vpntunnel="XXX" phase2_name="XXX" fctuid="XXX" advpnsc=0Example affected report shows N/A for each user entry:This is an issue on the FortiManagement Cloud side affecting reporting; it has no effect on FortiGate VPN functionality or access control.The issue has been reported, and an identified fix is scheduled for inclusion in FortiManagement Cloud version 26.4.a, currently expected for release in early December. After this fix, the User column in future VPN Reports should show correct names for both IKEv1 and IKEv2 Dialup IPsec gateways.The current FortiManagement Cloud version is displayed in the bottom left of the adminstrator portal, see Technical Tip: How to check the current FortiManagement Cloud version.

topics.title: Android FortiToken Mobile app shows error 'Server identity does not match' after upgrade to version 6.7.1.0046
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading the Android FortiToken Mobile app to version 6.7.1.0046, accepting push notifications fails with the error 'Server identity does not match'.ScopeAndroid FortiToken Mobile app version 6.7.1.0046 and above.SolutionAndroid FortiToken Mobile app version 6.7.1.0046 and higher enforce certificate pinning for push notifications. In particular, when FortiGate or FortiAuthenticator sends a push notification, this includes information on their server certificates (the default HTTPS server certificate).When the FortiToken app connects to FortiGate or FortiAuthenticator, it expects to receive the certificate that FortiGate or FortiAuthenticator indicates in the push notification. If a different certificate is presented instead (due to a reverse proxy, load balancer, or firewall in front of the FortiGate/FortiAuthenticator), this will trigger the error 'Server Identity does not match'.The error may occur even if the SAN of the proxy certificate and the FortiGate/FortiAuthenticator certificate are identical, as the validation happens via certificate fingerprints rather than SAN.There are two possible workarounds at present:Enter the token code manually.Without push notification, the FortiGate/FortiAuthenticator certificate does not have an impact, and the error will not occur. This may require disabling push notifications manually.Ensure FortiGate/FortiAuthenticator uses the exact same certificate as the device in front of it.If the proxy/gateway/load-balancer/etc. uses an identical certificate to the FortiGate/FortiAuthenticator server certificate, then the fingerprint in the push notification will match the fingerprint observed by the app when connecting for the reply.Related documentation:Troubleshooting certificate errors in FortiToken Mobile version 6.7.1 and aboveResolved Issues

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: WTPIMG files filling /tmp on FortiGate managed by FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to identify and resolve high memory usage on a FortiGate caused by FortiSwitch firmware images that accumulate in /tmp when FortiManager repeatedly pushes a FortiSwitch upgrade task that fails.ScopeFortiGate managing FortiSwitch units, managed by FortiManager with the 'Enforce Firmware Version' option enabled for the FortiSwitches in FortiSwitch Manager.SolutionSymptoms:FortiGate memory usage increases slowly and steadily, which can eventually lead to conserve mode.Process memory ('diagnose sys top-mem') stays stable and accounts for only a small part of the used memory.Shmem in 'diagnose hardware sysinfo memory' and the /tmp usage in 'fnsysctl df -h' increase together.Identification:/tmp is a tmpfs (RAM-backed) file system, so files stored in /tmp use FortiGate memory:fnsysctl cat /proc/mountsnone /tmp tmpfs rw,nosuid,noexec,relatime,size=20477164k 0 0.Files in tmpfs are kept in memory and are counted as Shmem in /proc/meminfo (Tmpfs)./tmp usage and Shmem:fnsysctl df -hFilesystem size used available Use% Mounted on none 19.5G 7.7G 11.7G 40% /tmpdiagnose hardware sysinfo memoryShmem: 8359276 kB.fnsysctl ls -al /tmpOutput:-rw-r--r-- 1 0 0 Sat Oct 17 16:14:25 2026 44274376 WTPIMGe5afIm -rw-r--r-- 1 0 0 Sat Oct 17 22:24:12 2026 44274376 WTPIMGsGXaDJ -rw-r--r-- 1 0 0 Sun Oct 18 04:24:56 2026 44274376 WTPIMGLjuCNE -rw-r--r-- 1 0 0 Sun Oct 18 10:25:10 2026 44274376 WTPIMGRvCXZH .../tmp contains many files of the same size named WTPIMG*:In the observed case, a new file of the same size (one FortiSwitch image) was written every 6 hours, and none were removed. After 38 days of uptime, 170 files were using about 7.2 GB in /tmp.On FortiManager, a FortiSwitch upgrade task for the FortiGate keeps reappearing and failing at the same interval.Root cause:With 'Enforce Firmware Version' enabled for the FortiSwitches in FortiSwitch Manager, FortiManager repeatedly triggers the FortiSwitch firmware upgrade task. Each attempt stores the FortiSwitch image in /tmp on the FortiGate, and the image is not removed when the task fails.Clearing the FortiManager firmware upgrade database (diagnose fwmanager profile clear) or resetting the DVM tasks (diagnose dvm task reset) does not stop the tasks while this option is enabled.Solution:'Enforce Firmware Version' is deselected for the affected FortiSwitches in FortiSwitch Manager on FortiManager.After this change, the repeating FortiSwitch upgrade task no longer runs.A FortiGate reboot clears /tmp, since tmpfs content is not kept across reboots.After the reboot, 'fnsysctl ls -al /tmp' and 'fnsysctl df -h' show no new WTPIMG* files and no further /tmp growth.Workaround:If the FortiManager configuration cannot be changed immediately, temporarily blocking communication between the FortiGate and FortiManager stops the repeating upgrade tasks.

Has anyone tested FortiGate-VM on ESXi 9.1 in a lab environment? topics.title: Unable to bypass critical vulnerability alert in FortiGate GUI
topics.summary: DescriptionA critical vulnerability warning screen in FortiOS 7.6.7 prevents users from accessing the FortiGate GUI. When clicking the Skip button, the action is not processed correctly, and instead of proceeding with the login, the user is logged out.ScopeFortiGateSolutionWhen accessing the FortiGate GUI on FortiOS 7.6.7, an alert screen appears displaying the message "Installed Firmware Contains a Critical Vulnerability."The screen provides the option "Skip upgrade & I understand the risk" to allow users to proceed with the login without upgrading the firmware.However, clicking this button does not proceed with the login as expected. Although the warning message instructs users to acknowledge and accept the risk with the following statement, "To continue logging in without upgrading, please acknowledge and be willing to accept the risk of doing so.", the acknowledgement is not properly processed, and the user is redirected back to the login screen instead of gaining access to the FortiGate GUI.The prompt blocks the GUI session in the following browsers where the defect appears , no login setting bypasses it.Tested across multiple browser sessions, and the button is unresponsive in all three:Google Chrome (standard mode)Google Chrome (Incognito mode)Microsoft EdgeCLI access via SSH is still working normally.Workaround:Log in from Firefox. The acknowledgement is processed and the session reaches dashboard.

topics.title: FortiZTP provisioning of FortiGate-VM to FortiManager fails with S-Series and FortiFlex Flex-VM licenses because auto-join-forticloud is disabled
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiZTP depends on the auto-join feature, which requires auto-join-forticloud to be enabled and config system central-management set to type fortiguard for provisioning to function.On FortiOS installations using a FortiGate-VMUL-S (S-Series Subscription) license, and on Flex-VM licenses.ScopeFortigate.FortiZTP provisioning target: on-premises FortiManager.FortiGate-VM license families: FortiGate-VMUL-S (S-Series Subscription), FortiFlex Flex-VM.Hypervisor: VMware Workstation. Deployment: fresh installation, factory default configuration.SolutionBackgroundFortiZTP requires a FortiGate model or license that supports the zero-touch provisioning (autojoin) feature, and FortiOS 5.2.2 or later. A valid certificate with the serial number as CN, signed by Fortinet, is also required for FortiZTP to function.For non-zero-touch models, FortiZTP supports one-touch provisioning, and DHCP must be configured on the chosen port.A FG-VM01 or FG-VM01V license is recommended for FortiGate-VM deployments because the autojoin feature is enabled by default on those licenses.SymptomsOn a FortiOS installation with a FortiGate-VMUL-S license, the following defaults are present:config system fortiguard show auto-join-forticloud endconfig system central-management show endThe output shows auto-join-forticloud disabled and type set to none. The none option means no central management. With those two defaults, the device does not send traffic to FortiGate Cloud, so FortiZTP provisioning to FortiManager cannot proceed.Resolution 1: enable autojoin manually before provisioningRun the following so that the FortiGate-VM can reach FortiGate Cloud, then restart the device and confirm that it is sending traffic to FortiGate CloudEnable auto-join for FortiZTP:Enable auto-join-forticloud:config system fortiguard set auto-join-forticloud enable endSet the central management type:config system central-management set type fortiguard endUnset the FortiGuard location (non-U.S. government FortiGate-VM only):config system fortiguard unset update-server-location endRestart and verifyRestart the device and confirm that the device is sending traffic to FortiGate Cloud, which is the documented verification step after changing these settings s4]. Then provision the device in the FortiZTP portal.Resolution 2: Use DHCP options 240/241 when the device has no internet accessFor FortiGates that cannot reach FortiCloud or the FortiDeploy servers, zero-touch provisioning can be done with a local DHCP server advertising the FortiManager location: option 240 (IP address of FortiManager) and option 241 (FQDN of FortiManager). This method only works when the FortiGate boots after a factory reset, because it is intended for a zero-configuration, out-of-the-box deployment. A factory-fresh FortiGate uses DHCP on the first interface and requests these options automatically. It is generally suggested to use one option or the other, because the FortiGate adds an entry under config system central-management for each option received. To prevent spoofing, the FortiGate no longer accepts a different FortiManager IP/FQDN received from DHCP after the initial FortiZTP setupExample FortiGate DHCP server configuration:config system dhcp server edit 1 set dns-service default set default-gateway 172.16.200.254 set netmask 255.255.255.0 set interface "internal" config ip-range edit 1 set start-ip 172.16.200.201 set end-ip 172.16.200.209 next end config options edit 1 set code 240 set type ip set ip 172.18.60.115 next edit 2 set code 241 set type string set value "fortimanager.example.com" next end next endIn this configuration, option 240 carries the FortiManager IP address and option 241 carries the FortiManager FQDN, which is transmitted as hexadecimal in the DHCP packet.Related noteFortiGate Cloud was renamed to FortiManagement Cloud starting September 8, 2026, which is worth reflecting in the wording and links of the article.Related articles:FortiZTP RequirementsHow to disable management tunnel to FortiGate CloudHow to perform zero touch provisioning with FortiManager and DHCP Option 240/241FortiZTP 26.1.a Administration GuideProvisioning FortiGate to FortiManager Cloud self-diagnosisFortiZTP provisioning errors due to wrong region - 'Incomplete - Waiting for connection'How to check whether a FortiGate has a paid FortiGate Cloud Service SubscriptionFortiZTP 25.4 Administration GuideCommunity Tip: Knowledge Article publishing rules and guidelines

topics.title: Configure an API user to update SSL inspection certificates on FortiGate
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to configure a restricted API user with specific permissions to update the CA certificate used in SSL inspection profiles.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionTo create an API user capable of updating the CA certificate in an SSL inspection profile, follow these steps.Create a custom deep inspection profileClone the default deep-inspection profile to a custom profile to allow modifications via the API.Configure the access profileCreate an access profile that grants read-write permissions to the firewall settings required for certificate updates while disabling other administrative capabilities.config system accprofile edit "ssl-cert-api-prof" set comments "API" set secfabgrp none set ftviewgrp none set authgrp none set sysgrp none set netgrp none set loggrp none set fwgrp custom set vpngrp none set utmgrp none set wanoptgrp none set wifi none set admintimeout-override disable set cli-diagnose disable set cli-get disable set cli-show disable set cli-exec disable set cli-config disable set system-execute-ssh enable set system-execute-telnet enable config fwgrp-permission set policy none set address none set service none set schedule none set others read-write end next endCreate the API userAssign the previously created access profile to a new API user.config system api-user edit ssl-cert-api set comments "REST API user for updating ssl-ssh-profile caname" set accprofile ssl-cert-api-prof next endRun the following command to generate the secret key for the API user. Refer to CLI Reference for more details.execute api-user generate-key ssl-cert-apiValidate the configurationUse a tool such as cURL to verify that the API user can retrieve and update the CA certificate name in the SSL inspection profile.To retrieve the current profile configuration:curl -k -H "Authorization: Bearer " "https:// /api/v2/cmdb/firewall/ssl-ssh-profile/api-deep-inspection"To update the CA certificate name:curl -k -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer " -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{"caname":"Custom_CA_SSL"}" "https:// /api/v2/cmdb/firewall/ssl-ssh-profile/api-deep-inspection"

topics.title: IP phone reboot loop after DHCP option 132 is configured for voice-VLAN assignment on FortiSwitch.
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to troubleshoot IP phones that successfully obtain a Voice VLAN IP address through DHCP Option 132 but then reboot and fall back to the native (Data) VLAN, resulting in a continuous boot loop.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.x, FortiSwitch managed mode, DHCP option 132 / LLDP-MED voice VLAN.SolutionWhen users connect their laptops to their IP phone by connecting to the passthrough port, the intent is to use the Data VLAN for data, and DHCP Option 132 is used to allow voice traffic to match the voice VLAN.The issue is that after connecting to the IP phone, if the phone receives a configuration update from the phone server, the phone will reboot and potentially lose its Voice VLAN assignment, fall back to the native (Data) VLAN, and enter a continuous reboot loop.The following will need to be confirmed from the FortiGate:Confirm that DHCP option 132 is configured on the native/Data VLAN interface using the below CLI commands:config system dhcp server show fullSample output below:config system dhcp server edit 1 set dns-service default set default-gateway 192.168.10.1 set netmask 255.255.255.0 set interface "internal" config ip-range edit 1 set start-ip 192.168.10.100 set end-ip 192.168.10.200 next end config options edit 1 set code 132 set type string set value "20" next end next end Note: DHCP option 132 should be configured on the native/Data VLAN interface and not the voice VLAN interface itself.Confirm the FortiSwitch port configurations (native + allowed VLANs) using the below CLI command:show switch-controller managed-switch Sample output is below (Note that "vlan", "allowed-vlans", and "untagged-vlans" should be verified.FGT-Core # show switch-controller managed-switch S248Exxxxxxxxxx config switch-controller managed-switch edit "S248Exxxxxxxxxx" set name "FSW-xxxx" set fsw-wan1-peer "fortilink" set fsw-wan1-admin enable set poe-detection-type 1 set version 1 set max-allowed-trunk-members 8 set dynamic-capability 15 config ports edit "port1" set vlan "VLAN_10_Users" set allowed-vlans set untagged-vlans set export-to "root" set mac-addr xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx next edit "port2" set vlan "VLAN_20_Voice" set allowed-vlans set untagged-vlans set lldp-profile "default-auto-isl" set export-to "root" set mac-addr xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx next edit "port23" set poe-capable 0 set vlan "default" set allowed-vlans set untagged-vlans set lldp-profile "default-auto-isl" set export-to "root" set mac-addr xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx next edit "port24" set poe-capable 0 set vlan "default" set allowed-vlans set untagged-vlans set lldp-profile "default-auto-isl" set export-to "root" set mac-addr xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx next edit "internal" set type internal set allowed-vlans set export-to "root" set mac-addr xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx next end next end Confirm FortiLink health and look for any NTP or VLAN warnings using the below command:diagnose switch-controller diagnose-connection Sample output below:FortiGate-100F # execute switch-controller diagnose-connection S248Exxxxxxxxxxx ================================================================== FortiLink interface diagnosis: ================================================================== FortiLink interface : fortilink DHCP server : Enabled (10.255.1.1 - 10.255.1.254) NTP server : Enabled (Listening on fortilink) HA mode : Standalone CAPWAP : Enabled on fortilink ================================================================== FortiSwitch (S248Exxxxxxxxxxx) diagnosis: ================================================================== Switch Status : Authorized / Up Management IP : 10.255.1.2 CAPWAP Tunnel : Up (10.255.1.1:5246 10.255.1.2:49152) Ping Reachability : Success (0% packet loss, avg 0.45 ms) NTP Sync Status : Synchronized (Stratum 3) Image Version : S248EP-v7.4.3-build0820,240415 (Compatible) REST API Status : Connected (HTTP 200) ================================================================== Result: No connection issues detected. Capture the DHCP traffic to verify option 132 in present in the DHCP Offer/ACK packets using the following CLI sniffer command:diagnose sniffer packet any 'port(67 or 68)' 6 0 lAfter converting the sniffer output to Wireshark-readable format, open the pcap file and look for DHCP option 132 in the DHCP Offer/ACK packets as outlined below:Resolution:After confirming that DHCP Option 132 is present in the packet capture, if the IP phone continues to reboot and lose its Voice VLAN assignment, contact the phone vendor to configure the Voice VLAN ID in the provisioning package.This ensures the Voice VLAN setting persists across reboots and configuration updates received from the phone server, preventing the phone from reverting to the native (Data) VLAN.

topics.title: Understanding Backslash Escape Characters in Syslog Alert Notifications
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen FortiAnalyzer sends an Event Handler alert notification to a syslog server, the message contains several key-value pairs describing the alert, followed by the original log that triggered the event.The original log is embedded in its entirety within the log= field as a single quoted string.Since the original log already contains double quotes ("), these characters must be escaped using a backslash (\) to distinguish them from the quotes defining the boundaries of the log= value.Users may also notice escaped forward slashes ("\/") in certain values, particularly when the content contains JSON-derived data.This article explains how the alert notification message is structured and why these escape characters are expected.Explanation of Syslog Alert Notification FormatHow an alert notification message is structuredWhen an Event Handler triggers an alert, FortiAnalyzer sends a syslog notification containing the alert information and the original log that triggered the event.The notification consists of:Alert information: Includes fields such as subject, device, severity, trigger, tag, and alertid.Original log (log=): Contains the complete log entry associated with the triggered event.For example:Jun 28 10:38:56 eFAZ FAZ-Alerting subject="desc:User login from SSH failed" device="eFAZ" severity="medium" from="eFAZ(FAZ-VMTM00000000)" trigger="Local Device Event" tag="Default,System,Local" alertid=202406181000000000 log="tz=\"-0700\" log_id=\"0001010014\" type=\"event\" subtype=\"system\" pri=\"alert\" desc=\"User login from SSH failed\" user=\"admin\" msg=\"Login from ssh: Failed for admin from 10.10.10.2 port xxx\" remote_ip=\"10.10.10.2\" remote_port=xxx operation=\"login failed\" performed_on=\"ssh(10.10.10.2)\" changes=\"'admin' login failed from ssh(10.10.10.2)\" valid=1 authmsg=\"Failed\" extrainfo=\"\" devid=\"FAZ-VMTM00000000\" itime=1718728xxx date=\"2026-06-28\" time=\"11:11:10\""The example illustrates that the original log is embedded inside the log= field rather than being sent as a separate syslog message.Why backslashes appear in the log fieldThe backslash \ is an escape character. It tells the parser that the following double quote is part of the actual log content and should not be interpreted as the closing boundary of the log= value.Related article:Creating notification profiles

topics.title: Verifying WPA3 SAE Transitional mode
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to verify that a Fortinet wireless network correctly advertises WPA3-SAE Transition Mode (WPA2/WPA3-Personal), enabling clients to connect using either WPA2-PSK or WPA3-SAE authentication.ScopeFortiAP.SolutionObjectiveThe objective is to verify that the FortiAP SSID advertises both WPA2-PSK and WPA3-SAE authentication methods.Specifically, verify that the RSN Information Element (RSN IE) in the wireless beacon frame contains both expected AKM (Authentication and Key Management) suites:00:0f2 (PSK) – WPA2-PSK00:0f:ac:8 (SAE) – WPA3-SAE (SHA256)Configure the FortiAP packet snifferConfigure a FortiAP radio to operate in sniffer mode using the following CLI configuration:config wireless-controller wtp-profile edit "FAP-SNIFFER" config radio-1 set mode sniffer set ap-sniffer-bufsize 32 set ap-sniffer-chan 36 set ap-sniffer-addr xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx set ap-sniffer-mgmt-beacon enable set ap-sniffer-mgmt-probe enable set ap-sniffer-mgmt-other enable set ap-sniffer-ctl enable set ap-sniffer-data enable end next endReplace xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx with the MAC address of the target client device.Note: Ensure that the configured sniffer channel matches the channel used by the target SSID.Transfer the capture file to a TFTP serverUse the appropriate command for your FortiAP model.FAP-U:tftp -l /tmp/wl_sniff.cap -r wl_sniff_remote.cap -p 192.168.50.100Standard FAP W1:ftftp -l /tmp/wl_sniff.cap -r wl_sniff_remote.cap -p 192.168.50.100Standard FAP W2:ftftp 192.168.50.100 -m binary -c put /tmp/wl_sniff.cap wl_sniff_remote.capReplace 192.168.50.100 with the IP address of your TFTP server.The capture file is stored temporarily on the FortiAP.Important: Download the capture file before rebooting the FortiAP.Inspect the capture in WiresharkOpen the downloaded .cap or .pcap file in Wireshark.Apply the following display filter to identify frames advertising the SAE AKM suite:wlan.rsn.akms.type == 8Locate a beacon frame belonging to the target SSID and expand the following fields:IEEE 802.11 Wireless ManagementTagged parametersTag: RSN InformationInspect the Auth Key Management (AKM) Suite Count and Auth Key Management (AKM) List fields.Expected resultsThe RSN Information Element should contain the following:Auth Key Management (AKM) Suite Count: 2Auth Key Management (AKM) List:OUIAKM typeAuthentication00:0f:ac2PSK (WPA2-PSK)00:0f:ac8SAE (SHA256) (WPA3-SAE)Example Wireshark output:Tag: RSN Information Auth Key Management (AKM) Suite Count: 2 Auth Key Management (AKM) List: 00:0f:ac (IEEE 802.11) PSK 00:0f:ac (IEEE 802.11) SAE (SHA256)Verification criteriaThe verification is successful when:The target SSID is identified in the captured beacon frame.The RSN Information Element contains an AKM Suite Count of 2.The AKM list contains both PSK (00:0f:ac:2) and SAE (00:0f:ac:8).This confirms that the SSID advertises both WPA2-PSK and WPA3-SAE authentication methods in the same RSN Information Element.

topics.title: Configure Fortinet Single Sign On (FSSO) for an IPsec IKEv2 users via syslog message
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to configure FSSO logon event from syslog message of FortiGate for IPsec IKEv2.ScopeFortiOS: all available branches.SolutionFSSO rules can be used for the traffic generated by remote IPsec VPN users. There is already an article describing how to configure the same for IKEv1 and SSL.VPN; meanwhile, this article describes how to achieve it for IPsec IKEv2.Technical Tip: How to configure Fortinet Single Sign-On (FSSO) for IPsec IKEv1 dial-up VPN clients using SyslogTechnical Tip: Configure Fortinet Single Sign On (FSSO) for SSL-VPN users via SyslogThe configuration part of FSSO-based authentication is skipped intentionally. These steps should be performed: IPsec logon event is generated on FortiOS.FortiOS sends a syslog message to the FSSO CA.FSSO CA processes the syslog message accordingly and sends an FSSO-based logon event to the configured firewalls.This document starts from point #3 - configuring FSSO CA to process syslog logon events:Go to FSSO CA -> Advanced Features -> Syslog Source List, click on "Enable this feature", then specify the port as desired. By default, it is 514.2. On the same page, "Syslog Source List," click "Manage LDAP Server" and configure LDAP server settings: Configure a syslog rule by clicking Syslog Source List -> Manage Rule -> Add (Logon, logoff events were taken from this source - Understanding VPN related logs):Note: The field "Client IPv4 Field" has a space at the end of the value: "assignip={{:client_ip}}"; it is required since the value is not in quotes in the syslog message.Configure the mapping between the syslog rule and the LDAP server. It is required to process logon events and verify the connected LDAP user account. Go to Syslog Source List -> Click the Add button:The "Remote User" value "DC" is the one that was created above in step #2:After configuring the settings on FSSO CA, IPsec IKEv2 settings could be configured:1. Phase1-interface settings:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "FGT-dialup" set type dynamic set interface "port4" set ike-version 2 set peertype any set net-device disable set mode-cfg enable set proposal 3des-sha256 set comments "VPN: FGT-dialup (Created by VPN wizard)" set dhgrp 14 set eap enable set eap-identity send-request set nattraversal enable set transport udp set ipv4-start-ip 172.11.10.10 set ipv4-end-ip 172.11.10.20 set ipv4-netmask 255.255.255.0 set dns-mode auto set save-password enable set client-auto-negotiate enable set client-keep-alive enable set psksecret ENC VAEgEZz5+0dQSQPKhZ7M3KBooXYrlMfZQq9CLMwlgu3KIi9XZjuopdoyQsvEg8L70fg+Rtk/BXZ76YjxXwEZCpMC+/gFrO0qmeIWqNGBBeES+5JF5dw/xX6a9B1glqlkeLPOWoTWfsvtXan0RZz4Ap4hXYQEGA0YTqcqsy2Wlgl96JZIEQtC+ifkmgkKtvhAqLWLBllmMjY3dkVA next endPhase2-interface settings:config vpn ipsec phase2-interface edit "FGT-dialup" set phase1name "FGT-dialup" set proposal aes128-sha256 aes256-sha256 set dhgrp 14 set keepalive enable set comments "VPN: FGT-dialup (Created by VPN wizard)" next endSyslog settings; kindly mention that these syslog settings were configured on multi-vdom mode-enabled FortiOS:fgt01-hub(Primary) (root) # show log syslogd override-setting config log syslogd override-setting set status enable set server "172.20.20.3" end fgt01-hub(Primary) (root) # show log syslogd override-filter config log syslogd override-filter set forward-traffic disable set local-traffic disable set multicast-traffic disable set sniffer-traffic disable set ztna-traffic disable set anomaly disable set voip disable config free-style edit 1 set category event set filter "((logid 0101037138) or (logid 0101037139) or (logid 0101037141))" next end endFirewall policies:For testing purposes, there are two firewall policies: First one (ID 39 ) for IPsec using local firewall group for IPsec authentication only.The second one (ID 1) uses the FSSO user group: Firewall authentication list:fgt01-hub(Primary) (root) # diagnose firewall auth list 172.11.10.10, ADUSER01 type: fsso, id: 0, duration: 5439, idled: 352 <<< FSSO server: brave.you-FSSO packets: in 56 out 656, bytes: in 3360 out 45039 group_id: 33556451 33556429 group_name: CN=DOMAIN USERS,CN=USERS,DC=BRAVE,DC=YOU CN=GR-001,DC=BRAVE,DC=YOU 172.11.10.10, aduser01 type: fw, id: 0, duration: 519, idled: 519 server: BRAVE packets: in 0 out 0, bytes: in 0 out 0 group_id: 3 group_name: All_Domain_usersRelated articles:FSSO Agent in polling modeHow FSSO works and how to troubleshoot FSSOHow to troubleshoot intermittent IPsec dial-up VPN disconnection

topics.title: Duplicate ADVPN shortcut tunnels established between spokes
topics.summary: DescriptionAuto Discovery VPN (ADVPN) 2.0 may create multiple shortcut tunnels between the same spokes when multiple overlays share the same physical underlay interfaces.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptomsDuplicate ADVPN shortcut tunnels appear between the same local and remote public IP addresses under the same parent tunnel. These tunnels have different tunnel IDs and network IDs. While flushing the shortcuts temporarily removes the duplicates, they are re-established over time. Root causeThis behavior occurs in ADVPN 2.0 when multiple overlays with different network IDs share the same physical underlay interfaces. If traffic is initiated in both directions, the path management mechanism may establish an additional shortcut over the same underlay path instead of reusing the existing one. AnalysisThe presence of duplicate shortcuts does not inherently cause packet loss or connectivity interruptions. Each shortcut maintains its own valid IPsec Security Associations (SAs), and traffic is forwarded through the shortcut selected by SD-WAN. The primary impact is unnecessary resource consumption for IKE/IPsec SA management, SLA monitoring, and SD-WAN path processing.To identify which shortcut paths are being selected for each SD-WAN service, run the following command:diagnose sys sdwan advpn-session ResolutionThere is no confirmed workaround in FortiOS 7.4 to prevent duplicate shortcut creation while preserving the existing multi-hub and multi-underlay architecture. Mitigation optionsIf resource consumption becomes an issue, consider these options, though they may impact ADVPN 2.0 functionality:Disable shortcut usage under the affected SD-WAN rules. This directs traffic through the hubs instead of using direct spoke-to-spoke shortcuts.Disable ADVPN 2.0 path management on the overlay zones using set advpn-select disable. This changes the path selection mechanism and requires validation to ensure it does not break the multi-hub architecture. Permanent fixAn enhancement introducing the single-advpn-per-underlay-pair option is targeted for FortiOS 7.6.9. This option prevents redundant shortcut establishment across overlays sharing the same underlay pair.

topics.title: FortiToken Mobile backup limitations and recovery considerations in MSP environments
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiToken Mobile backup limitations, recovery considerations, and recommended practices for Managed Service Providers (MSPs) managing multiple FortiToken Mobile tokens across independent customer environments.ScopeFortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiIdentity Cloud, FortiToken Mobile.SolutionScenarioIn a Managed Service Provider (MSP) environment, an administrator may manage multiple customer environments using a single mobile device containing several FortiToken Mobile tokens.These tokens may be provisioned by different FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, or FortiIdentity Cloud instances.If the mobile device is lost, damaged, reset or replaced, the administrator may lose access to multiple customer environments simultaneously.Centralized backup and restoration limitationsFortiToken Mobile does not provide a centralized backup and restoration mechanism for all activated Fortinet-issued tokens across independent issuing platforms.Although multiple tokens can coexist within the same FortiToken Mobile application, each token remains associated with its respective issuing platform.Consequently:Tokens cannot be collectively exported and restored using a general FortiToken Mobile backup file.Recovery requirements depend on the platform that issued each token.Replacing or resetting a mobile device may require coordination with multiple customer administrators.Mobile operating system backup and restoration should not be relied upon as a supported method of recovering activated Fortinet-issued tokens.Using the same Fortinet-issued token simultaneously on multiple mobile devices is not supported.Recovery considerations based on the issuing platformIssuing platformOriginal mobile device accessibleOriginal mobile device inaccessibleFortiGateAdministrator-assisted token reassignment.Administrator-assisted token reassignment.FortiAuthenticatorMobile token transfer, if enabled and supported by the provisioning configuration.Token re-provisioning or an available recovery mechanism.FortiIdentity CloudMobile token transfer, if enabled.Recovery or reactivation through the issuing platform.In environments where tokens are issued by multiple independent FortiGate appliances, token reassignment must be performed on each respective FortiGate.There is no single FortiToken Mobile operation that initiates token recovery across all independent customer environments.Refer to the FortiToken Mobile Transfer Guide for platform-specific transfer requirements and procedures.Example deploymentConsider an MSP administrator managing the following customer environments:CustomerIssuing platformToken recovery methodCustomer AFortiGateToken reassignmentCustomer BFortiGateToken reassignmentCustomer CFortiAuthenticatorTransfer or re-provisioningCustomer DFortiIdentity CloudTransfer or reactivationIf the administrator loses access to the original mobile device, the recovery process must be coordinated with the respective issuing platforms.Recovering the token associated with Customer A does not automatically recover the tokens associated with Customers B, C or D.Alternative authentication and emergency accessDepending on the issuing platform and its configuration, alternative authentication methods may be available to reduce the risk of administrative lockout.These may include:Email-based OTP authentication.Temporary email or SMS OTP authentication on FortiAuthenticator.Emergency codes on FortiAuthenticator, where configured.Separately provisioned and authorized backup administrator accounts.These mechanisms provide alternative authentication or recovery options rather than backing up or restoring existing FortiToken Mobile tokens.Alternative authentication methods should be configured according to the customer's security policies and verified before an actual recovery scenario occurs.Recommended practices for MSP environmentsTo minimize operational disruption when a mobile device becomes unavailable:Maintain individual administrator accounts with independently assigned tokens.Avoid relying on a single administrator or mobile device as the sole access mechanism for multiple customer environments.Maintain secure emergency administrative access for each customer environment.Document the issuing platform, token assignment, responsible administrator, and recovery procedure for each customer.Verify token transfer eligibility before replacing or resetting a mobile device.Periodically validate emergency access procedures.Revoke or reset affected token activations promptly if a mobile device is lost or stolen.Do not store token activation codes, QR codes, OTP values or other authentication secrets in unsecured documentation.SummaryFortiToken Mobile allows administrators to manage multiple tokens within a single application. topics.title: ZTNA SAML authentication with Entra ID is slow to load the authentication and destination pages on macOS endpoints.
topics.summary: DescriptionUsers on macOS experience blank windows or slow loading when authenticating via SAML with Entra ID for ZTNA applications when a ZTNA rule for login.microsoftonline.com is present.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient EMS, FortiAuthenticator.SolutionWhen using Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) with SAML authentication via Microsoft Entra ID on macOS, the following issues occur:The authentication window appears blank.The login page takes an excessive amount of time to load.Users must refresh the page multiple times to enter credentials.ZTNA tunnels close abruptly shortly after opening.These symptoms do not occur on Windows endpoints.Root causeA conflict occurs when a ZTNA rule is created for login.microsoftonline.com while simultaneously using SAML authentication with Entra ID.On macOS, FortiClient traffic is not excluded from ZTNA interception as it is on Windows. When a ZTNA rule matches login.microsoftonline.com, the FortiGate expects the user to be authenticated before forwarding the traffic. However, the user cannot authenticate because the traffic required to reach the SAML login page is intercepted and blocked by the ZTNA rule. This creates a circular dependency where authentication cannot complete because the authentication server is protected by a ZTNA rule.ResolutionOption 1: Remove the ZTNA rule for the login domainRemove the ZTNA rule for login.microsoftonline.com. This allows the SAML authentication traffic to reach Entra ID over the public internet without ZTNA proxy interception, enabling the login process to complete.Option 2: Adjust proxy mode on macOSIf the login window remains blank, change the proxy_mode setting in the ZTNA profile on FortiClient EMS. Set this value to 4 to use the FortiClient macOS proxy extension, which is the method recommended by Apple for network traffic interception.Log in to the FortiClient EMS console.Navigate to the ZTNA profile configuration.Set the proxy_mode value to 4.Deploy the updated profile to the macOS endpoints.Note: This may allow the login window to load, but it may introduce intermittency when loading internal applications, requiring multiple browser refreshes.Option 3: Use an alternative Identity Provider (IdP)Use FortiAuthenticator as the SAML IdP to resolve loading issues on both Windows and macOS.Option 4: Fortinet TAC support can provide an interim FortiClient version to resolve this issue: "FortiClient_7.4.9.4911.interim_macosx".

topics.title: Preventing IPsec tunnel-bound traffic from exiting Internet interfaces without static blackhole routes
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to use BGP link-down failover and firewall deny policies to help prevent traffic destined for workloads reachable through IPsec tunnels from exiting through Internet interfaces when the tunnel routes are unavailable.This approach provides policy-based traffic blocking; it does not install a blackhole route in the routing table.ScopeFortiGate with two BGP neighbors established over IPsec tunnels.Example topologyAll IP addresses and subnets below are illustrative documentation values.SolutionEnable link-down failover for the BGP neighborsEnsure each BGP neighbor is associated with its corresponding tunnel interface. Enable link-down-failover for both neighbors:config router bgp config neighbor edit "203.0.113.1" set link-down-failover enable next edit "203.0.113.2" set link-down-failover enable next end endCreate address objects for the IPsec tunnel destination prefixesCreate a firewall address object for the remote workload subnet 198.51.100.0/24.For deployments with multiple remote subnets, create the required address objects and collect them into an address group. Ensure all destination prefixes requiring protection are included.Configure the firewall policiesConfigure the policies in the following order:Order 1Policy name - IPsec tunnel accessIncoming interface - Relevant LAN interfacesOutgoing interface - IPsec tunnel interfaces or their zoneSource - 192.0.2.0/24Destination - 198.51.100.0/24Action - ACCEPTOrder 2Policy name - IPsec tunnel leakage preventionIncoming interface - Relevant LAN interfacesOutgoing interface - Internet interfaces or WAN zoneSource - 192.0.2.0/24Destination - 198.51.100.0/24Action - DENY, with logging enabledOrder 3Policy name - Normal Internet accessIncoming interface - Relevant LAN interfacesOutgoing interface - Internet interfaces or WAN zoneSource - 192.0.2.0/24Destination - As requiredAction - ACCEPTFor the IPsec tunnel leakage prevention policy:Include all relevant source networks.Include every Internet egress interface or the applicable zone.Set the service to ALL and the schedule to always.Enable logging for denied traffic.Place the policy above any Internet access policy that could permit traffic to the protected remote subnets.Use the appropriate interface or zone objects for the deployment, including the applicable SD-WAN zone where relevant.Expected behaviorWhen an IPsec tunnel route to 198.51.100.0/24 is available, traffic follows the selected tunnel and is evaluated against the IPsec tunnel access policy.If both tunnel routes are withdrawn and route selection directs the traffic toward an Internet interface, the IPsec tunnel leakage prevention policy denies and logs matching traffic before it reaches the normal Internet access policy.VerificationDuring an approved maintenance window:Confirm that a client in 192.0.2.0/24 can reach a workload in 198.51.100.0/24 through the expected IPsec tunnel.Make both IPsec tunnel paths unavailable and confirm that the remote workload routes are withdrawn.Generate traffic from the LAN client to the remote workload.Verify that the traffic is denied and logged by the IPsec tunnel leakage prevention policy.Restore the IPsec tunnel paths and confirm that routing and connectivity recover.
