topics.title: Best practices for Fortinet Single Sign-On (FSSO) deployments
topics.summary: DescriptionHow Fortinet Single Sign-On (FSSO) works at concept level and which design decisions make an FSSO deployment stable, flexible and scalable.Many FSSO deployments work non-optimally. Such setups may run into issues later: after a new domain controller is added, after a collector failover, or when the number of users grows. Understanding the flow makes it possible to recognize where design can be improved and to change it before it causes an incident.This article is not a configuration guide. Step-by-step configuration is covered by the articles linked at the end.ScopeFortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FSSO Collector Agent, DC Agent, and TS Agent in Windows Active Directory environments.SolutionTable of contents:Authentication basicsHow FSSO worksFlow diagramDesign best practicesTroubleshooting along the flowAuthentication basics:User identity versus IP address:A firewall policy matches packets, and a packet carries a source IP address, a destination, and a service. It does not carry a username. To allow or log traffic per user or per group, FortiGate needs a table that says which user is currently behind which IP address, and which groups this user belongs to.Directory and domain controller:The identity itself is stored in a directory. In a Windows domain environment, Active Directory (AD), this role is taken by the domain controllers (DCs), which hold the users, their passwords, and their group memberships.A DC is a server that holds a copy of the directory and answers authentication requests against it. When a user logs on to a domain workstation, the workstation sends the request to a DC, and the DC checks the credentials and replies.Active and passive authentication:With active authentication, FortiGate itself asks the user for credentials (for example, with a captive portal) and checks them against a user database.With passive authentication, FortiGate never asks. It is told that a user has already authenticated somewhere else, and it treats the IP address of this user as logged on.Unlike SAML, LDAP, or RADIUS authentication, FSSO is a passive method. It does not trigger the authentication. The FSSO components listen in on an authentication that has already taken place between the workstation and the DC, treat this event as trusted, and share the result.Three consequences follow from this, and most FSSO design rules are derived from them:FSSO is IP-based. Only one user can exist per IP address (Terminal Servers with TS Agent are the exception).FortiGate only knows what it has been told. If the logon was not detected, or was detected with the wrong IP address or without the right group, the policy matching is affected.Windows AD may not report logoffs. Something has to check whether a logon is still valid. Collector Agent and FortiAuthenticator can do this periodically.How FSSO works:FSSO has three roles:Login sources detect that a user has logged on.For Windows domain users, this is either the Security event log of the DCs (polling mode) or a DC Agent installed on the DCs.The collector is the center of FSSO.It is either a FortiAuthenticator or the FSSO Collector Agent software on a Windows server. It processes the logons, keeps the user database of current logons, and forwards them.FortiGate receives the user logon list and uses it in policies and logs.The flow below describes the most common setup, a Windows domain logon. The step numbers match the diagram in section 3.Step 1 - The user logs on to the domain.The workstation first has to find a DC. It asks DNS for the service (SRV) records of its AD domain, in the form _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs. , and prefers a DC of its own AD site (see the Microsoft documentation How domain controllers are located in Windows). The DC that answers is not fixed. Any DC that serves the site of the client can handle the logon, and the same client can use a different DC the next day.To verify this on the workstation, use echo %logonserver% to show the DC that handled the current logon, and nltest /dsgetdc: to show the DC that the locator returns at this moment.Step 2 - The DC records the logon.A successful authentication creates entries in the Security event log of the DC that handled it. This article calls such an entry a Windows logon event.Common event IDs relevant to FSSO are:Event IDMeaning in WindowsNote4768Kerberos authentication ticket (TGT) requestedContains user and client IP address4769Kerberos service ticket requestedNot supported alone; requires 47684776Credential validation by the DC (NTLM)Contains user and workstation name4624Account successfully logged onContains user, workstation name, and source addressWhich of these IDs are read depends on the use of Collector Agent or FortiAuthenticator and their configuration. The full list per product, including the legacy Windows 2003 IDs, is in Technical Tip: Windows event IDs used by FSSO in WinSec polling mode.In current environments, 4624 is the event seen most often. 4768, together with 4769 and 4776, are also

topics.title: Analytics and dashboards fail with certificate errors on FortiSIEM nodes after upgrade to 7.6.x
topics.summary: DescriptionUpgrading a FortiSIEM node to version 7.6.x may cause SSL certificate validation failures, preventing analytics and dashboards from loading.ScopeFortiSIEM.SolutionSymptomsAfter upgrading a FortiSIEM node, Analytics and Dashboards may fail to load. In this scenario, the AppServer logs on the replica nodes display the following error, and the corresponding error message is shown in the GUI.(certificate_unknown) No trusted certificate found sun.security.validator.ValidatorException: No trusted certificate foundRoot causeThe issue is caused by missing internal FortiSIEM certificate entries in the SSL keystore and truststore files on the nodes. Specifically, the fortisiem-appserver-trust-ca entry is missing from cacerts.p12 and the fortisiem-appserver-key entry is missing from keystore.p12. topics.title: FortiNAC integration with FortiClient EMS does not polls EMS correctly when Multi-Tenancy is enabled
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiNAC fails to integrate with FortiClient EMS when Multi-Tenancy is enabled on the FortiClient EMS server, and hosts are not polled correctly from EMS. Test Connection and Poll status both report success, but in practice FortiNAC does not poll all details or hosts from FortiClient EMS.ScopeFortiNAC with FortiEMS Service Connector, FortiEMSSolutionSymptomsWhen Multi-Tenancy is enabled on the FortiClient EMS server, the FortiNAC integration fails. Based on the debug logs, the polling request returns the following error:request from global is not allowed Below are sample logs from the debug logs.2026-11-25 19:54:47.303 +0000 https-jsse-nio-0.0.0.0-8443-exec-46] DEBUG yams.FortinetEMSServer - cookie-name = csrftoken 2026-11-25 19:54:47.303 +0000 https-jsse-nio-0.0.0.0-8443-exec-46] DEBUG yams.FortinetEMSServer - cookie-value = 2026-11-25 19:54:47.616 +0000 https-jsse-nio-0.0.0.0-8443-exec-46] DEBUG yams.FortinetEMSServer - response val = {"result": {"retval": -5, "message": "Request from global is not allowed."}} 2026-11-25 19:54:47.616 +0000 https-jsse-nio-0.0.0.0-8443-exec-46] DEBUG yams.FortinetEMSServer - FortinetEMSServer:getEndpointArray - start 2026-11-25 19:54:47.616 +0000 https-jsse-nio-0.0.0.0-8443-exec-46] DEBUG yams.FortinetEMSServer - message = Request from global is not allowed. 2026-11-25 19:54:47.616 +0000 https-jsse-nio-0.0.0.0-8443-exec-46] DEBUG yams.FortinetEMSServer - cookie-name = sessionidRoot causeThe issue occurs because the FortiNAC Service Connector is configured to use a Global administrator account. When Multi-Tenancy is active on FortiClient EMS, authentication requests from the Global site are not permitted for this integration; the connector must use an account associated with a specific site. ResolutionTo resolve this issue, create a site-specific administrator account on the FortiClient EMS server and update the FortiNAC configuration.Log in to the FortiClient EMS server.Create a new administrator account specifically under the target site (e.g., the specific organization site) rather than the Global site.Log in to the FortiNAC GUI.Navigate to the Service Connector settings for FortiClient EMS.Replace the Global administrator credentials with the credentials of the newly created site administrator account.Save the configuration and verify that the integration is successful.

topics.title: How to fix the error code 2502 during FortiClient Windows installation
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to solve FortiClient error code is 2502 during installation.ScopeFortiClient.SolutionIf you encounter the following error when installing FortiClient:"The installer has encountered an unexpected error installing this package. This may indicate a problem with this package. The error code is 2502"This issue occurs when installing, updating, or uninstalling the program because the system's temporary folder lacks write permissions.The two most common solutions are:Run the installer with administrator privileges (Quick fix):Since .msi files do not display a direct "Run as administrator" option, you can force the process via the console:Press the "Windows + X" keys and select Terminal (Administrator) or open the Command Prompt (as Administrator).Type msiexec /i (with a space at the end), drag the FortiClient installer file into the console window so that its full path is inserted, and press Enter.(If you are uninstalling, you can open Task Manager, end the explorer.exe process, go to File > Run new task, type explorer.exe, and check the box "Create this task with administrative privileges" before proceeding with the uninstallation.)Fix permissions for the "Temp" folder:If the previous method fails, the installer may still be blocked from writing temporary files in Windows:Open File Explorer and go to C:\Windows.Locate the Temp folder, right-click on it, and select Properties.Go to the Security tab and click Advanced.Click Add > Select a principal.Type "Everyone," click Check Names, and then click OK.Check the Full control box, click OK, and then click Apply.Try installing or uninstalling FortiClient again.

topics.title: Configure SNMP an firewall rules in EMS 7.4.x
topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to configure Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) on FortiClient Endpoint Management System (EMS).ScopeFortiClient EMS.SolutionTo configure SNMP on FortiClient EMS, follow these steps:Enable SNMP on FortiClient EMS by running the command:config set snmp --enabled trueSet the SNMP community string by running the command: config set snmp --snmp.community publicSet the SNMP host by running the command: config set snmp --snmp.host 192.0.2.1Verify the SNMP configuration is correct by running the command:config get snmp --enabled config get snmp --snmp.host config get snmp --snmp.communityVerify that there are no firewall rules blocking the SNMP traffic.system get firewall --allConfigure a firewall rule to allow SNMP and assign a network adapter.system set firewall allow --service --adapter allIf issues persist, check the FortiClient EMS version and ensure it is running the latest release. Keep in mind there is a known bug (BUG-ID 1243221) that was resolved in versions 7.4.8 and 8.0.0.For more information on configuring SNMP on FortiClient EMS, refer to the FortiClient EMS Release Notes and the Resolved Issues section.

topics.title: FortiSOAR Exchange connector reply-all function does not work or displays HTML as plain text
topics.summary: DescriptionThe reply_all function in the Exchange connector renders HTML code as plain text in the email body instead of rendering it as HTML, or the reply_all() function fails.ScopeFortiSOAR Exchange connector 4.7.0 or 4.8.0SolutionSymptomsAfter upgrading the Exchange connector to version 4.7.0 or 4.8.0, the Send Reply_All function does not work, fails with the error reply_all() got an unexpected keyword argument 'to_recipients,' or the HTML code is displayed as plain text in the email body. The HTML is not rendered correctly for the recipient. The CauseThe email_operations.py file in the Exchange connector does not use the HTMLBody class for the reply body, and a new field has been added in the new connector version (to_recipients=cc_emails), which causes the email client to treat the content as plain text. SolutionModify the connector configuration file to ensure the email body is sent as HTML.SSH into the FortiSOAR instance.Open the email_operations.py file using a text editor:sudo vi /opt/cyops/configs/integrations/connectors/exchange_4_7_0/email_operations.pyNavigate to line 472.Replace the following line:msg.reply_all(subject=subject, body=parsed_body, to_recipients=cc_emails)Use this line:msg.reply_all(subject=subject, body=HTMLBody(parsed_body))Save the changes and exit the editor.Restart the uwsgi service to apply the changes:systemctl restart uwsgiVerify that the reply all function renders HTML correctly.

topics.title: SD-WAN 'set default enable' is not applied to local-out traffic when a blackhole or summary route is present
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes why traffic that is originated by the FortiGate is dropped when a blackhole or summarized route is configured for the overlay range, even though an SD-WAN rule with set default enable is configured for that range.ScopeFortiGate, SD-WAN (WAN Intelligence). Observed on FortiOS version 7.6.x; the behavior is not release-specific.SolutionAn SD-WAN rule is evaluated only after the destination is resolved by a Forwarding Information Base (FIB) lookup. This lookup is bypassed when set default enable is configured, so forwarding traffic can be steered by the rule without a route via an SD-WAN member.Two conditions must be kept in mind:Local-out traffic (traffic initiated by the FortiGate itself, for example to a management server) is not affected by set default enable, even when set interface-select-method sdwan is configured. A routing table lookup is always performed.A blackhole route (a summary route with no outgoing interface) is a terminal entry, so it is matched for every outgoing interface. Packets that match it are dropped, even when set gateway enable is configured on the rule.Example of the condition: An aggregate is summarizing the overlay range:config router static edit 602 set dst 10.0.0.0 255.0.0.0 set distance 220 set blackhole enable set vrf 1 next endS 10.0.0.0/8 [220/0] is a summary, Null, [1/0]With this route installed, sessions to the spoke range 10.100.0.0/16 and to the management server 10.50.0.0/16 are no longer created, and the hit_count of the SD-WAN rule is no longer increased:diagnose firewall proute listThe route and the rule can be reviewed with:get router info routing-table all diagnose sys sdwan service4 diagnose sys sdwan memberWhere the drop must be confirmed, the packet flow can be traced:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug flow filter addr 10.50.0.10 diagnose debug flow show function-name enable diagnose debug flow trace start 100 diagnose debug enable Debug output is stopped and cleared with:diagnose debug flow trace stop diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset diagnose debug flow filter clearWorkaround.A route that is more specific than the blackhole route is preferred by the FIB lookup, so the local-out destination is resolved before the blackhole route is reached. More specific static routes pointing at the SD-WAN zones are configured ahead of the blackhole route; several subnets are placed in one entry with set dstaddr so the number of routes is kept low:config router static edit 600 set dstaddr "spoke_overlay" "mgmt_servers" set sdwan-zone "zone_underlay_inter" "zone_underlay_intra" set tag 201 set vrf 1 next endset vrf and set tag are configured only where a non-default VRF or route tagging is in use.Related documents:Technical Tip: Understanding Default and Gateway Parameters in SD-WANAdditional fields for configuring WAN intelligenceDebugging the packet flow

topics.title: With private-data-encryption enabled, can an admin still change a local certificate's private-key password and export the usable private key?
topics.summary: I'm documenting, for a security assessment, exactly what protection private-data-encryption (PDE) + TPM give to a locally generated certificate's private key against an authenticated administrator. topics.title: IPsec IKEv2 VPN authentication fails with CA does not match when using EMS trust store
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiGate users may encounter authentication failures in IPsec IKEv2 remote access VPNs when combining the EMS trust store with specific peer group validation settings.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient/EMS.SolutionSymptoms.After upgrading to FortiOS version 7.6.7 or FortiOS version 7.6.8, FortiClient reports 'Authentication failed' during IPsec IKEv2 VPN connection attempts. The issue occurs when the following configuration is used:set cert-trust-store emsset peertype peergrpset peergrp Debug logs for fnbamd show the following error:__quick_check_peer-CA does not match. 'EMS_Client_Validator' check ret:badThis results in the failure message: 'certificate validation before eap failed'.Root cause.In FortiOS version 7.6.7 and above, IKE delegates peer certificate validation to fnbamd. When cert-trust-store ems is configured, the certificate chain is built from the EMS CA cache. These certificates have an empty cmdb_name. If mandatory-ca-verify is enabled in the peer object, fnbamd compares the local CMDB CA name against this empty name, causing a mismatch and authentication failure.Resolution.Allow the EMS trust store to handle certificate trust and remove the explicit user peer reference from the Phase 1 configuration.Enter the IPsec Phase 1 interface configuration:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit Change the peer type to any to remove the peer group restriction:set peertype anyEnsure the EMS trust store and other required settings remain enabled:set cert-trust-store ems set ems-sn-check enable set eap enable set remote-gw-match ztna set remote-gw-ztna-tags next endNote: The GUI may display a warning stating 'Specifying a Peer Certificate or Peer Group is recommended'. This is a general advisory for signature-authenticated IKEv2 tunnels and can be safely ignored when using cert-trust-store ems, as the EMS trust store already establishes the certificate trust.

topics.title: Administrator SSO authentication fails after upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.8.SolutionAfter upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential. The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login for FortiGate administrators with Entra ID acting as SAML IdP.Security Fabric SSO with root FortiGate as IdP, for example see Configuring single-sign-on in the Security Fabric. Confirmed not affected:VPN user SSO authentication.Other FortiOS versions including FortiOS 7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2.Local administrator authentication.Remote administrator authentication using RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+.While access to the FortiGate from FortiManagement Cloud (FortiGate Cloud) is technically not affected, SSO authentication to the FortiGate is still not possible over this management path. Issue matching:To confirm the issue, check the FortiOS crashlog for a matching "FORTISM Violation" from the time of the access attempt. This can be done by accessing the FortiGate using a local administrator account and executing diagnose debug crashlog read | grep YYYY-MM-DD .FGT-A(Primary) # diagnose debug crashlog read | grep 2026-10-20 6545: 2026-10-20 11:09:52 domain=WEB_AUTH domainid=37 acl=write msg="gFORTISM Violation: pid-236, 6546: 2026-10-20 11:09:52 api-open_w(), path-/tmp/ftnt1_sp_metadata.xml]." 6547: 2026-10-20 11:10:24 domain=WEB_AUTH domainid=37 acl=write msg="gFORTISM Violation: pid-236, 6548: 2026-10-20 11:10:24 api-open_w(), path-/tmp/ftnt1_sp_metadata.xml]."This issue is tracked under Issue ID #1338764. See FortiOS 7.6.8 Known Issues. Workaround:At this time, the only available workaround is to use another administrator authentication method.If no suitable administrator account exists, console access to a physical device can be used to recover access, see Technical Tip: Boot the backup firmware and config via console.If the device is centrally managed by FortiManager or a valid FortiManagement Cloud subscription, an administrator can be added. See Recover access to FortiGate via FortiManagement Cloud. Resolution:A fix for this issue exists and is planned for inclusion in FortiOS 7.6.9, currently expected to release in late November 2026. FortiOS firmware release schedules are subject to change without notice. Related article:Create a "break glass" admin account on the FortiGate as a backup for remote authentication/MFA (Recommendation)

topics.title: Troubleshooting FortiEDR logs not appearing on FortiAnalyzer
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the step-by-step troubleshooting when FortiEDR event logs sent via Syslog are missing or not displayed as FortiEDR logs on FortiAnalyzer.ScopeFortiAnalyzer.FortiEDR.SolutionStep 1: Verify the FortiEDR configuration.Confirm FortiEDR is configured as described in the following article:Configuring FortiEDR to send logs to FortiAnalyzerMake sure the Syslog destination uses the 'FAZ' format, the event types are enabled in the Notifications pane, and 'Send syslog notification' is enabled in the Playbook assigned to the Collector Group of the affected device.Step 2: Check the Test message on FortiAnalyzer.On FortiEDR, go to Administration -> Export Settings -> Syslog and select 'Test'.On FortiAnalyzer, go to Log View -> Logs -> Syslog.The Test message should appear as a generic Syslog entry. Unresolved placeholders such as ${Organization} and ${CollectorGroup} are expected for Test messages.Test message received: the connection works; continue to Step 3.Test message not received: check the firewall, NAT, and routing between the FortiEDR Central Manager and FortiAnalyzer, then go to Step 4.Step 3: Trigger a real incident and check FortiAnalyzer.Download the EICAR test file on an endpoint in the affected Collector Group and confirm the incident appears under Incidents on FortiEDR.On FortiAnalyzer, go to Log View -> Logs and filter by the FortiEDR 'devid' with a wide time range. Also check Log View -> Log Browse for a log file of the FortiEDR device.Incident displayed as FEDR Log: the issue is resolved.Incident not displayed: continue to Step 4.Step 4: Check the payload that reaches FortiAnalyzer.Do not rely on the connection status shown on FortiEDR. Sniff the traffic on FortiAnalyzer while triggering the incident again, and check that the log format is correct.diagnose sniffer packet any 'udp and port 514' 3Press Ctrl+C to stop the capture. If the Syslog destination uses TCP, use 'port 514' (or the configured port) instead.Check the payload:No packets: check the firewall, NAT, and routing. Syslog is sent from the FortiEDR Central Manager IP.Real 'devid=FEDR...' present and the fields populated: the payload is correct; continue to Step 5.Placeholders such as ${SystemEventTemplateFields.ComponentType} instead of real values: the logs are malformed by FortiEDR. Example of a correct payload (shortened):type=event subtype="Security Event" ... classification=Malicious ... devid=FEDR0xxxxxxxx ...Step 5: Check log reception on FortiAnalyzer.Run the following commands while triggering the incident.diagnose test application fortilogd 3 diagnose test application fortilogd 5 Healthy example for 'fortilogd 3':FEDR0xxxxxxxxxxxx status=up, root status=alive last-recv=1787905951 last-upload=0If the payload reaches FortiAnalyzer with a real devid but the log is still not displayed in Log View, the issue is on the FortiAnalyzer parsing side.Step 6: Collect debug output if needed (and send it to Support).Enable the debug below, trigger the incident again, then reset the debug:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application fortilogd 255 diagnose debug filter " " diagnose debug timestamp enable diagnose debug enableTo check the device connection and admission (TLS handshake, certificate, and login), use:diagnose debug application oftpd 255 Related article:Configuring FortiEDR to send logs to FortiAnalyzer

topics.title: FortiSwitch logs are not displayed under CLI (0 logs found) when event logging to flash memory is enabled
topics.summary: DescriptionOn FortiSwitch, execute log display returns 0 logs found even though logging is enabled and the configuration matches other units that display logs normally. The logs exist but are stored on a different log device than the one the CLI is reading.ScopeFortiSwitch running FortiSwitchOS 8.0.SolutionSymptomsExecute log display returns 0 logs found. / 0 logs returned. MGT-SW01 # execute log display 0 logs found. 0 logs returned.Execute log filter dump looks the same on working and affected units (device: memory).SW01 # execute log filter dump category: event device: memory start-line: 1 view-lines: 10 max-checklines: 0Diagnose debug application miglogd -1 shows __handle_cron_message-Disk uploading log 90% full recurring each minute.MGT-SW01 # dignose debug application miglogd -1 MGT-SW01 # MGT-SW01 # diagnose debug console timestamp enable MGT-SW01 # MGT-SW01 # diagnose debug enable MGT-SW01 # 2026-10-02 08:28:01 miglog_main.c[569] __handle_cron_message-Disk uploading log 90% full 2026-10-02 08:29:01 miglog_main.c[569] __handle_cron_message-Disk uploading log 90% full 2026-10-02 08:30:02 miglog_main.c[569] __handle_cron_message-Disk uploading log 90% full 2026-10-02 08:30:02 miglog_main.c[712] __handle_logs-540 bytes received 2026-10-02 08:30:02 miglog_main.c[680] handle_next_log-New log request (ID: 0x9F00, length: 536) 2026-10-02 08:30:02 miglog_main.c[681] handle_next_log-Original log request (ID: 0x0) 2026-10-02 08:31:02 miglog_main.c[569] __handle_cron_message-Disk uploading log 90% fullCauseThe units whose logs are missing have event logging to flash memory enabled, and the flash log area has reached its full-warning threshold. The Disk uploading log 90% full line matches the default second full-warning threshold of 90 for the config log disk setting.The default log-view device is 0 (memory), so with logs going to flash, the default view shows nothing.ResolutionPoint the log view at the device that actually holds the logs, or move logging back to memory.Option 1: View the logs that are already in flash (no configuration change):execute log filter device # lists 0: memory, 1: flash, and the current setting execute log filter device 1 execute log displayOption 2: Restore logging to memory:This is what recovered 5 of the 6 units on the ticket:config log disk setting set status enable end

topics.title: FortiGate logs show ICAP connection errors and client sessions are dropped during file uploads because the ICAP connection queue becomes full.
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiGate logs show ICAP connection errors and client sessions are dropped during file uploads because the ICAP connection queue becomes full.ScopeFortiGate, FortiProxy.SolutionSymptomsWhen downloading or uploading files through a FortiGate configured with an ICAP profile, the webpage may take a long time to load and eventually time out. The FortiGate logs display the following error message:msg="ICAP connection error. Client session dropped" reason="ICAP server disconnected"WAD debug logs may show the following warning:wad_icap_srv_conn_on_error :516 ICAP ..(nil):(:0->x.x.x.x:1344)... wad icap port cancel/error Root causeThe issue occurs when the ICAP connection queue becomes full. The max-connection limit is distributed across all WAD workers in a first-come, first-served pattern. If the ICAP server takes too long to respond or fails to send a response on time, connections remain occupied. Once the available connections for the workers are exhausted, subsequent requests are queued. If these requests exceed the queue timeout, the FortiGate terminates the session and logs a port cancel error.Additionally, we can observe that the source port is displayed as (nil) in the debug output, indicating that the source-side socket/connection reference is NULL in this error-handling context. ResolutionIncrease the maximum number of connections allowed for the ICAP server to prevent the connection queue from filling up.Access the Command Line Interface (CLI) of the FortiGate.Run the following commands to increase the max-connections limit (for example, from 100 to 500):config icap server edit " " set max-connections 500 next endIf the issue persists, collect the following diagnostics for further analysis: Collect system status:get system status diagnose sys icap-remote-server status diagnose wad health worker diag wad stats worker.icap_client diagnose wad stats worker.conn_pool diagnose sys top 2 20 Enable WAD debugs:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose wad filter clear diagnose wad filter src diagnose wad debug enable category icap diagnose wad debug enable category ssl diagnose wad debug enable category http diagnose wad debug enable category scan diagnose wad debug enable category session diagnose debug enable Run packet sniffer:In a separate CLI session, run the following command to capture traffic between the client and the ICAP server:diagnose sniffer packet any '(host and port 1344) or host ' 6 0 a Reproduce the issue:Initiate the file upload or download from the client and maintain the test for 2 to 3 minutes until the error occurs. Finalize logs:Run the status commands from Step 1 again during the issue, then disable debugs and generate a TAC report:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset execute tac report

topics.title: Managed devices missing after upgrade FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to troubleshoot an upgraded FortiManager causing the managed devices to go missing.Scope FortiManager.SolutionCheck FortiManager and FortiGate connectivity:diagnose debug application fgfmsd 255In this case, the debug will show keepalive and success, indicating that the FGFM tunnel exists and is working. With this information, the issue is isolated within the FortiManager database instead of connectivity with the managed device:FGFMs( -6917-- ): fgfm_keepalive_handler: old chksum: 03 6d db 79 ce 12 aa b8 76 20 f1 9e 9e 57 e9 1d, auto_ret rieve_pending = 0. FGFMs( --6917- ): fgfm_keepalive_handler: new chksum: 03 6d db 79 ce 12 aa b8 76 20 f1 9e 9e 57 e9 1d FGFMs( --6917- ): server:send: reply 200 request=keepalive cur_tun_serial=Check the related database:diagnose dvm device listThe output should show an empty list with no devices, despite there being an FGFM tunnel.Perform rollback:The rollback should be performed using a VM snapshot. If a snapshot is not available, perform the rollback using the following guide:Downgrading to previous firmware versionsCheck the device database again:Since the rollback to the last known good version was performed, the list should show devices. If not, it is possible the database is already corrupted and needs to be restored to an older, last known good version.If the device list appears, check the entries for a duplicate entry. Example:fmgfaz-managed 666 - STSC-FT-FW01 root 35.00155 (regular) 7.0 MR4 (2731) Rev2 |- STATUS: dev-db: not modified; conf: in sync; cond: offline; dm: autoupdated; conn: down |- vdom:�3]root flags:1 adom:root pkg:minstalled]root_Policy_Package fwmprof:linstalled]FG80F-FirmwareUpgrade tmplgrp:dinstalled]03 root |- vdom:t4133]VDOM1 flags:1 adom:root pkg: installed]VDOM1_Policy_Package |- vdom:y3430]VDOM2 flags:1 adom:root pkg:�installed]VDOM2_Policy_Package |- vdom:M12189]ROOT flags:0 adom:root pkg:�never-installed] |- vdom:o12362]ROOT flags:1 adom:root pkg: never-installed]FortiManager detected two VDOMs named "ROOT" and assigned them different OIDs. During the upgrade, the database is checked, and this duplicate entry caused the corruption.Remove the device:A device can be removed via the GUI as per the following guide:Deleting a deviceOr using the following command:diagnose dvm device delete Note: Put the FortiManager in 'Offline mode' to avoid the references from being deleted along with the device:Technical Tip: How to reset ADOM settings in FortiManager/FortiAnalyzerPerform upgrade:After the device is removed, perform the upgrade to the target version again and re-add the device. The upgrade should not cause the issue to recur because the duplicate entry that caused the database corruption has been removed beforehand.

topics.title: FortiGate Cloud API proxy returns HTTP 500 'version not supported' for FortiOS version 8.0 devices
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiOS API requests proxied through FortiGate Cloud fail with a version not supported error when targeting devices running FortiOS version 8.0.0.ScopeFortiGate, FortiGate Cloud.SolutionSymptoms.When using the FortiGate Cloud API to proxy requests to a FortiGate device running FortiOS version 8.0.0, the API returns an HTTP 500 error. This occurs for requests such as CMDB and event-log reads.Example failed requests:GET /forticloudapi/v1/fgt/ /api/v2/cmdb/system/global?account_id= GET /forticloudapi/v1/fgt/ /api/v2/log/forticloud/event/system?rows=1&account_id= The response body contains the following error:error=internal_error, error_code=-1, error_description="version not supported"Root cause.The FortiGate Cloud API proxy does not support the API versioning used by FortiOS version 8.0.0 devices. Resolution.This issue is resolved in FortiGate Cloud version 26.4. Update the FortiGate Cloud environment to version 26.4 or above to restore API proxy functionality for FortiOS version 8.0.0 devices.

topics.title: Rebuilding a FortiGate-VM in Azure without changing its network identity
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a step-by-step procedure for replacing a FortiGate virtual machine with a fresh deployment of the same generation, while keeping its existing network interfaces, IP addressing, and configuration.ScopeFortiGate-VM deployed in Microsoft Azure.SolutionSometimes a FortiGate-VM in Azure has to be rebuilt, for example because of a corrupted OS disk, a damaged image or a clean-slate requirement, even though the VM generation stays the same. Azure has no built-in rebuild function for this, so the approach is to deploy a fresh VM, move the original network interfaces across so that the firewall keeps the same IP addresses and routes, and then restore the configuration.Phase 1: Requirements to meet first.Location: Same Azure region, subscription, and resource group as the current VM. A NIC can only be attached to a VM in the same location and subscription.VM generation: Same as the current VM (choose the matching Marketplace image).Licensing model: Identical: BYOL stays BYOL, and PAYG stays PAYG.FortiOS version: Identical on both VMs. Do not restore a configuration from an older release onto a newer one, as it needs manual header edits and can fail to parse. If the Marketplace no longer offers your exact build, deploy the closest one and bring it to the identical version before restoring.VM size: Must support the same number of NICs as today, and accelerated networking if the current NICs use it.Access: Serial console access (boot diagnostics enabled on the VM), needed to set up interfaces if the firewall is not reachable after the swap.BYOL only: Internet access on the new VM for license activation, so you may need to attach a temporary public IP directly to one of its NICs. Have the license file or key at hand.FortiManager: If the firewall is managed, remove it there first.Phase 2: Preserve the current state.Export the running configuration from the existing FortiGate (Configuration -> Backup) using a super_admin account.Write down each NIC's name, its portN mapping, its MAC address, and its order in the Azure Portal.BYOL only; release the license so it is not active on two VMs at once. FortiGuard must not see the same license used twice at the same time. The following commands should be executed:execute vm-license-options reset execute update-nowDeallocate the old VM. A guest shutdown is not enough, because NICs can only be added or removed while the VM is stopped (deallocated).Phase 3: Prepare the replacement VM.Deploy a new FortiGate VM from the Marketplace, same region, subscription, resource group, generation, and FortiOS version. A single-VM template is enough.Activate the license.Shut down (deallocate) the new VM. Do not restore the backup yet. It will be restored after the NIC swap, once the VM has the same number of NICs the configuration defines.Phase 4: Swap the network interfaces.Azure only allows detaching NICs from a stopped VM, and a VM must always keep at least one NIC. That is why the swap follows a specific order.Detach every NIC from the new VM except its primary.Attach one of the NICs you removed from the new VM to the old VM, so it still has an interface.Detach the original NICs from the old VM.Attach the original NICs to the new VM, keeping the same order as in the Azure Portal, with the original NIC-1 set explicitly as primary.Remove the new VM's own original NIC, which is no longer needed now that the original NIC-1 is primary.Phase 5: Bring it up, restore, and validate.Start the new VM and follow the boot process on the serial console. If management is not reachable, configure one interface and enable HTTPS or SSH from the CLI.Restore the backup (Configuration -> Restore). The VM reboots afterwards.Check the basics: get system status (version, serial, license), interface status and IPs, routing, policies, VPN tunnels, and management access.Verify the port mapping. FortiGate assigns ports by the order NICs are detected at boot. Compare the MACs with the NICs in the Azure Portal.Clean up anything the Marketplace deployment created automatically (the unused NICs, a temporary public IP, an NSG, and so on).Keep the old VM deallocated until being confident, then delete it.If the FortiGate is part of an HA pair:Temporarily disable HA override, and rebuild the secondary first to avoid an unexpected failover.Back up both units. Shut down the secondary first, or both if your maintenance window allows.For each rebuild, follow Phases 3 to 5: restore the configuration only after the NICs have been swapped and the VM has booted. Configure a management interface and enable HTTPS or SSH on the console, then restore.Once the new secondary is healthy, repeat for the primary.If the SDN connector uses Managed Identity, assign the same roles to the new VMs. A Service Principal needs nothing extra, since its credentials are in the backup.

topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to remove implicit system-generated local-in policies that may show TCP port 443 as open on public interfaces due to IKE TCP transport settings.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionFirst, these are implicit admin local-in policies, so they cannot be deleted. If the requirement is to disable this or removed from this section, you need to find out the underlying services that is running or listening on that port.Implicit policies are found at Policy and objects -> Local-In policies.In this example, the implicit rule is tied to the ike-tcp-port setting. This port is used for TCP IKE negotiations. topics.title: SNMP buffer limitations
topics.summary: DescriptionSNMP has a buffer limitation of 1400 bytes. This is a hard limitation of the SNMP on FortiGate. This in effect means that if bulk requests are made towards the FortiGate which exceed this response buffer the response values to the OIDs will be Null.ScopeFortiGate, all versions.SolutionThis limitation can be identified within a packet capture. This can either done via GUI (Using the packet capture tool) for port 161 or CLI with the following command.diagnose sniffer packet any 'port 161' 6 0 aWhen inspecting the response send out by FortiGate we see the error message 'tooBig'. This indicates that the out buffer was surpassed and hence the responses are the Null value.The solution to this issue is to limit the bulk requests made by the SNMP client.

topics.title: LDAPS fails to connect even with a correct CN field CA certificate
topics.summary: DescriptionLDAP authentication over LDAPS (TCP 636) fails with certificate verification errors due to an incorrect Root CA certificate installed on the FortiGate.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptomsLDAP authentication over LDAPS (TCP 636) fails. You may see an error message on the GUI, and debug logs show the following error:[1686] __verify_cb-Cert error 20, unable to get local issuer certificate. Depth 0. Subject '/CN= ' [1374] __ldap_tcps_connect-tcps_connect( ) failed: ssl_connect() failed: 167772294 (error:0A000086:SSL routines::certificate verify failed). Root causeThe issue occurs because the Root CA certificate installed on the FortiGate does not match the CA that signed the LDAP server certificate. Starting from FortiOS 7.4.4, the LDAPS/STARTTLS server certificate issuer is enforced, meaning the correct Root CA must be present in the certificate store to validate the server certificate.There can be more than one similar root CA certificate on the domain controller server with the same CN. In a scenario like this, a user might end up importing the wrong CA on the FortiGate. ResolutionVerify that the Root CA certificate installed on the FortiGate is the exact issuer of the LDAP server certificate by comparing the Subject Key Identifier (SKI) and Authority Key Identifier (AKI). Verify certificate identifiersOpen the LDAP server certificate on the Domain Controller.Select Certification Path and double-click the issuer certificate.Select Details and note the value of the Subject Key Identifier (SKI).Next, check the AKI field of the LDAP server certificate, and it should match the SKI of the Root CA certificate.Download the CA certificate installed on the FortiGate.Select Details and note the SKI.Compare both SKI values. If they do not match, the wrong Root CA is installed on the FortiGate. Install the correct Root CA certificateExport the correct Root CA certificate from the Domain Controller or CA server.Select System -> Certificates.Select Create/Import -> CA Certificate.Upload the correct Root CA certificate and select OK.Select User & Authentication -> LDAP Servers.Edit the LDAP server and select the newly imported CA certificate in the Certificate field.Select OK to save the configuration.

topics.title: SNMP configuration on fortiSwitch interface is lost after reboot
topics.summary: DescriptionOn a FortiGate-managed FortiSwitch, SNMP access configured locally on the switch interface is lost after rebooting the switch.After the reboot, SNMP polling to the FortiSwitch interface fails because the SNMP access permission is no longer enabled.ScopeFortiGate-managed FortiSwitchSolutionSymptoms:SNMP polling to the FortiSwitch fails after the switch reboots.SNMP access configured locally on the FortiSwitch interface is no longer available after rebootCause:On FortiGate-managed FortiSwitches, management access permissions are controlled through the FortiGate's FortiSwitch local-access security policy.When SNMP access is configured locally on the FortiSwitch interface, the configuration may not be retained after a reboot or synchronization with the FortiGate.Solution:Apply the following configuration on the FortiGate CLI:config switch-controller security-policy local-access edit "default" set internal-allowaccess https ping ssh snmp set mgmt-allowaccess https ping ssh snmp next endConfigure a FortiGate-managed FortiSwitch locally through its CLI; the configuration may be lost after a reboot or when the switch synchronizes with the FortiGate.This is because the FortiGate maintains the managed FortiSwitch configuration in its own configuration database. Local changes made directly on the switch are not synchronized back to the FortiGate.Hence, pushing the configuration from the FortiGate is the recommended step.

topics.summary: DescriptionSNMPv3 service on a FortiSwitch may become unstable or fail to respond to queriesScopeFortiSwitch.SummarySymptom:The server reports an unstable connection to the FortiSwitch over SNMPv3: the service connects and disconnects frequently, or stops responding to queries entirely.In some cases, the snmpd process crashes and restarts every few seconds, with a segmentation fault visible in the crash logs.The server sends a get-bulk query for LLDP tables (e.g., 1.0.8802.1.1.2.1.3). topics.title: FortiSwitch port1 reserved by the FLinkDhcpDisc trunk
topics.summary: DescriptionOn FortiSwitch FS-1xxG models managed through FortiLink, a static trunk named _FLinkDhcpDisc_ can be created with port1 as its member. This reserves port1 for FortiLink discovery and prevents it from carrying its configured access and tagged VLANs.Deleting the trunk manually restores the intended port configuration temporarily. However, the trunk can reappear after configuration synchronization from the FortiGate.This issue is resolved in FortiSwitchOS 7.4.9 GA and later.ScopeFortiSwitch FS-1xxG models managed by a FortiGate through FortiLink, running affected FortiSwitchOS releases earlier than 7.4.9.The issue was reproduced with the following configuration:FortiGate running FortiOS 7.4.11.FortiSwitch FS-1xxG models running FortiSwitchOS 7.4.8 and below.SolutionThe following symptoms can indicate this issue:Port1 does not carry its configured access and tagged VLANs, such as the access point management VLAN and wireless VLANs.The FortiSwitch configuration contains a static trunk named _FLinkDhcpDisc_, with port1 configured as its member.Run the following command to verify the trunk configuration:show switch trunkThe output contains an entry similar to the following:config switch trunk edit "_FLinkDhcpDisc_" set auto-isl 1 set static-isl enable set members "port1" next endThe FortiSwitch logs contain repeated FortiLink: internal echo reply timed out events, potentially accompanied by port1 link up and down events and associated STP changes.Deleting the _FLinkDhcpDisc_ trunk restores the intended port configuration temporarily. However, the trunk reappears after configuration synchronization from the FortiGate.A known issue affecting FortiSwitch FS-1xxG models causes the default _FLinkDhcpDisc_ trunk to be created on port1 when ports 2 to 8 are used.The trunk reserves port1 for FortiLink discovery and prevents the port from being used with its intended VLAN configuration. This can also result in FortiLink internal echo reply timeout events and associated port link state changes.The issue is documented in the FortiSwitchOS 7.4.9 release notes under resolved issue IDs 1208893 and 1219236.To resolve the issue, upgrade the affected FortiSwitch to a FortiSwitchOS release containing the fix, remove the existing discovery trunk, and synchronize the configuration from the FortiGate.Identify the running FortiSwitchOS version.Run the following command on the affected FortiSwitch:get system statusUpgrade the FortiSwitchOS firmware.Upgrade the affected FortiSwitch to FortiSwitchOS 7.4.9 GA or later. FortiSwitchOS 7.6.5 GA or later also contains the fix.Verify the FortiGate and FortiSwitchOS compatibility using the FortiLink compatibility matrix before upgrading.For a FortiGate running FortiOS 7.4.11, use FortiSwitchOS 7.4.9 GA as the target release.Remove the existing discovery trunk.After upgrading, run the following commands on each affected FortiSwitch:config switch trunk delete "_FLinkDhcpDisc_" endTrigger configuration synchronization from the FortiGate.Run the following command on the FortiGate to trigger configuration synchronization with the affected FortiSwitch:diagnose switch-controller trigger config-sync Lab-SwitchReplace Lab-Switch with the actual managed FortiSwitch name.Monitor the configuration synchronization status.Run the following command on the FortiGate:execute switch-controller get-sync-status allThe following output shows an example where the FortiSwitch configuration synchronization is in progress or pending:Managed-devices in current vdom root: FortiLink interface : fortilink SWITCH-ID (SERIAL) STATUS CONFIG MAC-SYNC HTTP-UPGRADE Lab-Switch-(FS1XXXXXXXXX) Up Sync - topics.title: FortiOS REST API returns 401 after upgrading to 7.6 or 8.0
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter an upgrade from FortiOS 7.4 to the 7.6 or 8.0 branch, REST API calls that use plain username and password (HTTP Basic) can fail with 401.ScopeFortiGateSolutionSymptomScripts and monitoring tools that authenticate with a username and password stop working on the upgraded FortiOS version. A plain request such as the one below is rejected:curl -k -v -u username:password https://192.0.2.10/api/v2/cmdb/system/vdomOutput example:< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized < WWW-Authenticate: error="invalid_token"The credentials are valid, and the same account can still sign in to the GUI. What the API no longer accepts is the HTTP Basic header on its own.WorkaroundThe workaround is to authenticate first and reuse the session cookie for subsequent API requests.Once authenticated through the API endpoint, store the returned session cookies and reuse them for all subsequent API requests instead of providing credentials each time.Log in and save the cookies:FGT=https://192.0.2.10 curl -k -sS -i --compressed -c cookies.txt \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H "Origin: $FGT" \ -H "Referer: $FGT/login" \ -d "{\"username\":\"$FGT_USER\",\"password\":\"$FGT_PASS\"}" \ "$FGT/api/v2/authentication"Call the API with the cookie jar:curl -k -sS -i --compressed -b cookies.txt \ "$FGT/api/v2/cmdb/system/vdom"Receiving an HTTP 200 response containing the VDOM list confirms that the session is working, provided the API call matches the above example.Instructions for running it:Keep the credentials in environment variables (FGT_USER, FGT_PASS), not in the command line or in shell history.The Origin and Referer headers are also required to make the request resemble a GUI login."-k" skips certificate validation. Use it only in a lab environment. In production, install a trusted certificate or pass the "--cacert".Treat cookies.txt as a secret and delete it when the job ends. Sessions also expire under the administrator's idle timeout. Long-running scripts must log in again on a 401.Recommended solutionCreate a dedicated REST API administrator, restrict it to the hosts that need it, and generate a key. Adjust the profile, VDOM, and source address to your environment.The key is displayed only once in FortiGate and must be stored securely in a secrets manager before being used in subsequent API calls through the Bearer authorization header.Example:curl -sS --cacert fgt-ca.pem \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $FGT_TOKEN" \ "$FGT/api/v2/cmdb/system/vdom"Why this approach is recommended:No password is stored in scripts, and the token can be revoked without modifying a normal user account.Access is limited by the profile and the trusted-host list.There is no login step, cookie jar, or session expiry to handle.Related documents:Enhance administrative authentication and session monitoringResolving API connection failure in FortiGate

topics.title: BGP not supported within VRF
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes FortiSwitch BGP support within a VRF.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionBased on the official Fortinet documentation for FortiSwitchOS, it is necessary to distinguish between general BGP support and BGP support within a VRF.Fortinet's Feature Matrix identifies both BGP and VRF as supported features on applicable FortiSwitch models. However, when examining routing protocol integration with VRF, Fortinet explicitly identifies OSPF VRF support as a supported capability.Fortinet's official Feature Matrix confirms that OSPF supports VRF.There is no equivalent documented BGP VRF support entry in the FortiSwitchOS Feature Matrix.Although BGP and VRF are individually supported features, the available official Fortinet documentation does not establish support for running BGP within a VRF on FortiSwitch.Therefore, BGP over VRF is not supported.Recommendation:If dynamic routing within a VRF is required, OSPF is the routing protocol explicitly documented by Fortinet for this functionality.Related document:FortiSwitch Feature Matrix

topics.title: Troubleshooting certificate errors in FortiToken Mobile version 6.7.1 and above
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiToken Mobile version 6.7.1 and above may show a certificate error when it connects to an on-premises FortiAuthenticator or FortiGate during push approval, token activation, or token export (moving tokens to a new phone). The app cannot verify the server certificate because it is untrusted, expired, or not valid for the address the app used to connect.Tokens issued through the Fortinet cloud service are not affected because cloud endpoints use publicly trusted certificates. A certificate error can still occur if a TLS-inspecting proxy intercepts the connection, or if the trusted root certificates on the device are outdated.ScopeFortiToken Mobile version 6.7.1 and above on Android, connecting to an on-premises FortiAuthenticator or FortiGate.SolutionIdentify the error.FortiToken Mobile displays the Untrusted Certificate screen. Depending on the error, the app blocks the connection or offers Allow once, Always allow, and Block (cancel).For example:The server's certificate is not from a trusted certificate authority. The app offers Allow once, Always allow, and Block.Select Allow Once or Always Allow only if thinking that the certificate is valid, or after the administrator confirms that it is valid and correct.The certificate issue must still be resolved on the server.Verify the server certificate.The system administrator must verify the server certificate against the following requirements, and correct or replace it where it does not comply.Subject Alternative Name (SAN).FortiToken Mobile matches the connection address against the SAN entries only. The Common Name (CN) is not used for this validation.A certificate with the correct hostname in the CN but no matching SAN entry is rejected, except in the case described under SAN verification exception. The SAN must contain the exact hostname or IP address used by the app.SAN verification exception.FortiToken Mobile version 6.7.1 and above on Android skips the hostname check against the SAN when the payload fingerprint already proves the identity of the server. Certificate expiry is still enforced.Certificate validity.Confirm that the certificate is within its validity period.notBefore is the date from which the certificate becomes valid.notAfter is the date on which the certificate expires.Renew or replace the certificate if it has expired or is not yet valid.Signature algorithm.The certificate must use a signature algorithm of SHA-256 or stronger. Certificates signed with SHA-1 or MD5 are rejected. Reissue the certificate using SHA-256 or a stronger supported algorithm.Self-signed certificate trust.A self-signed certificate is rejected unless explicitly chosen to trust it. FortiToken Mobile offers Allow once and Always allow when it encounters a self-signed certificate.Trusting a self-signed certificate does not resolve an address mismatch. The certificate must still contain the correct hostname or IP address in its SAN. Otherwise, the retry fails with a hostname mismatch error.Certificate verification checklist.The hostname or IP address configured in FortiToken Mobile matches one of the entries in the certificate SAN, unless the SAN verification exception applies.The notBefore and notAfter dates cover the current date.The signature algorithm is SHA-256 or stronger.Any self-signed certificate is explicitly trusted, where applicable.Retest.After correcting the certificate:Restart the service on FortiAuthenticator or FortiGate.Retry push approval on the mobile device.Retry adding a token, where applicable.Confirm that the certificate error no longer appears.Reinstalling FortiToken Mobile or reactivating tokens is not required after the server certificate has been corrected.Expected outcome.When the server presents a valid certificate that matches the address used by FortiToken Mobile, is within its validity period, and meets the required signature algorithm standard, the affected connections succeed. If the error persists, recheck the SAN entries, the certificate validity dates, the signature algorithm, and the exact address used by the app.

topics.title: Procedure to stop configuration synchronization from primary to secondary FortiGate in HA cluster
topics.summary: DescriptionThe article explains the steps to follow in order to stop configuration synchronization from the primary to the secondary FortiGate in an HA cluster with an active-passive setup.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionIn the event where Primary and secondary FortiGates are exhibiting the same mismatch behavior for example an object is stuck on memory cache of the configuration and FortiGate is unable to remove/delete the entry and after attempting to troubleshoot (checksum recalculate, reboot etc) it did not help to solve the issue and at this point the HA cluster should be isolated and then the configratuon file should be reuploaded on each unit individually but with minimal production impact and most importantly when the secondary is brought back to the cluster the primary should not synchronize its faulty database to the secondary.Example:The secondary is isolated, correction steps are done, and configuration is uploaded. Now the primary FortiGate needs to undergo the same but with minimal production impact, and in order to achieve this, follow the steps below.Steps:On both the primary and secondary FortiGates, enter the command below:config system ha set group-name "fggg" set mode a-p set hbdev "port8" 0 set sync-config disable set override enable endThe 'sync-config' parameter should be set to disable; this will stop the configuration being pushed to the secondary.The 'override' should be enabled on the Primary and secondary to avoid HA re-election.Once the above is done, the secondary FortiGate can be joined to the cluster, and after performing all the checks, a manual failover can be performed to elect the Secondary as the new Primary FortiGate.Once the primary is elected, the former Primary can be isolated from HA to restore the configuration.Now, revert back the configuration (sync-config) to enable it as below:config system ha set sync-config enable set override enable endBring back the former primary to the cluster and wait for HA to be synchronized.

topics.title: FortiGate Power outage: The DNS resolution does not work
topics.summary: DescriptionUsers cannot access servers using hostnames following a FortiGate power failure and reboot, although access via IP address remains functional.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms:After a FortiGate power failure and subsequent reboot, users experience the following issues:Unable to access servers using hostnames.Servers remain accessible when using the IP address directly.The environment uses SD-WAN. Cause:The issue is typically caused by a failure in DNS resolution or the loss of DNS cache/settings following an unexpected power cycle, preventing the translation of hostnames to IP addresses. Solution:Verify and restore DNS functionality on the FortiGate to ensure hostnames resolve correctly.Verify that the FortiGate can resolve external and internal hostnames using the command line interface. This can be checked using the following:show system dns execute ping www.fortinet.com execute ping In case the first step does not work, perform a packet capture and check the query-response from the DNS server.diagnose sniffer packet any "port 53" 4 O lIf DNS over TLS (DOT) is configured, use:diagnose sniffer packet any "tcp port 853" 4 0 lCheck the DNS server configuration to ensure the correct DNS servers are assigned and reachable from FortiGate.If the DNS settings are incorrect, update them using the document Important DNS CLI commands.Clear the DNS cache to remove any stale or corrupted entries resulting from the power failure.diagnose test application dnsproxy 1 diagnose test application dnsproxy 14 diagnose test application dnsproxy 7 diagnose test application dnsproxy 1 ----> Clear DNS cache.diagnose test application dnsproxy 14 ----> Clear hostname cache.diagnose test application dnsproxy 7 ----> Dump DNS cache.Verify that the DNS service is responding by testing resolution from a client machine using the nslookup command.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Local In policy does not work, allow VPN traffic to establish
topics.summary: DescriptionA local-in policy configured to restrict IPsec VPN access to authorized IP addresses may fail to block unauthorized traffic if an existing IKE cache entry forces session creation.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms.A local-in policy is configured to allow IKE traffic only from specific authorized IP addresses. Initially, the policy correctly drops traffic from unauthorized IPs. However, after some time, unauthorized IPs can successfully establish a VPN tunnel because the traffic is no longer evaluated against the local-in policy, as it matches an existing session. Root cause.The IKE cache of the VPN forces the FortiGate to create a session for the incoming traffic. When a session already exists in the session table or is cached, the device may bypass the local-in policy evaluation for subsequent packets of that flow, allowing the tunnel to establish despite the restriction policy. Resolution.To resolve this issue and ensure the local-in policy is strictly enforced, clear the existing VPN tunnels and the session list to remove the cached entries.Flush the IPsec tunnels to clear the IKE cache.Clear the session table to remove any active sessions associated with the unauthorized IP addresses.Run the following commands in the CLI to clear the sessions and tunnels. Execute the clear with filter to clear a specific VPN tunnel.diagnose vpn ike gateway cleardiagnose sys session clear

topics.title: IKEv1 dial-up XAuth fails after ‘peer has not completed XAUTH exchange’ when no user group is defined in the tunnel or firewall policy
topics.summary: DescriptionIKEv1 dial-up (FortiClient) IPsec VPN using XAuth fails to authenticate users when the Phase 1 XAuth user group is set to ‘Inherit from policy’, and no user group is referenced in the firewall policy. It also shows how to fix it.On its own, the debug message peer has not completed XAUTH exchange is not an error. FortiGate logs it right after sending the XAUTH request to the client, and it also appears on successful connections. The actual failure is the message XAUTH failed for user " ", retry(N), which appears without any FNBAM authentication lookup.ScopeFortiOS version 7.x (validated on v7.6.7), IKEv1 dial-up VPN (Main or Aggressive mode) with XAuth type ‘Auto server’ and user group set to ‘Inherit from policy’.SolutionSymptom: Phase 1 (PSK) authentication succeeds, but the user is rejected during XAuth, even with correct credentials. FortiClient retries and then deletes the ISAKMP SA.Debug commands:diagnose vpn ike log filter rem-addr4 diagnose debug application ike -1 diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug enableFailure output:ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1:5: PSK authentication succeeded ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0:5: initiating XAUTH. ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0:5: sending XAUTH request ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0:5: peer has not completed XAUTH exchange ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0:5: received XAUTH_USER_NAME 'aluno' length 5 ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0:5: received XAUTH_USER_PASSWORD length 8 ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0: XAUTH user "aluno" ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0: XAUTH failed for user "aluno", retry(2). ... ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0: XAUTH failed for user "aluno", retry(1). ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0:5: recv ISAKMP SA deleteCause: When the XAuth user group is set to ‘Inherit from policy’ (no authusrgrp configured), FortiGate builds the list of allowed user groups from the firewall policies whose incoming interface is the dial-up tunnel. If none of those policies reference a user group, FortiGate has no group to check the user against. XAuth then fails immediately, without sending an authentication request to the FNBAM daemon (no XAUTH pending line).Fix: Use one of the following options.Option 1: Add the user group as a source in the firewall policy whose incoming interface is the tunnel.config firewall policy edit set srcintf "VPN-IKEV1" set dstintf "virtual-wan-link" set srcaddr "IPSEC-VPN-RANGE" set dstaddr "all" set groups "Alunos_Tshoot" set action accept set schedule "always" set service "ALL" set nat enable next endIn the GUI: Policy & Objects -> Firewall Policy -> Edit the policy > Source > Add the user group.Option 2: Set the user group directly in Phase 1.config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "VPN-IKEV1" set xauthtype auto set authusrgrp "Alunos_Tshoot" next endIn the GUI: VPN -> VPN Tunnels -> Edit the tunnel -> Authentication -> XAuth -> User group: ‘Specify’.Expected output after the fix:ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0:6: peer has not completed XAUTH exchange ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0: XAUTH user "aluno" ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0: XAUTH 78245830721538 pending ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0:6: XAUTH 78245830721538 result FNBAM_SUCCESS ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0: user 'aluno' authenticated group 'Alunos_Tshoot' 2 ike V=root:0:VPN-IKEV1_0: tunnel up event assigned address 10.212.134.200Verification:diagnose vpn ike gateway list name VPN-IKEV1_0 xauth-user: aluno groups: Alunos_Tshoot 2 assigned IPv4 address: 10.212.134.200/255.255.255.255Note: If no firewall policy references the dial-up tunnel interface at all, the connection fails earlier, in Phase 1, with: VPN-IKEV1: ignoring IKE request, no policy configured.

topics.title: Factory Reset Commands Restricted to built-in super_admin in FortiOS 7.6.5 and later
topics.summary: DescriptionWhy administrators assigned to a custom access profile cannot execute factory reset commands, even when all permission groups are configured with read-write access.ScopeFortiGate, FortiOS 7.6.5 and later.SolutionStarting with FortiOS 7.6.5 and 8.0.0, FortiOS restricts certain sensitive CLI operations to the built-in super_admin profile, and this restriction applies to both local administrators and remote administrators authenticated through TACACS+, RADIUS, or LDAP. FortiOS 7.4 and earlier do not include this restriction. The following commands require the built-in super_admin profile:execute factoryreset execute factoryreset2 execute factoryreset-for-central-management execute factoryreset-shutdown execute restore vmlicense diagnose forticare direct-registration To verify the behaviour, follow the procedure described below: Verify the FortiOS VersionRun the following command to confirm the firmware version and build:get system status Verify the Administrator PermissionsLog in using the affected administrator account and check the list of available commands by entering the following command. The factoryreset series of commands will not be listed:execute ? Attempting to run the command by manually typing it will return an error, whereas other permitted execute commands will continue to function normally:Command fail. Return code -61 Additional Information:These commands can modify critical device settings, restore licensing, change registration information, or reset the device configuration. As a result, custom administrator profiles cannot execute these commands regardless of their assigned permissions. To perform a factory reset or execute any of the restricted commands, log in using an administrator account assigned to the built-in super_admin profile. This can be the default admin account or a dedicated super_admin account with appropriate security controls, such as two-factor authentication and trusted hosts. Note: There is no custom access-profile permission that can override this restriction. The behavior is intentional and is not a firmware defect. Additionally, automation scripts and provisioning workflows that use the following commands must execute under an account assigned to the built-in super_admin profile.

topics.title: Technical Guide: Understanding the FortiGate NP7 packet flow & drop types for troubleshooting packet loss issues
topics.summary: Description This article describes the packet flow in NP7-based FortiGate platforms and the several available drop counters tracked with NP7 diagnostics, which can be used to trace the flow and troubleshoot packet drop issues with hardware acceleration enabled (enabled by default). Also, additional in-depth NP7 troubleshooting commands, common issues, and solutions are discussed. Scope FortiGates with NP7 network processors. Solution Table of Contents: Introduction NP7 Packet Flow NP7 DCE drop counters Further Troubleshooting NPU packet sniffers NPU performance monitors Packet Buffer Allocator (PBA) Health check NPU IPSec offload failures NPU session statistics NPU Host Interface statistics Additional NP7-related CLI outputs Common issues and troubleshooting tips Related documents Introduction: The Network Processor Units (NPUs) in FortiGates assist with hardware acceleration of traffic when a session is offloaded from the CPU (Kernel) to the NPU upon session creation. There have been several generations of NPUs, and the current FortiGate models utilize NP7, NP7Lite, NP6, NP6XLite, and NP6Lite. The F & G series FortiGates have the NP7 network processors, for example the 400F, 401F, 600F, 601F, 2600F, 2601F, 900G, 901G, etc: FortiGate NP7 architectures. To troubleshoot packet loss issues, an understanding of the packet flow through various components of the NP7 FortiGate platform would be needed, based on which corresponding diagnostic commands to trace the issue can be run. This article discusses the NP7 packet flow, as well as the various drop types available via diagnostic commands for the components and their interactions in the platform. NP7 Packet Flow: Before starting with troubleshooting any packet loss issues, it is important to understand the packet flow through the system (& the network) to trace the flow through the various components of a FortiGate, with corresponding diagnostic commands, and then narrow down the possible reasons for the drops (if any). A packet flow on the NP7 platform varies depending on whether the packet entering a physical port is part of an existing session or is part of a new session. Packet flows for these two scenarios are discussed below at a high level, between various components of a 4201F platform as an example, but should be similar for other NP7 platforms as well. The reference architecture used for the above packet flow illustrations is here: FortiGate 4201F architecture. Here is a typical packet flow on an NP7 platform, along with the diagnostic commands that can be used to trace the path and drops (if any), as the packet is traversing the various modules and sub-modules in the platform. Note that the exact packet flow would further depend on the traffic type and configurations on the device, and might differ from the steps illustrated below - but the explanation should generally apply for the most common scenarios. While the focus of this guide is to explain the various packet hand-off states in an NP7 platform and the specific troubleshooting commands to use to trace the drops, a high-level end-to-end packet flowchart is also available here for reference: Packet flow: NP6 and NP6lite sessions, and applies to NP7 as well. Step 1. A packet enters the ISF module (Integrated Switch Fabric) through one of the physical ports of the FortiGate. The ISF does basic packet buffering and flow control. Port statistics can be retrieved using below CLI commands. Review especially the 'rx' counters, which correspond to packets ingressing the ISF module of the FortiGate. Repeat these CLI commands multiple times and look for 'Switch Error Counters' increments like CRC, over, under, collision, etc., in the deviceinfo nic command to check for drops in the ISF. FortiGate# diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic port1 FortiGate# fnsysctl ifconfig port1 FortiGate# fnsysctl cat /proc/net/bcm/stats Step 2. ISF then distributes the packets to NP7 modules using a 5-tuple hash over the CGMAC interfaces, as illustrated in the diagram. In a 4201F FortiGate platform, ISF connects to the NP7 modules over 2x 100G interface modules referred to as CGMAC (0 & 1). Review the 'rx' packet counters and drop counters over these CGMAC interfaces with the CLI commands below, which correspond to the packets entering the NP7 modules. FortiGate# diagnose npu np7 cgmac-stats 0 v Step 3. Packet next enters the EIF pipelines (Ethernet Interface pipelines) of NP7, from where they are distributed to the other sub-components of the corresponding NP7 module for processing. Use the below CLI commands to check for drops in EIF pipelines. FortiGate# diagnose npu np7 dce-eif-drop 0 v Step 4. The packet is now processed in the various sub-modules of NP7, depending on the packet's protocols and attributes. topics.title: Technical Tip: Whitelist IP addresses and URLs using firewall policies
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to create a rule to whitelist or bypass traffic that is required to not be inspected, namely by using an object group to easily populate the list in the GUI.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionGo to Policy & Object -> Addresses: Choose the tab 'Address Group': Create new objects: one for IP addresses and one for URLs: Go to Policy & Object -> Firewall Policy: Create a new policy, and choose the LAN interface as a source, and set the destination to the WAN or SD-WAN interface: Choose the newly added object groups as the Source: Since the traffic will be forwarded to the Internet, enable Network Address Translation (NAT). To 'whitelist' or bypass the traffic the Security Profiles must be deactivated, and 'no-inspection' for 'SSL Inspection: In the logging section, for monitoring purposes, the option to be chosen is "All sessions", since 'Security Events' will only log Security (UTM) events (e.g. AV, IPS, firewall web filter) that are currently disabled. Once the traffic is confirmed to be matching the policy, the logging can be disabled. Save the new policy.It is necessary to move the firewall policy to the top to avoid matching all the other firewall policies: Now that the firewall policy is in place, edit the object group to add the IP addresses or URLs: In the section 'Select Entries', choose the option to add a new object, then choose address: For URLs, change the type to 'FQDN' and input the URL desired. Adding a wildcard is supported, but it is recommended to make sure that the DNS settings are properly set in order to populate the DNS resolutions to the FQDN objects properly. For IP addresses, choose the type 'Subnet'. This type supports subnets and specific IP addresses. To add a specific range of IP addresses, use the type 'IP Range'. Observe the new address object, added to the whitelist object group: Save the configuration once all of the object addresses are added, and confirm the configuration by hovering the mouse over the whitelist objects: Relevant notes:Additional IP addresses or FQDNs can be added later by editing the Address Group under Policy & Objects -> Addresses.The firewall policy does not need to be modified when new members are added to the existing Address Group.For FQDN address objects, FortiGate must be able to resolve the configured FQDN to the corresponding IP addresses.Wildcard FQDN objects operate differently from standard FQDN objects. Standard FQDN objects are resolved directly by FortiGate, while wildcard FQDN entries are populated based on matching DNS traffic observed by FortiGate.Confirm that the traffic matches the intended firewall policy.On FortiOS 7.4 and later, the 'Policy Match' feature can be used from the firewall policy page to identify the policy that matches specific traffic parameters.The source interface, source address, destination address, protocol, and destination port used for the lookup should represent the actual traffic being tested.Policy Match identifies the firewall policy that would match the specified traffic. It does not generate traffic or confirm destination reachability.Related articles:Technical Tip: Firewall policy lookupsTechnical Tip: Using a wildcard FQDNTechnical Tip: How to disable SSL InspectionTechnical Tip: FQDN based firewall policies are not working intermittentlyTechnical Tip: Using Internet Service Database vs FQDN Address Objects in FortiGate Firewall Policy
