topics.title: High memory usage in the IKE daemon with dial-up IKEv2 VPN in FortiOS 7.6.8
topics.summary: DescriptionIn FortiOS 7.6, the Internet Key Exchange daemon (iked) can exhibit continuous monotonic resident memory growth under dial-up IKEv2 VPN deployments using dynamic EAP authentication with certificate validation. Although dial-up users disconnect normally during non-business hours, resident memory occupied by the iked process does not decrease. Over multiple days of operation, memory usage can climb to several hundred megabytes, eventually consuming a significant percentage of system RAM and potentially contributing to memory conserve mode.This symptom occurs specifically in environments running pure IKEv2 where dynamic dial-up tunnels handle frequent user connection setups, re-authentications, and Phase 2 Security Association (SA) rekeys. Internal daemon metrics reveal an accumulation of certificate structures (cfg.cert), cryptographic memory allocations (crypto.mem), and message buffers (vmbuf) that remain allocated in the daemon heap.ScopeFortiGate, FortiOS 7.6.8.SolutionWhen dial-up clients establish IKEv2 sessions using EAP and certificate authentication, the iked daemon dynamically allocates memory structures to validate certificates, store peer identifiers, negotiate child security associations, and track connection state.In FortiOS 7.6.8, certain de-allocation paths during session termination fail to decrement reference counts on certificate structures and cryptographic context blocks. As a result, even when active user sessions terminate and the number of connected tunnels drops, the allocated memory is retained within the daemon heap rather than returned to the operating system. Over time, high volumes of dynamic user logins, disconnections, and automatic Phase 2 SA re-keys cause steady memory accumulation.Diagnostic steps:To confirm whether your FortiGate is experiencing this specific condition, perform the following diagnostic checks from the CLI:Identify iked resident memory consumption:diagnose sys top-mem 20Review the output to locate /bin/iked. Note the process ID and resident memory value in kilobytes. In standard stable operations, iked resident memory typically remains around 80 MB (approximately 1% on an 8 GB system). If iked ranks as the top memory consumer and continuously grows over multiple days without releasing memory, proceed to inspect internal counters.Inspect internal IKE daemon allocation counters:diagnose vpn ike countsExamine the following specific counters:cfg.cert: Displays the number of active certificate objects referenced by the daemon. If this counter displays tens of thousands or over one hundred thousand entries on a device configured with only a few static certificates, certificate references are not being freed upon session termination.crypto.mem: Displays the total allocated versus freed cryptographic memory allocations. A large disparity indicating millions of unfreed allocations points to crypto context retention.vmbuf: Displays the number of active virtual memory message buffers in the daemon heap.Verify established tunnel and gateway counts:diagnose vpn ike status diagnose vpn ike gateway listCompare active established connections with total historical connections created. If active connections decrease while iked resident memory continues to rise, memory retention is occurring across disconnected sessions.Automated workaround configuration:While the engineering team analyzes the defect, you can mitigate memory accumulation without rebooting the FortiGate by restarting the iked daemon. Restarting iked terminates active VPN tunnels and resets daemon resident memory to its baseline level (approximately 80 MB).To avoid user disruption during production hours, configure a native FortiOS Automation Stitch to execute the restart command during off-peak weekend maintenance windows:config system automation-trigger edit "Weekend_Iked_Restart_Sun" set trigger-type scheduled set trigger-frequency weekly set trigger-weekday sunday set trigger-hour 3 set trigger-minute 0 next end config system automation-action edit "Iked_Restart_Action" set action-type cli-script set script "fnsysctl killall iked" set accprofile "super_admin" next end config system automation-stitch edit "Weekend_Iked_Restart" set trigger "Weekend_Iked_Restart_Sun" config actions edit 1 set action "Iked_Restart_Action" next end next end endNote: This example automation stitch runs weekly on Sunday at 03:00 AM using the "super_admin" profile to execute "fnsysctl killall iked" (which can also be run manually in the CLI for an immediate reset). Adjust the schedule as needed, and configure it under "config global" on multi-VDOM devices or directly in system settings on single-VDOM devices.Verification:Check the automation stitch configuration:show system automation-stitch Weekend_Iked_RestartFollowing the scheduled execution, verify that iked resident memory has returned to baseline:diagnose sys top-mem 20Verify that internal daemon structure counters have reset:diagnose vpn ike counts

topics.title: SD-WAN IPv6 health-check failure after dynamic DHCPv6 prefix change (lnkmtd errno 99)
topics.summary: DescriptionOn a FortiGate configured with an SD-WAN IPv6 Performance SLA using automatic source selection (set source6 ::), the health-check may fail permanently (100% packet loss) after the WAN interface acquires a new IPv6 prefix via DHCPv6.While manual ICMPv6 pings from the CLI succeed and regular IPv6 traffic forwards normally over the new address, the link-monitor daemon (lnkmtd) continues attempting to bind probe sockets to the old, removed IPv6 address. This causes a local socket bind failure with Linux kernel errno 99 (EADDRNOTAVAIL), preventing health-check probes from being sent out the interface.ScopeFortiGate, SDWAN, DHCPv6.SolutionWhen an SD-WAN IPv6 health-check is set to automatic source selection (set source6 ::), lnkmtd binds an ICMPv6 raw socket to the interface's primary global IPv6 address.When an upstream ISP router or modem reboots and allocates a new IPv6 prefix via DHCPv6, the FortiGate updates the interface IP. However, lnkmtd does not dynamically update its cached socket binding upon receiving the address change. The daemon retains the previous address in its monitor structure and attempts to bind subsequent probe sockets to that address.Because the old address no longer exists on the interface, the kernel rejects the socket creation with "errno 99" (Cannot assign requested address). As a result, no ICMPv6 probes leave the FortiGate.To identify this condition, enable link-monitor debugging on the FortiGate CLI:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug application link-monitor -1 diagnose debug enableWhen the issue is present, the console outputs:lnkmtd::lnkmt_addr_mode_bind6(72): ---> lnkmtd: fails to bind source IP (2001:db8:1::2) to intf(wan), errno(99) lnkmtd::ping_create_socket(468): ---> Fail to create ping socket for monitor(Google_DNS_IPv6-2-VIRTUAL_WAN_LINK-2), peer(2001:4860:4860::8888), errno = 99In this output, "2001:db8:1::2" is the obsolete IPv6 address previously assigned to the WAN interface.To turn off debugging:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug resetWorkaround:Toggling the health-check (set probe-packets disable/enable) does not release the stale socket. Use one of the following methods to restore monitoring:Method 1: Restart lnkmtd (Recommended).fnsysctl killall lnkmtdThe daemon restarts in seconds, detects the current DHCPv6 interface address, binds new sockets, and restores the health-check immediately without dropping active traffic sessions.Method 2: Re-bind source address via CLI.Temporarily define the new source address explicitly in the health-check, then return it to automatic:config system sdwan config health-check edit " " set source6 next end endAfter the health-check recovers, unset the parameter:config system sdwan config health-check edit " " unset source6 next end endTo verify that the health-check link state returns to alive:diagnose sys sdwan health-check status

topics.title: Missing FortiSASE dynamic ZTNA tag IPs on FortiGate SPA Hub
topics.summary: DescriptionOn a FortiGate configured with a FortiClient EMS connector using Share all FortiClients (share-all: enabled), such as an on-premises Secure Private Access (SPA) Hub terminating tunnels from FortiSASE, remote user IP addresses may intermittently disappear from dynamic firewall address objects (diagnose firewall dynamic list).Although the remote FortiClient endpoint remains connected, compliant, and correctly tagged on FortiClient EMS, the FortiGate removes the client's VPN IP from the dynamic ZTNA address table. As a result, firewall policies referencing the dynamic posture tag silently deny access to internal resources until the user disconnects and reconnects with a different IP address, or until the FortiClient NAC daemon (fcnacd) is restarted.ScopeFortiGate, FortiOS 7.6, FortiClient EMS, FortiSASE.SolutionWhen FortiClient EMS is configured with Share all FortiClients enabled, the FortiGate receives endpoint records globally without interface bindings (VDOM -1 in shared memory). The FortiGate link and endpoint control daemon (fcnacd) stores these records in internal shared memory (ec-shm) and populates the dynamic address object tables used by the firewall.In environments where dynamic VPN IP addresses are frequently reassigned, such as remote users connecting through FortiSASE Secure Internet Access (SIA) PoPs, a new user can receive a VPN IP recently released by another endpoint. In FortiOS 7.6.8 and earlier, fcnacd does not track reverse IP-to-UID ownership for share-all endpoints. When a delayed offline or disconnect event from the previous IP leaseholder arrives, fcnacd processes the deletion and removes the IP mapping from the dynamic firewall address table, inadvertently evicting the active compliant user.To verify whether an IP address is missing from the dynamic table:Check the dynamic address list:diagnose firewall dynamic listLocate the EMS dynamic tag object (for example, EMS1_ZTNA_Corporate_Tag). Check whether the active client VPN IP (for example, 100.64.1.12) is absent from the resolved IP list while physical IPs or MAC addresses remain visible.Inspect the shared memory endpoint table:diagnose endpoint ec-shm listReview the records for the missing IP. When this issue occurs, multiple endpoint records (UIDs) may share the same IP address, or the record indicates Share-all: enabled with VDOM (-1) while the dynamic firewall address table omitted the active IP.Capture daemon synchronization activity:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug application fcnacd -1 diagnose debug enableIf the FortiGate receives the endpoint IP in the ipblock update from FortiClient EMS (fcems_addr_update_in_cmdb) but does not populate the IP in the dynamic list, the address mapping has been suppressed by the stale ownership record.To disable debugging:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug resetWorkaround:To restore missing IP mappings without rebooting the FortiGate or interrupting user traffic, restart the FortiClient NAC daemon:fnsysctl killall fcnacdRestarting fcnacd flushes the internal endpoint shared memory cache (ec-shm) and triggers an immediate resynchronization with FortiClient EMS. The daemon re-evaluates all active compliant endpoints and restores all missing IP addresses to the dynamic address table within seconds.Verify that compliant endpoint IP addresses have repopulated:diagnose firewall dynamic listNote: This behavior is resolved in FortiOS 8.0.3 and FortiOS 7.6.9. On earlier releases in environments with high IP churn, an Automation Stitch executing "fnsysctl killall fcnacd" on a periodic schedule (such as daily off-peak) can be used to prevent stale cache entries until the firmware is upgraded.

topics.title: FortiToken Mobile activation emails are not generated or sent when the username is 36 characters or longer
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiToken Mobile activation emails are not generated or sent when the username is 36 characters or longerScopeFortiOS version 7.4.8/7.6.4 and above.SolutionSymptomsWhen a user has a username consisting of 36 characters or more, the following behavior occurs during FortiToken Mobile activation:The token status changes to "provisioning" when the "Send Activation Code" action is used or when a token is assigned.No activation email is generated or sent to the user.Packet captures on TCP port 25/465 show that no SMTP/SMTPS session is attempted to the mail server.No relevant error is logged by the alertmail daemon, but a GUI error might appear.Activation emails are sent normally for users with usernames of 35 characters or fewer, as the following debug output shows.FGT # show user local config user local edit "userlongwithalmost35characters1234" send mail 2026-11-09 11:16:50 connecting to 208.91.114.151 port 465 2026-11-09 11:16:50 send mail 0xb6fb3d0 session 0xb700510 2026-11-09 11:16:50 session_io_event: creating ssl structure for session 0xb700510 2026-11-09 11:16:50 create_ssl: 0x7f981c6000 2026-11-09 11:16:51 sessionn 0xb700510, SSL connected 2026-11-09 11:16:52 session: 0xb700510, rsp_state: greeting, code: 220 2026-11-09 11:16:52 session: 0xb700510, rsp_state: ehlo, code: 250 2026-11-09 11:16:52 session: 0xb700510, rsp_state: mail, code: 250 2026-11-09 11:16:52 session: 0xb700510, rsp_state: rcpt, code: 250 2026-11-09 11:16:52 session: 0xb700510, rsp_state: data, code: 354 2026-11-09 11:16:53 session: 0xb700510, rsp_state: data2, code: 250 2026-11-09 11:16:53 session: 0xb700510, rsp_state: quit, code: 221 2026-11-09 11:16:53 session finined 2026-11-09 11:16:53 _session_on_destroy 2026-11-09 11:16:53 Root cause:A software limitation exists in FortiOS where usernames exceeding 35 characters prevent the system from triggering the activation email process.Resolution:There is currently no workaround for this limitation. Ensure the username is 35 characters or fewer for the activation email to be sent.Fortinet Research and Development is working to increase this limit in future releases.

topics.title: DHCP relay failure in FortiOS 7.4.4 due to DHCP option 54 behavior change
topics.summary: DescriptionDHCP relay requests fail to reach the DHCP server in FortiOS 7.4.4 due to a change in relay behavior regarding Option 54.ScopeFortiNAC, FortiGate.SolutionSymptomsDHCP clients are unable to obtain an IP address. Packet captures show that the DHCP server sends a DHCPOFFER and the client responds with a DHCPREQUEST, but the DHCPREQUEST packet never reaches the DHCP server. Root causeStarting from FortiOS 7.4.4, the DHCP relay behavior changed. In versions prior to 7.4.4, the relay forwarded requests to all configured DHCP servers. In FortiOS 7.4.4 and later, the relay forwards requests only to the server IP address specified in the DHCP Server Identifier (Option 54). If Option 54 contains an incorrect IP address, the relay drops the packet with the error "can't find a matching server in the relay".For example, the packet capture shows the DHCP relay forwarding the DHCPDISCOVER packet to the DHCP server at 172.20.200.3. However, the DHCP server responds with 172.20.200.2 in the DHCP Server Identifier (Option 54).Since the IP address in Option 54 does not match the configured DHCP relay server address, the FortiGate drops the subsequent DHCPREQUEST packet instead of forwarding it to the DHCP server.ResolutionEnable the dhcp-relay-request-all-server setting on all interfaces that relay DHCP requests. This forces the FortiGate to forward requests to all configured DHCP servers regardless of the Option 54 value.Connect to the FortiGate CLI.Run the following commands to enable the relay for all servers on the affected interface:config system interface edit set dhcp-relay-request-all-server enable next end

topics.title: Missing wifi-certificate causes "daemon /bin/eap_proxy" to restart every 2 seconds
topics.summary: DescriptionIn rare conditions, the global FortiOS wifi-certificate and wifi-ca-certificate parameters may have no referenced certificate after upgrade, causing the eap_proxy daemon to continuously restart. This affects IKEv2 and Wi-Fi user authentication.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionIf user authentication flows aren't working as expected after upgrade or during initial feature configuration, check the crashlog for eap_proxy restarts as part of troubleshooting:diagnose debug crashlog read 16382: 2026-11-18 10:18:24 the killed daemon is /bin/eap_proxy: status=0x0 16383: 2026-11-18 10:18:26 the killed daemon is /bin/eap_proxy: status=0x0 16384: 2026-11-18 10:18:28 the killed daemon is /bin/eap_proxy: status=0x0If eap_proxy is restarting frequently, check the current global configuration.Expected (healthy) output:FortiGate # show full system global | grep wifi- set wifi-ca-certificate "Fortinet_Wifi_CA" set wifi-certificate "Fortinet_Wifi" FortiGate # If either parameter shows a blank string, this represents an issue: eap_proxy will be unable to start correctly with this configuration.FortiGate # show full system global | grep wifi- set wifi-ca-certificate '' set wifi-certificate '' FortiGate # If needed, the eap_proxy failing to start can be seen in eap_proxy debug output:diagnose debug application eap_proxy -1 diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug enable ELOOP: remaining socket: sock=7 eloop_data=(nil) user_data=(nil) handler=0x5555e40478 ELOOP: remaining socket: sock=8 eloop_data=(nil) user_data=(nil) handler=0x5555e3dc70 ELOOP: remaining socket: sock=9 eloop_data=(nil) user_data=(nil) handler=0x5555e40a38 ELOOP: remaining socket: sock=5 eloop_data=(nil) user_data=(nil) handler=0x5555e3ed88 2026-11-18 10:17:21 1795018641.698405: 2026-11-18 10:17:21 TLS: Trusted root certificate(s) loaded 2026-11-18 10:17:21 1795018641.699823: 2026-11-18 10:17:21 OpenSSL: tls_global_client_cert - Failed to load client certificate error:80000002:system library::No such file or directory ... 2026-11-18 10:17:21 1795018641.716719: 2026-11-18 10:17:21 lo: Unable to setup interface. Signal 17 received - terminatingNote: eap_proxy can fail to start for other reasons, with similar entries in the crashlog. For an example, see Technical Tip: EAP_Proxy consuming high CPU after upgrade to FortiOS v7.2.5 or v7.4.0.ResolutionIf the Wi-Fi certificate configuration has an issue, revert to default Wi-Fi certificate configuration as follows.config system global unset wifi-ca-certificate unset wifi-certificate endAlternatively, manually set the intended certificates. For example:config system global set wifi-ca-certificate "Fortinet_Wifi_CA" set wifi-certificate "Fortinet_Wifi" endIf Wi-Fi certificate configuration loss after upgrade is reproducible, consider opening a Fortinet support ticket as outlined in How to create a ticket for Fortinet TAC, as this would likely represent an unknown new issue.

topics.title: Input not as expected error when enabling Log application health metrics on Firewall policy
topics.summary: DescriptionEnabling the Log application health metrics feature on a firewall policy via the GUI may result in an "Input not as expected" error due to a failure to automatically disable NPU offloading.ScopeFortiOS 8.0.0.SolutionWhen attempting to enable the "Log application health metrics" feature on a firewall policy through the graphical user interface (GUI), the system returns an "Input not as expected" error and fails to save the policy.The "Log application health metrics" feature requires NPU offloading to be disabled for the specific firewall policy. While configuring this feature via the command line interface (CLI) automatically disables NPU offloading, the GUI does not perform this action automatically, leading to a validation error. To resolve this issue, manually disable NPU offloading for the firewall policy using the CLI before enabling the health metrics feature on GUI, or configure the entire setting via the CLI:Run the following commands to disable NPU offloading for the affected policy:config firewall policy edit set auto-asic-offload disable next endAfter disabling the offload, enable the "Log application health metrics" in the GUI or continue via the CLI:config firewall policy edit set passive-wan-health-measurement enable next endThis is known GUI issue 1277938, which is resolved in FortiOS 8.0.1. See FortiOS 8.0.1 Resolved issues.For more information on this feature, refer to Graphical display for application performance monitoring analytics.

topics.title: Troubleshooting FortiAP Deployment Failures in FortiEdge Cloud – Maximum Paid-Tier Device Limit Reached
topics.summary: DescriptionThe troubleshooting steps to identify and resolve Access Point (AP) deployment failures in FortiEdge Cloud.ScopeFortiEdge Cloud.FortiAP.Solution Verify that the Access Point has a valid FortiManagement Cloud license and that it falls within the Freemium limit in FortiEdge Cloud.Perform Access Point Deployment in the Alternate Domain [Global (Canada)]:In certain scenarios, Access Point deployment issues in the Europe domain can be resolved by temporarily deploying the Access Point in the Global (Canada) domain and then moving it back to Europe.If you are currently using the Europe domain, switch to the Canada domain.Navigate to Devices -> Inventory Devices -> FortiAP -> Click Asset Sync.Locate and select the affected Access Point -> Click Deploy -> choose the network -> Click OK.Verify whether the Access Point is successfully deployed.Undeploy the Access Point from the Global (Canada) domain:Navigate to Networks and choose the Network to which the Access Point was deployed. This will open the selected network's portal.Navigate to Wireless > Access Points -> select the deployed Access Point -> Click Actions -> Undeploy.This process will remove the Access Point from the Canada domain and make it available for deployment in the Europe domain.Redeploy the Access Point in the Europe Domain::After successfully undeploying the Access Point from the Canada domain, switch back to the Europe domain and initiate the deployment process.Log in to the FortiEdge Cloud Europe domain.Navigate to Devices -> Inventory Devices -> FortiAP -> Click Asset Sync to synchronize the Access Point inventory.Locate and select the affected Access Point -> Click Deploy and assign the Access Point to the required network.Once the deployment process is completed, verify whether the Access Point is successfully onboarded and visible under the intended network.Contact Fortinet Support if the Issue Persists:If the Access Point still fails to deploy after following all the troubleshooting steps, raise a support ticket with Fortinet Technical Support for further investigation by sharing the following details:Access Point Serial Number, Target Domain (Europe, Canada, or Global) where the Access Point needs to be deployed, and the Cloud Account Email ID: the email address associated with the FortiEdge Cloud account.

topics.title: ICMP error traffic matching an existing HTTPS firewall policy with VIP
topics.summary: DescriptionWhy FortiGate may match an ICMP error packet against an existing HTTPS session established through a Virtual IP (VIP), even when the corresponding firewall policy permits only HTTP and HTTPS servicesScopeFortiGate.SolutionConsider the following topology, where an external client accesses an internal web server through a VIP configured on FortiGate.VIP configuration:In this example, two port-forwarding VIPs are configured on FortiGate to translate incoming HTTP and HTTPS traffic destined for 10.20.9.248 to the internal web server at 10.20.17.66.config firewall vip edit "Web-Server-VIP-HTTPS" set extip 10.20.9.248 set mappedip "10.20.17.66" set extintf "any" set portforward enable set extport 443 set mappedport 443 next edit "Web-Server-VIP-HTTP" set extip 10.20.9.248 set mappedip "10.20.17.66" set extintf "any" set portforward enable set extport 80 set mappedport 80 next endFirewall policy configuration:The configured VIPs are referenced as destination address objects in firewall Policy ID 51, which permits HTTP and HTTPS traffic from external clients to the internal web server.config firewall policy edit 51 set name "Inbound-Web-Access" set srcintf "wan1" set dstintf "port2" set action accept set srcaddr "Allowed-Clients" set dstaddr "Web-Server-VIP-HTTPS" "Web-Server-VIP-HTTP" set schedule "always" set service "HTTPS" "HTTP" set utm-status enable set inspection-mode proxy set ssl-ssh-profile "certificate-inspection" set av-profile "default" set ips-sensor "default" set logtraffic all next endAlthough ICMP is not explicitly configured as an allowed service, the following fields are observed in the traffic logs:result="accept (0B/0B)" policyid=51 proto=1 service=HTTPSICMP error messages contain the original IP header and a portion of the transport-layer header of the packet that triggered the error.FortiGate can use this embedded information to identify an existing session and process the ICMP error in the context of that session and its associated firewall policy.Packet capture analysis:The following packet capture illustrates an ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) message received by FortiGate, advertising a next-hop MTU of 1480 bytes.Observe the following fields within the ICMP packet:Outer destination IP: 10.20.9.248 (VIP). Embedded source IP: 10.20.9.248 (VIP). Embedded destination IP: 103.113.105.169 (client). Embedded TCP source port: 443. Embedded TCP destination port: 62679.The embedded IP and TCP headers correspond to the return direction of the HTTPS session established through the VIP.FortiGate can associate the ICMP error with the existing HTTPS session and apply the corresponding NAT translation.In the outbound packet capture, observe that the outer destination IP and the embedded source IP have been translated from the VIP address (10.20.9.248) to the mapped server address (10.20.17.66).The following table illustrates the observed packet translation:Packet fieldIncoming packetOutgoing packetOuter source IP103.113.105.16910.20.9.248Outer destination IP10.20.9.24810.20.17.66ICMP Type/Code3/43/4Next-hop MTU14801480Embedded source IP10.20.9.24810.20.17.66Embedded destination IP103.113.105.169103.113.105.169This explains why the traffic logs may display the following combination:proto=1: The outer packet is ICMP.service=HTTPS: The recorded service classification corresponds to the HTTPS session context in this example.policyid=51: The firewall policy associated with the original session.Note:It is expected behavior for ICMP error messages associated with a valid existing session. It does not indicate that the HTTPS firewall policy permits arbitrary ICMP traffic. ICMP error messages that cannot be associated with an existing session do not benefit from this implicit session-based handling.

topics.title: FortiGate Policy Type field in Local Traffic log displays raw internal token
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue where the Policy Type field in the Local Traffic log details pane displays an unmapped raw internal string instead of a human-readable label in FortiOS 8.0.1.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionWhen reviewing Local Traffic logs in the Web GUI of FortiGate version 8.0.1, the Log Details side pane displays a raw internal token in the Policy Type field. Instead of a human-readable label, the field shows Firewall::policytype.HTTPS.Steps to reproduce:Select Log & Report -> Local Traffic.Double-click a local traffic log entry to open the Log Details side pane.Scroll down to the Action / Policy section.Observe the Policy Type field displaying Firewall::policytype.HTTPS.This is a cosmetic UI localization bug where the frontend string translation mapping is missing for the Policy Type field in the Local Traffic log details pane.Workaround:This is a cosmetic display issue and does not affect the actual functionality of the device.To identify the policy type, analyze other surrounding log fields such as the policy ID, source IP, and destination IP.Fixed Schedule:The permanent fix will be in firmware versions 7.6.10 and 8.0.4.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Capturing both ingress and egress Traffic on a FortiSwitch port using the unused physical interface on the FortiGate
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen troubleshooting network traffic, it may be necessary to capture packets in both ingress and egress directions on a FortiSwitch port. If a laptop with Wireshark is unavailable, a FortiGate with an unused physical interface can be used as an alternative packet capture destination.ScopeFortiSwitch, FortiGate.SolutionThe following steps describe how to configure this setup.Configure port mirroring on the FortiSwitch.Configure port mirroring on the FortiSwitch to mirror traffic from the port under investigation to a designated destination port using the document Configuring a SPAN mirror. Make sure to configure the lldp-profile on the destination port to 'default'.For example:config switch mirror edit "1" set dst port5 set src-egress port2 set src-ingress port2 set status active end config switch physical-port edit port5 set lldp-profile default endConnect the FortiSwitch to the FortiGate.Connect the FortiSwitch mirror destination port to an unused physical interface on the FortiGate.Before proceeding, ensure that:The FortiGate interface is not part of any firewall policies.The interface is not assigned to a software switch, hardware switch, or other interface configuration that could interfere with packet capture.The FortiGate interface should be dedicated to receiving mirrored traffic.Start the packet capture on the FortiGate.Access the FortiGate CLI and execute the following command to capture packets arriving on the interface connected to the FortiSwitch mirror destination port:diagnose sniffer packet "" 6 0 aReplace with the name of the FortiGate physical interface connected to the FortiSwitch mirror destination port.Analyze the captured traffic.Once the sniffer is running, the FortiGate CLI displays the mirrored packets received from the FortiSwitch.The capture includes both ingress and egress traffic from the monitored FortiSwitch port, provided that both directions are enabled in the port-mirroring configuration.This approach allows packet-level troubleshooting without requiring a separate laptop or Wireshark installation.

topics.title: FortiSIEM version 7.6.1 upgrade fails with 'The operation would result in removing the following protected packages: kernel-core'
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue where the FortiSIEM version 7.6.1 upgrade fails during the yum update stage due to the protected kernel-core package and provides the steps required to resolve the issue.ScopeFortiSIEM supervisor, worker, and collectors.SolutionSymptoms.During the upgrade of FortiSIEM to version 7.6.1, the process fails during the yum update stage. The upgrade logs show the following error:upgrade : UPGRADE | yum update ...| localhost | FAILED | 2.34s - stdout: Last metadata expiration check: 0:00:19 ago on Tue 17 Nov 2026 11:12:35 AM IST. (try to add '--skip-broken' to skip uninstallable packages or '--nobest' to use not only best candidate packages) - rc: 1 - stderr: Error: Problem: The operation would result in removing the following protected packages: kernel-core Root cause.The upgrade fails because the package manager attempts to remove or modify the kernel-core package during dependency resolution. Since kernel-core is a protected package, the yum update operation cannot complete, and the FortiSIEM upgrade process is terminated.Resolution.Update the operating system kernel and reboot the FortiSIEM Supervisor before retrying the FortiSIEM version 7.6.1 upgrade.Take a VM snapshot of the FortiSIEM node to ensure a recovery point exists.Update the kernel package by running:yum update kernel -yReboot the FortiSIEM node.Verify that all FortiSIEM services are operational and that the GUI is accessible.Retry the upgrade to FortiSIEM version 7.6.1.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: 'fatal: Unauthorized user. exiting' in the SSH debug
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the 'Unauthorized user' error observed when accessing a FortiGate through SSH. It explains how to troubleshoot the error by verifying the administrator credentials and trusted-host configuration, and provides steps to allow SSH access from the required source IP address.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionWhen attempting to access the FortiGate through SSH, the following messages may be observed in the SSH debug:SSH: userauth-request for user prov service ssh-connection method none SSH: attempt 0 failures 0 SSH: input_userauth_request() calling GetPwNam return UNAUTH. Exiting SSH: fatal: Unauthorized user. exiting.The SSH key exchange has completed successfully before the error occurs:SSH: KEX doneThis indicates that the SSH connection is established and the failure occurs during the user authentication stage.Verify that the username being used for the SSH connection is correct and that the password is valid.If the administrator uses remote authentication such as RADIUS, LDAP, or TACACS+, verify the corresponding remote-authentication configuration as well.Check the administrator trusted-host configuration.FortiGate allows admin access to be restricted to specific trusted IP addresses or subnets. When trusted hosts are configured for an administrator, the administrator can log in only from the configured trusted hosts. This restriction applies to SSH and other administrative access methods.From the CLI, check the administrator configuration:show system adminAlternatively:config system admin edit show next endLook for the trusthost entries, for example:set trusthost1 10.0.1.1 255.255.255.255The trusthost parameter specifies the IPv4 address or subnet from which the administrator can connect to the FortiGate.From the GUI, navigate to: System -> Administrators.Edit the affected administrator account and check the Restrict login to trusted hosts configuration. Add the IP address or subnet the administrator connects from, if required.Add the source IP address to the trusted hosts.If the SSH connection originates from 10.0.1.1 and trusted hosts are configured, add the source IP to the administrator's trusted hosts.For example:config system admin edit set trusthost1 10.0.1.1 255.255.255.255 next endAfter applying the configuration, retry the SSH connection.If the source is a subnet rather than a single host, configure the appropriate subnet and netmask.If the administrator account is not intended to be restricted to specific source IP addresses, review the trusted-host configuration and remove any unintended restrictions.Do not add individual IP addresses unnecessarily if unrestricted administrative access is intended.Understanding the SSH debug.The following message may also appear:SSH: This ip 10.0.1.1 is not blockedThis message should not be interpreted as confirmation that 10.0.1.1 is an authorised trusted host.It indicates that the IP address was not blocked at that stage of the SSH connection. The subsequent authentication processing can still fail with:SSH: fatal: Unauthorized user. exiting.Therefore, both messages can appear in the same debug output.Example:In the reported case, the following messages were observed:SSH: This ip 10.0.1.1 is not blockedFollowed by:SSH: userauth-request for user prov service ssh-connection method none SSH: input_userauth_request() calling GetPwNam return UNAUTH. Exiting SSH: fatal: Unauthorized user. exiting.The SSH key exchange completed successfully, but the authentication of the administrator was not successful.The source IP address 10.0.1.1 was not included in the trusted-host configuration of the affected administrator account. After adding 10.0.1.1 as a trusted host, SSH access was successful.Related documents:Best practicesconfig system adminAdministrator account options

topics.title: FortiOS object UUID is a creation TIMESTAMP! How to decode them

Identify when any policy or object was created!Policies and objects with a uuid field (show firewall policy , show firewall address and so on) record when that FortiGate created them. The first three groups of the UUID follow the RFC 4122 time-based (version 1) layout, which holds a 60-bit timestamp. The version digit reads 5, but the timestamp fields decode the same way. I’ve checked decoded values against objects with known creation times, and they match to the minute.LayoutGroup Holds 1 (8 hex) Low 32 bits of the time 2 (4 hex) Middle 16 bits of the time 3 (4 hex) Version digit, then the top 12 bits of the time 4 and 5 Clock sequence and node; not time The reassembled value is a count of 100 ns intervals since 1582-10-15 00:00 UTC.Example: 333dc400-f240-51f0-8000-000000000000Drop the first digit of group 3: 51f0 becomes 1f0. topics.title: FortiProxy HA split-brain after sequential upgrade on VMware
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiProxy VM clusters using unicast heartbeat may experience a split-brain scenario where both units become primary after a sequential firmware upgrade to version 7.6.ScopeFortiProxy.SolutionSymptomsDuring or after a sequential firmware upgrade to FortiProxy 7.6, the following symptoms may occur in an Active-Passive High Availability (HA) cluster on VMware using unicast heartbeat:The secondary unit reports "System upgrade failed" in the console after rebooting.Both the primary and secondary units assume the primary role simultaneously (split-brain).The primary unit reports the peer as lost.The secondary unit reports the primary unit is lost.Intermittent blocking of web traffic occurs due to incomplete FortiGuard registration or connectivity issues. Root causeThis behavior is caused by bug ID 1323217. In FortiProxy 7.6, when a cluster member is rebooted, the secondary unit stops answering ARP requests on the heartbeat link. Because the primary unit cannot resolve the secondary unit via ARP, it reports the peer as lost and promotes itself to primary, while the secondary unit also assumes the primary role. Resolution WorkaroundsIf the split-brain occurs, use one of the following workarounds:Reboot the secondary unit. This forces the unit to broadcast a Gratuitous ARP (GARP) upon boot, which allows the primary unit to resolve the secondary unit and restore the HA state.Manually add a static ARP entry on the primary unit for the secondary unit's heartbeat interface:diagnose ip arp add Note: The diagnose ip arp add command creates a runtime entry that is lost after a reboot. To make the ARP entry persistent, configure it under config system arp-table. Preventative measuresTo avoid this issue, consider the following options:Upgrade Firmware: Install FortiProxy 7.6.8 or later, which contains the fix (recorded against build 1675).Change Heartbeat Mode: Use multicast heartbeat instead of unicast. On VMware, ensure that promiscuous mode and MAC address changes are enabled on the heartbeat port group and the data interface. Multicast design does not rely on the ARP resolution that triggers this bug.

topics.title: The FortiManagement Cloud Web GUI provides an incorrect configuration revision file for download
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue where, when attempting to download a specific older configuration revision from the FortiManagement Cloud Web GUI, the downloaded file contains a newer firmware version and configuration than the one selected. ScopeFortiManagement Cloud, FortiGate. SolutionA bug in the FortiManagement Cloud Web GUI causes a mismatch between the selected configuration revision and the actual file delivered for download. This behavior may occur when the firmware version information displayed in the configuration revision history is not synchronized with the actual backup file, particularly after a firmware upgrade.To retrieve the correct configuration file, select an earlier configuration revision and verify whether the downloaded file contains the expected configuration.A fix for this issue is planned for an upcoming FortiManager Cloud release.

topics.title: FortiAP clients missing from FortiGate GUI and wireless runtime reporting after HA role change
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter a FortiGate High Availability (HA) role change, managed FortiAPs can remain online while their wireless clients stop appearing in the FortiGate GUI, even though the clients remain authenticated and continue passing traffic.This article describes how to confirm the condition and restore wireless client reporting.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.x and FortiAP 7.6.x.SolutionSymptoms:FortiAPs remain up in CWAS_RUN in the diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c wtp output, but only FortiAPs that rejoined after the role change report their clients.diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c ws shows VAPs with BSSID 00:00:00:00:00:00 and state N/A. Some VAPs also report a configuration failure.A client is authenticated on the FortiAP with active traffic counters, and the FortiGate session table shows sessions in both directions. However, diagnose wireless-controller wlac -d sta returns no entry for the client.The FortiGate GUI client monitor does not list the client.Example output:401F-HA-2 (vdom1) # diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c ws -------------------------------WTP SESSION 1---------------------------- WTP session : 9-10.100.100.3:5246 MP07 CWAS_RUN,7087 11,12 Ctrl in_ifIdx : 88/fap-lan indev : 0/ Data in_ifIdx : 88/fap-lan indev : 0/ mesh uplink : ethernet id : PU431FTH20027288 mgmt_vlanid : 0 wtp_wanlan_mode : wan-only refcnt : 10 deleted : no plain_ctl : disabled wtp-mode : normal wtp-report-index : 1 data-chan-sec : clear-text ctl-msg-offload : ac=0bff/wtp_loc=0bff/wtp_rem=03ff/oper=03ff session_id : 5f4bed54114567f910ea290e324e5c46 ehapd cfg : ongoing message queue : 0/128 max 0 tId_10_sec : 2573 Ekahau : disabled Aeroscout : disabled FortiPresence : disabled wpad_sockname : /tmp/capwap/cwHapdSocket_3 BLE-RTLS : disabled Radio 1 : AP wlan cfg : SOL_Open vap-01(1) : SOL_Open 00:00:00:00:00:00 lsw lbr SOL_Open Config failed State N/A(11) Age 7087 Radio 2 : AP wlan cfg : br2 tun-1 SOL_Open vap-01(1) : br2 00:00:00:00:00:00 lsw fortinet.br2 Config failed State N/A(11) Age 7087 Radio 3 : Monitor Radio 4 : Virtual Lan AP wlan cfg : Radio 5 : Not ExistRoot cause:The wireless controller runtime state, including the VAP table and wireless client table, is not fully rebuilt on the new primary after an HA role change when multiple client daemons are configured (acd-process-count greater than 1 under config wireless-controller global).The CAPWAP control plane remains operational, allowing FortiAPs to continue serving clients and forwarding traffic. However, the controller retains stale client information.Only FortiAPs that subsequently rejoin the controller repopulate their entries, allowing their clients to be reported correctly.Resolution:The reported issue will be fixed in the upcoming FortiOS 7.6.10 GA release.Workaround:Restore wireless client reporting using one of the following methods.Note: These operations restart the affected FortiAPs or the wireless controller daemon and may temporarily interrupt wireless connectivity. Perform them during a maintenance window.Reset the affected FortiAPs.Reset the affected FortiAP to force it to rejoin the controller and repopulate its client information.To reset a specific FortiAP, run the following:execute wireless-controller reset-wtp To reset all managed FortiAPs:execute wireless-controller reset-wtp allTo limit the impact, reset a specific FortiAP group instead:execute wireless-controller reset-wtp Note:The all option restarts every managed FortiAP and disconnects all wireless clients.If a newer FortiAP firmware image is available on the FortiGate and image download is enabled, the FortiAP downloads and installs it when rejoining the controller.Configure a single client daemon.When multiple client daemons are configured, the wireless client information may not be synchronized across all daemons.Set acd-process-count to 0 as a mitigation:config wireless-controller global set acd-process-count 0 endVerify the accepted values for the running FortiOS release before applying the configuration:get wireless-controller globalRestart the wireless controller daemon.Restart the wireless controller daemon to refresh its operational state:execute wireless-controller restart-acdVerification:After applying the workaround, run the following commands to verify wireless client reporting and VAP status.Verify connected wireless clients:diagnose wireless-controller wlac -d staTo check a specific client:diagnose wireless-controller wlac -d sta Verify the combined client database:When multiple client daemons are configured, use the following command to retrieve the combined client information:diagnose wireless-controller wlac -p data -d staTo inspect individual daemons, replace data with the daemon index:diagnose wireless-controller wlac -p 0 -d sta diagnose wireless-controller wlac -p 1 -d sta0: Parent daemon1: First child daemonVerify VAP status:Confirm that the VAPs have valid BSSIDs and are in the running state:diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c wsExpected result:Wireless clients are list

topics.title: FortiGate option is greyed out for object conflicts during policy import
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes why the FortiGate option is greyed out when resolving object conflicts during policy import into FortiManager and how to resolve the issue.ScopeFortiManager.SolutionWhen Importing policies and objects from managed devices, FortiManager allows object conflicts to be resolved by selecting either the FortiGate or FortiManager version of an object.If the object is a global object present in FortiManager Global Database, the FortiGate option is greyed out, and FortiManager is selected by default. This is expected because global objects can only be edited in the Global ADOM.In environments where the Global ADOM is not used, this behavior can also occur if an object was mistakenly promoted to the Global ADOM and subsequently deleted from it. The local ADOM may continue to treat the object as a global object (identified by the Globe icon beside the object name), preventing selection of the FortiGate option during import conflict resolution.Objects should not be promoted to the Global ADOM in environments where global object management is not used.To resolve this condition for an affected local object:Clone or recreate the affected object using a temporary name.Replace all references to the original object in policies and object groups with the cloned object. Refer to: Find and replace objects.Delete the original object after all references have been replaced.Rename the cloned object to match the original object name. If the object already exists on FortiGate, this preserves the matching name.Retry the policy import and verify that the FortiGate option is available when resolving the object conflict.

topics.title: How to consolidate multiple Policy Packages and newly added FortiGate policies into a Single Policy Package
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to consolidate policies from multiple policy packages into one shared policy package while retaining device-specific policies.ScopeFortiManager.SolutionA shared policy package can contain common policies for all installation targets and additional policies restricted to selected devices/VDOMs.Before proceeding, back up the configurations, verify firmware and ADOM compatibility, and review interface mappings and referenced objects. This workflow assumes the devices and packages are within the same ADOM.Scenario 1: Consolidating existing policy packages.Select or create the destination policy package.Compare policies in the source packages. Retain one copy of equivalent common policies and separate policies for differing requirements.Copy the required policies into the destination package and review their order.Add the relevant devices/VDOMs to the destination package’s Installation Targets.Configure Install On for each policy:Installation Targets: Applies the policy to all package targets.Selected devices/VDOMs: Applies the policy only to those targets selected.Review the installation preview for each device, install, and verify the resulting policies and traffic.Example:Four FortiGates use two policy packages. Both packages contain a common DNS policy, but each also contains a different policy that must be retained.Source packageInstallation targetsPoliciesPKG_AFGT1 and FGT2Common-DNS and Allow-HTTPSPKG_BFGT3 and FGT4Common-DNS and Allow-NTPThe objective is to create one shared package without extending HTTPS or NTP access to devices that do not require it.Copy the policies into the destination package.Clone PKG_A and name it PKG_Main; this gives the starting point with PKG_A policies already in the new package.From PKG_B, copy Allow-NTP and paste it into PKG_Main. Do not copy Common-DNS again after confirming that the two DNS policies are equivalent.Configure the installation scope.Add all four FortiGates to the Installation Targets of PKG_Main.Enable Column Settings -> Install On and configure:PolicyInstall OnCommon-DNSInstallation TargetsAllow-HTTPSFGT1 and FGT2Allow-NTPFGT3 and FGT4Select the Install On value for each restricted policy, select the required devices/VDOMs, and select OK.Preview and verify.Use the shared policy package PKG_Main and install it on all devices. Review the installation preview for each device. The expected result is:DevicePoliciesFGT1 and FGT2Common-DNS and Allow-HTTPSFGT3 and FGT4Common-DNS and Allow-NTPScenario 2: Adding a new FortiGate and consolidating its policies into the shared package.Add the FortiGate to the appropriate ADOM through Device Manager -> Devices & Groups -> Add Device.Import its existing policies into a separate package for review. Refer to this document: Importing policies and objects from managed devices.Resolve object conflicts carefully and compare imported policies with the shared package. Refer to this document: What to do when an object conflict occurs.Copy additional policies into the shared package. Retain existing common policies where their settings are equivalent.Verify interface/object mappings and add the new device/VDOM to the shared package’s installation targets.Restrict device-specific policies using Install On.Review the installation preview for the new device, install, and verify.Notes:Make sure to check the Normalized interfaces and add appropriate mapping. Refer to this document: Configuring normalized interface per-device mapping rules.Matching policy names or IDs do not establish equivalence. Compare the complete policy settings.Install On controls installation scope; it does not automatically merge packages or preserve local policies.Retrieving a configuration does not automatically merge policies into the shared package.Verify IPsec tunnels, routes, and other device-level dependencies separately.Policies with Install On set to 'Installation Targets' will apply to all devices. Review their scope before installation.After validation, confirm device associations with the shared package and delete unused packages.Related documents:Editing policiesInstalling policies to specific devicesInstalling a policy package

topics.title: DNS Database Configuration Lost After Upgrading to FortiOS 8.0.1
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue where DNS database configurations are lost after upgrading a FortiGate from FortiOS 8.0.0 to FortiOS 8.0.1.The issue occurs when DNS database entries have names starting with a period ( . ). These entries may fail to load during the upgrade process, resulting in the DNS database configuration being removed.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionAfter upgrading to FortiOS 8.0.1, the DNS database configuration under config system dns-database is missing.The configuration error log displays the following error:>>> "edit" ".fortinet.me" @ root.system.dns-database:failed command (error -2004)Attempting to configure a DNS database entry with a name starting with a period also produces the following error:LAB_FGT (dns-database) # edit ".fortinet.me" Table name '.fortinet.me' contains illegal character! Command fail. Return code -2004The issue appears to be related to DNS database entry names beginning with a period ( . ).In FortiOS 8.0.0, DNS database entries with names starting with a period are accepted. However, in FortiOS 8.0.1, these names are rejected during configuration parsing.As a result, when the FortiGate processes the existing configuration during the upgrade, the affected DNS database entries fail to load and are omitted from the running configuration.SolutionWorkaround:Before upgrading to FortiOS 8.0.1, review the existing DNS database configuration and rename any entries whose names begin with a period ( . ).Before upgrading, verify the existing DNS database configuration:show system dns-databaseIdentify DNS database entries with names starting with a period.For example:config system dns-database edit ".fortinet.me"Rename the affected DNS database entries to names that do not begin with a period.For example:config system dns-database edit "fortinet.me"Ensure that the corresponding DNS database settings and DNS entries are retained.Verify the updated configuration:show system dns-databaseOnce the configuration has been updated and verified, proceed with the FortiOS upgrade.After upgrading, verify that all DNS database entries are present:show system dns-databaseNote: Always back up the FortiGate configuration before performing a firmware upgrade.

topics.title: FortiManager unable to push device-level configuration to HA FortiGate VM in public cloud
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiManager cannot push certain device-level configuration changes, including VLAN and system interface configurations, to FortiGate VMs deployed as an HA cluster in public cloud environments. As a result, FortiManager may be unable to generate an install preview or install these configuration changes.ScopeFortiManager.FortiGate VM deployed in HA mode on the following public cloud platforms:Amazon Web Services (AWS).Microsoft Azure (AZ).Google Cloud Platform (GCP).SolutionWhen FortiManager manages a FortiGate HA cluster in a public cloud environment, it cannot install certain device-level configuration changes.Examples include the following configuration areas:config system ha config system interface config system sdn-connector nic config system sdn-connector route-tableAlthough the FortiManager Administration Guide explicitly references AWS and Azure, the same limitation applies to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) deployments.Because these configuration objects are device-specific, FortiManager cannot push them to HA FortiGate virtual machines in public cloud environments.Workaround.To modify VLANs, interfaces, or other affected device-level settings:Make the required configuration changes directly on each FortiGate cluster member using either the GUI or CLI.Verify the cluster members are in sync:get system ha status diagnose sys ha dump-by vclusterBoth members must show the same configuration before proceeding.After the changes have been applied successfully, retrieve the configuration from the FortiGate devices into FortiManager.Verify that the FortiManager Device Database is synchronized with the FortiGate configuration.Retrieving the configuration ensures that FortiManager reflects the running configuration on the managed devices and prevents database mismatches.Verifying FortiManager virtual machine resources.If FortiManager exhibits unexpected behavior during install previews, configuration retrievals, or installation operations, verify that the FortiManager virtual machine meets the minimum system requirements.When additional virtual disk space has been added, run the following commands:execute lvm extend diagnose sys fsck harddiskIf the FortiManager virtual machine was previously undersized, expand the virtual disk from the cloud or hypervisor platform before running these commands.Additional information:Although the FortiManager Administration Guide explicitly references AWS and Azure, the same limitation is also applicable to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) deployments.Related documents:Minimum system requirementsManaging FortiGate HA clustersFortiManager and FortiAnalyzer-VM platform disk issuesExtending disk space in FortiAnalyzer-VM/FortiManager-VM

topics.title: Technical Tip: How to block mDNS traffic with Firewall Policies for specific subnet/user group
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to block mDNS traffic with firewall policies for a specific subnet or SSID user profile. This is useful when users still want to allow mDNS at a global level but only want to block mDNS for some specific subnet/user profile when it generates lots of traffic. Scope FortiGate. Solution Many devices and services use multicast IPs; hence, FortiGate has default multicast addresses configured. mDNS uses multicast IP 224.0.0.251, which is configured in the FortiGate as a multicast address. To allow mDNS traffic globally and yet block for specific user groups or subnets, follow the method below. Create a Firewall policy using the multicast IP address as the destination and define the source subnet and user group. Select service as port 5353. Add a rule to deny any service with Destination IP 224.0.0.251 for IPv4 mDNS. Add another rule to deny any service with Destination IP ff02::fb for IPv6 mDNS. Creating a custom service in the CLI console. config firewall service custom edit "mDNS" set tcp-portrange 5353 next end GUI output: Firewall Policy in CLI console: config firewall policy edit 1 set name "mDNS_block" set srcintf "port2" set dstintf "port1" set srcaddr "AP_User_Range" set dstaddr "mDNS_multicast_address" set schedule "always" set service "mDNS" set logtraffic all set groups "Wifi_guest" next end Firewall policy in GUI:

topics.title: Technical Tip: How to block AnyDesk and TeamViewer using Application Control signatures
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to block remote access applications using application control. Scope FortiGate. Solution Enable Application Control: Go to Security Profiles -> Application Control. Select 'CREATE NEW' to create an application control profile. Name the profile. To Block AnyDesk and TeamViewer in the Application Control profile: Under 'Application and Filter Overrides'. Select 'CREATE NEW'. Search for 'AnyDesk' and 'Team' in the application signature database. Set the 'Action' to 'Block'. Save the changes. Apply the Application Control Profile to a Policy: Go to Policy & Objects -> IPv4 Policy. Identify the policy handling outgoing internet traffic. Edit the policy and: Select the Inspection mode 'Proxy-based'. Enable 'Application Control'. Select the created application control profile. Enable 'SSL/SSH Inspection' and select a profile configured for **Deep Inspection**. Install the Deep Inspection certificate on the client. Save the policy. Monitor Traffic: Go to Log & Report -> Security Events -> Logs -> Application Control to verify that application traffic is detected and blocked. Note: The latest AnyDesk application version 9.x may not be blocked when the firewall is operating in proxy mode using Application Definitions v34.00124. However, it is successfully blocked when flow inspection mode is used. This issue is resolved in Application Definitions v35.00130 and later, where the AnyDesk Application signature has been improved to account for traffic changes in newer versions.

topics.title: FortiToken Mobile 6.5.0.0030 on Android 16 - activation fails because globalftm.fortinet.net certificate chain is no longer trusted
topics.summary: Hi,I am experiencing a FortiToken Mobile activation failure on Android 16 with FortiToken Mobile 6.5.0.0030.The error shown during activation is: "Invalid server certificate - FortiToken Mobile cannot validate the server certificate."I found an older Fortinet Community discussion describing a very similar problem after upgrading to Android 13:FortiToken Mobile cert error on Android 13https://community.fortinet.com/support-forum-92/fortitoken-mobile-cert-error-on-android-13-115185In that thread, the original poster later reported: "Fortinet support said this is bug 765700."Fortinet also documented bug 765700 in the FortiToken Mobile Android 5.2.3 release notes:FTM Android 5.2.3 Known issueshttps://docs.fortinet.com/document/fortitoken/5.2.3/ftm-android-5-2-3-release-notes/999611/known-issuesBug 765700 is described there as: "'Untrusted Certificate' popup throws when activating/completing token transferring or approving/denying Login Requests"Fortinet later listed bug 765700 in the FTM Android 5.3.2 resolved issues:FTM Android 5.3.2 Resolved issueshttps://docs.fortinet.com/document/fortitoken/5.3.2/ftm-android-5-3-2-release-notes/666021/resolved-issuesThe description says that part of the Untrusted Certificate issue was fixed.Interestingly, bug 765700 was still listed as a known issue in FTM Android 5.3.3, specifically mentioning an Untrusted Server Certificate during FortiToken activation:FTM Android 5.3.3 Known issueshttps://docs.fortinet.com/document/fortitoken/5.3.3/ftm-android-5-3-3-release-notes/999611/known-issuesThere is also a Fortinet troubleshooting article for the exact error message:Troubleshooting Tip: Invalid server certificate - FortiToken Mobile cannot validate the server certificatehttps://community.fortinet.com/fortiauthenticator-8/troubleshooting-tip-invalid-server-certificate-fortitoken-mobile-cannot-validate-the-server-certificate-101390My current case is different enough that I cannot confirm whether this is a regression of bug 765700 or a separate issue.The same FortiToken activation code works successfully with FortiToken for Windows. This indicates that the token itself and the Fortinet provisioning service are functional.I investigated the Android failure further.FortiToken Mobile 6.5.0.0030 sends the initial SoftToken.MobileProvisionRequest to: https://globalftm.fortinet.net/SoftToken/Provisioning.asmx/MobileDuring initial provisioning, the application first uses its check_system_certs TLS validation path. If certificate validation fails, the request ends with SSLHandshakeException and the application displays the certificate error dialog.I also checked the application's Android Network Security Configuration. FortiToken Mobile 6.5.0.0030 targets API 35 and trusts several bundled Fortinet certificates plus: It does not include: globalftm.fortinet.net currently presents this certificate chain: globalftm.fortinet.net-> DigiCert SHA2 Extended Validation Server CA-> DigiCert High Assurance EV Root CAThe leaf certificate is currently valid from 8 April 2026 until 23 October 2026.On my Android 16 device, DigiCert High Assurance EV Root CA is no longer present in the active Conscrypt APEX trust store: /apex/com.android.conscrypt/cacertsThe old certificate is still present under: /system/etc/security/cacerts but it is absent from the active APEX CA set.To verify this independently of the FortiToken application, I extracted all 120 certificates from the device's Conscrypt APEX trust store and used them as the only CA bundle with OpenSSL.Validation of globalftm.fortinet.net fails:depth=2 C = US, O = DigiCert Inc, OU = www.digicert.com, CN = DigiCert High Assurance EV Root CAverify error:num=19:self-signed certificate in certificate chainVerification error: self-signed certificate in certificate chainVerify return code: 19 (self-signed certificate in certificate chain)As an A/B test, I used exactly the same Android CA bundle against: ftc.fortinet.com:8688That endpoint validates successfully:depth=2 C = US, O = DigiCert Inc, OU = www.digicert.com, CN = DigiCert Global Root G2depth=1 C = US, O = DigiCert Inc, CN = DigiCert Global G2 TLS RSA SHA256 2020 CA1Verification: OKVerify return code: 0 (ok)This strongly suggests that the problem is specifically related to the certificate hierarchy currently used by globalftm.fortinet.net.Another relevant observation is that changing FortiToken Mobile's "Allow connection to an unverified server" setting does not solve initial token activation.From the application flow, this option is used by other operations such as push authentication and token transfer. The initial provisioning flow, however, simply displays the certificate error after the SSLHandshakeException and terminates the activation attempt.Installing the legacy DigiCert root as an Android user CA also does not appear to be a valid workaround because FortiToken Mobile's Network Security Configuration trusts system certificates but does not include user certificates.Could Fortinet please confirm:

topics.title: Technical Tip: EMAC VLAN support with NP offloading
topics.summary: Description This article describes the support of EMAC VLAN with NP offloading. Scope FortiGate. Solution The Media Access Control (MAC) Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) feature in Linux allows configuring multiple virtual interfaces with different MAC addresses (and therefore different IP addresses) on a physical interface. FortiGate implements an enhanced MAC VLAN consisting of a MAC VLAN with bridge functionality. Refer to the following document for more information on the EMAC VLAN functionality of FortiGate: Enhanced MAC VLANs The following points should be considered before configuring EMAC VLAN in the environment: NP6 only partially supports EMAC VLAN offloading. For example, traffic between EMAC VLANS (where the emac-vlan is not assigned a VLAN ID) is not offloaded. NP6 offload is disabled for IPsec over pure EMAC VLANs (where the emac-vlan is not assigned a VLAN ID), see notes. For cases that have issues with EMAC VLAN when offloading is enabled, apply the following workaround/fix for the issue: It is possible to disable NPU offloading on the policy and/or IPSec phase 1 using an EMAC VLAN interface: config firewall policy edit set auto-asic-offload disable end config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit set npu-offload disable end NP6xlite behaves the same as NP6, so EMAC VLAN offloading to NPU is only partially supported by the ASICs. The same workaround/fix will work, as mentioned for NP6. Note: Due to some restrictions on offloading EMAC VLAN traffic, newer FortiOS releases (starting v6.2.8, v6.4.9, v7.0.2) will disable the EMAC VLAN traffic offloading to NP6 or NP6xlite (SoC4) for scenarios where it is not supported, which is the case of IPSec. Starting with v7.6.4, EMAC offloading support has been introduced for SOC4 platforms. This enhancement prevents MAC address flapping, ensuring that the same MAC address is retained before and after the offload process. The problem is addressed under issue ID 114861. Resolved issues 7.6.4 Consider using the NP7 platform if offloading traffic over the EMAC VLAN interface is of priority, as NP7 processors are better with EMAC offload. For NP7 and NP7Lite platforms, Site-to-Site IPsec traffic can be offloaded when the tunnel interface is attached to an EMAC-VLAN interface that is attached to an IEEE 802.1Q VLAN interface in a basic topology. In more advanced deployments, such as environments using SD-WAN, VRRP, or VRFs, functional limitations may affect hardware offloading and the Sessions passing through two EMAC-VLAN interfaces are not supported for NP7/NP7Lite offload. Related articles:Technical Tip: NP7/NP7Lite offloading for site-to-site VPN traffic - tunnel interface attached to EMAC-VLAN interface that is attached to IEEE 802.1Q VLAN Interface NP7 fastpath aNP7 fastpath and EMAC VLANs | FortiOS Hardware Acceleration Manual
