topics.title: Technical Tip: How to resolve the issue when EMS upgrade fail due to max index row size exceeded in PostgreSQL
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an EMS migration issue where the max index row size was exceeded in PostgreSQL when upgrading EMS from version 7.4.7 to 7.4.8.ScopeFortiClient EMS.SolutionEMS version 7.4.7 failed to be upgraded to version 7.4.8 due to the max index row size in the PostgreSQL database.Upon checking the EMS migration log, the following error is shown in the log:sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (psycopg2.errors.ProgramLimitExceeded) index row size 3072 exceeds btree version 4 maximum 2704 for index "ix_vuln_details_severity_category_cve_list_reference" DETAIL: Index row references tuple (1609,13) in relation "vuln_details". HINT: Values larger than 1/3 of a buffer page cannot be indexed. Consider a function index of an MD5 hash of the value, or use full text indexing.To resolve this issue, run the following commands one by one in the EMS machine Linux shell:# sudo -i emscli # db # DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_vuln_details_severity_category_cve_list_reference; # CREATE INDEX ix_vuln_details_severity_category_cve_list_reference ON public.vuln_details USING btree (severity, category); # \qAfter the above, perform the migration again. If the upgrade issue still persists, then raise a TAC ticket (Support) and continue troubleshooting with a TAC engineer.

topics.title: Diagnosing TCP packet loss and retransmissions using iperf3, FortiGate sniffer, and Wireshark
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to troubleshoot TCP throughput degradation, identify packet loss, and correlate network performance metrics between iperf3, packet capture from the FortiGate, and Wireshark. Specifically, it it details how TCP sequence numbers can be leveraged to pinpoint packet loss.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionPreparation and recommended Practices:To ensure accurate sequence tracking and protocol decoding in Wireshark without truncation issues, always capture packets using an SSH client like PuTTY.Converting CLI capture to Wireshark file:Run the FortiGate packet sniffer via SSH, ensure logging is enabled, and use the FGT2ETH tool to convert it. See this article for more info: How to import 'diagnose sniffer packet' data to WireShark.Ensuring Capture Integrity (Zero Dropped Packets):When stopping your CLI packet capture (using ^C), always verify that 0 packets were dropped by the kernel. This confirms that your FortiGate successfully captured every single packet without buffer exhaustion during high-speed traffic tests.^C 12336 packets received by filter 0 packets dropped by kernelDisable NPU offload:Disable NPU offload on the matching firewall policy to capture all the traffic. See this article for more info: Technical Tip: FortiGate Disable Hardware Acceleration.config firewall policy edit 2 set name "AllowInternet" set uuid 48410dd6-e04b-51f1-6869-a61baae82f55 set srcintf "port3" set dstintf "port1" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "ALL" set logtraffic all set nat enable set auto-asic-offload disable set np-acceleration disable next endCapturing the handshake:Always start the packet capture before initiating the iperf3 test. Capturing the initial SYN and SYN-ACK packets allows Wireshark to record the Initial Sequence Numbers for both endpoints and accurately compute Relative Sequence and Acknowledgment numbers starting from 0.Set up iperf3 client and server:On the client, install iperf3 and use the command below:$iperf3 -c 192.168.12.2 -t 30On the FortiGate, make the PC connected port iperf3.R2 # diagnose traffictest client-intf port3 client-intf: port3 R2 # diagnose traffictest server-intf port3 server-intf: port3 R2 # diagnose traffictest port 5201 port: 5201 R2 # diagnose traffictest run -sTopology:PC1 --- SW --- FGT1 --- ISP.Analysis:Step 1: Execute a standard TCP throughput test from the client to the server.Retr (Retransmission) tracks the number of TCP segments re-sent due to packet loss, while Cwnd (Congestion Window) measures the amount of unacknowledged data the sender is allowed to have in flight.Step 2: After converting the capture, 'right-click' the interesting traffic and follow the TCP stream.In Wireshark, 'right-click' any interesting packet -> Follow -> TCP Stream.Find the TCP SYN packet, expand the TCP section, and add sequence number, acknowledgement number, relative sequence number, next sequence number, and relative acknowledgement number as a columnsStep 3: Pinpointing packet loss using relative sequence & ack numbers.Follow the TCP stream and look for the following.TCP previous segment not capturedTCP fast retransmissionTCP out-of-orderTCP spurious retransmissionIn this example, packets flow from PC1 (192.168.12.99) to FGT1 (192.168.12.2). So, add another filter (ip.src == 192.168.12.99).Based on packet 208, the next expected relative sequence number is 181038. However, the subsequent packet jumps to 227374, which Wireshark flags as 'TCP Previous segment not captured' to indicate packet loss.Lost Bytes = 227374 - 181038 = 46,336 bytes.At a payload size of 1448 bytes, approximately 32 (46336/1448) TCP segments were dropped.Because the sender did not receive an acknowledgment (ACK) for the data starting at sequence number 181038, the sender eventually retransmitted that missing segment later in the stream (at packet 265). Once that retransmission filled the gap, the receiver could successfully process the out-of-order packets it had already cached up to sequence number 227374.Step 4: Direct connection.PC1 -- FGT1 -- ISP.This confirms that the intermediate switch was dropping the packets.Related articles:How to import 'diagnose sniffer packet' data to WireSharkTroubleshooting Tip: Configure FortiGate as speed test (iPerf) serverTechnical Tip: Analyze TCP sequence numbers through Wireshark

topics.summary: DescriptionAn explanation of the FortiAP connection process and basic troubleshooting with FortiSASE.ScopeFortiAP, FortiSASE.SolutionWith AP connected with FortiSASE, the last one act like FortiAP controllerConnection Flow (4 phases):Discovery = AP discovers the SASE AC by resolving the SASE turbo URL (e.g. turbo-xxxxx.edge.fortisase.com) via DNS, or via FortiZTP provisioning from FortiEdge Cloud, DNS (UDP 53).CAPWAP Control Channel = AP establishes a DTLS-encrypted CAPWAP control channel to the AC, UDP 5246.IPsec Data Tunnel = After control channel is up, an IPsec tunnel is established for the data plane, UDP 4500 (NAT-T).RUN State = Both channels up -> AP enters on "RUN" mode and is managed by FortiSASE.Typical FortiSASE config:AC_DISCOVERY_TYPE:=3 AC_HOSTNAME_1:=turbo-xxxxx.edge.fortisase.com Note: AC discovery type 3 means that AP is going to find controller through DNS, and AC hostname is the URL to resolve.What a connected AP looks like:FortiAP # wcfg | grep fsm -A 10 fsm-state : RUN 197 wtp-ip-addr : *.*.*.*:5246[m] - *.*.*.*:36600 ac-ip-addr : *.*.*.*:5246 - *.*.*.*:5247 FGVM64-v7.4-build2795 DNS LOAD data-chan-sec-cfg : clear-text dtls ipsec-sn ipsec data-chan-sec-oper : ipsec-sn cipher(ctrl) : ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256Note: IP directions are hidden.Troubleshooting:Check AP state mode in the FortiAP CLI:wcfg | grep fsm -A 10Test DNS resolution from the AP:cw_diag debug dns 3Or manually resolve:nslookup turbo-xxxxx.edge.fortisase.comRun a capwap debug on FortiAP:don ton To turn debugging off:doff toff

topics.title: Erroneous email regarding FortiGate Cloud managed devices asking to upgrade to a non-existent version of FortiOS
topics.summary: DescriptionWhy a customer may receive an erroneous email regarding FortiGate Cloud-managed devices asking to upgrade to a non-existent version of FortiOS.ScopeFortiOS managed by FortiGate Cloud.SolutionAs of November 17, FortiGate Cloud has erroneously sent a set of users an email indicating that FortiOS devices managed by FortiGate Cloud are out of date and need to upgrade to a non-existent version of FortiOS:A recent issue was identified that resulted in a small number of customers receiving inaccurate FortiOS upgrade notifications.The issue was traced to a misconfiguration on an internal DNS server, which caused an internal system to reference incorrect firmware upgrade information. Consequently, certain customers received upgrade recommendations that did not align with the intended guidance for their respective environments.Following identification of the issue, Fortinet's Engineering team immediately implemented the following corrective actions:Removed the misconfigured internal DNS server from the production DNS configuration.Refreshed the FortiOS firmware image catalog using the FortiGuard production infrastructure to ensure firmware version accuracy.Identified and contacted all affected customers with correction notices, advising them to disregard the previously issued upgrade recommendations.The issue has been fully resolved, and the corrective measures have been implemented to prevent further inaccurate notifications.

You may need to refresh the current page' error. See this link for more info - FortiGate GUI Issue with error 'Connection to the FortiGate was lost temporarily. You may need to refresh the current page.'.SSH and telnet sessions time out or drop unexpectedly.Ping requests to the FortiGate management IP address drop or show high latency.The system temporarily enters conserve mode, or CPU spikes are observed on the dashboard.Transit traffic may experience latency or packet loss during the burst window.Identification and troubleshooting:To identify the root cause of the traffic burst, data must be gathered during the event or review historical logs immediately after access is restored.Review historical resource usage and crash logsIf the burst causes the system to drop access, review the crash logs to see if processes were killed or if the system entered conserve mode.R2 # diagnose debug crashlog readSearch for any latest crash in the output.Monitor real-time system top (During the Event)If you can maintain or establish an SSH connection during a burst, check which processes are consuming the CPU. topics.title: OSPF adjacency fails on aggregate IPsec tunnels
topics.summary: DescriptionOSPF neighborship drops and fails to reach Full state when using aggregate IPsec tunnels due to incorrect load balancing algorithms.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms:OSPF neighbors fail to establish adjacency or frequently drop the connection. The system logs show the following error messages:H1 # diagnose ip router ospf all enable H1 # diagnose ip router ospf level info H1 # diagnose debug console timestamp enable H1 # diagnose debug enable 2026-11-12 09:44:29 OSPF: NFSM[Local-Agg:172.28.0.14-10.200.2.253]: neighbor addr or tun-id changed 2026-11-12 09:44:29 OSPF: NFSM[Local-Agg:172.28.0.14-10.200.2.253]: Status change Full -> Down 2026-11-12 09:44:29 id=20302 msg="OSPF: %OSPF-5-ADJCHANGE: neighbor Local Agg:172.28.0.14-10.200.2.253 Down " 2026-11-12 09:44:29 OSPF: NFSM[Local-Agg:172.28.0.14-0.0.0.0]: Start 2026-11-12 09:44:29 OSPF: NFSM[Local-Agg:172.28.0.14-10.200.2.253]: Down (HelloReceived) Root cause:The issue occurs when OSPF traffic is distributed across multiple members of an aggregate IPsec tunnel. If the aggregate tunnel algorithm is not set to the load balancing algorithm, OSPF packets may switch between different tunnel members. This causes the receiving FortiGate to detect a change in the neighbor address or tunnel ID, which forces the OSPF neighborship to drop.config system ipsec-aggregate edit "Local-Agg" set member "Tunnel-1" "Tunnel-2" set algorithm L3 next endconfig system ipsec-aggregate edit "Remote-Agg" set member "Tunnel-1" "Tunnel-2" set algorithm Redundant next endIn the configuration above, local-agg tunnel is configured with an L3 algorithm. However, the remote-agg is configured with Redundant algorithm. This causes remote side tunnel to always send the traffic only with Tunnel-1 until its down.Resolution: Ensure that the algorithm for the aggregate IPsec tunnel is set to L3 on both ends of the connection. This ensures that traffic for a specific L3 flow remains on the same tunnel member. Configure the aggregate IPsec tunnel to use the L3 algorithm by running the following commands:config system ipsec-aggregate edit "Remote-Agg" set algorithm L3 next endVerify that the same configuration is applied to the remote FortiGate device.Related articles:IPsec aggregate for redundancy and traffic load-balancingHow to aggregate tunnel interfaces

topics.title: How the FortiGate determines what certificate chain to send for cross-signed certificates, depending on what service said certificate is used for
topics.summary: DescriptionThe behavior of the certificate chain sent by the FortiGate differs based on what daemon is used for that service. This article documents this behavior.ScopeFortiOS.SolutionA cross chained certificate is one in which there are two or more potential certificate paths for it to be trusted. It is possible to import all of the certificates in both chains into the firewall and it will present at least one chain.For this example, assume that "Cert-1" has two different, valid certificate chains. "Cert-1" is signed by "Intermediate-1". There are two different versions of the certificate for "Intermediate-1": one is signed by "Root-1" and the other is signed by "Root-2". All 5 certs are imported into the FortiGate.This is an illustration detailing the two potential certificate paths:Depending on which service "Cert1" is being used for, the behavior for matching the certificate chain will be different. GUI / HTTPS access: "node" (the process handling portions of the GUI on the FortiGate) relies on OpenSSL to build the chain for it. The order in which the CA certs are presented to OpenSSL (if it reads Intermediate1.cer or Intermediate1(Root2 signed).cer first) determine which chain will be sent to the client. This however is non-deterministic and cannot be predicted like the other processes unfortunately. One chain would have to be removed for a specific one to be presented.SSL VPN: This daemon will use the configuration order to determine which certificate chain to use. First it will load the certificates in the CA store, check which one had signed our leaf (server) certificate, and then check for a root for that intermediate certificate. If "Intermediate1.cer" was imported first (appears first in the config), then the "Root1" chain will be presented. (Note: if Root1.cer is missing, and Intermediate1.cer was matched, only Intermediate1.cer will be presented. It will not switch to the other, full chain.)IPsec / other services whom use FNBAMD: Similar situation to GUI / HTTPS access where the presented cert chain is effectively arbitrary (as long as it actually matches). It is whichever cert FNBAMD reads from memory first, so it is not deterministic. To send a specific chain, you have to remove the conflicting one.FGFMD / FortiManager: The chain is specifically set in the configuration, it is not automatic: How to configure intermediate certificates to be used in FGFM protocol.Inbound DPI in Proxy-based mode: WAD is the daemon handling Proxy-based inspection, and this would depend on if you are in multi-VDOM mode or not. If you are in multi-VDOM mode, WAD will check the certificate store in Global first, going from uppercase A-Z, then lowercase a-z. It will then do the same in the VDOM WAD was called from. If you have a single VDOM, it will just be from uppercase A-Z, then lowercase a-z.Inbound DPI in Flow-based mode: Again, a similar situation to GUI / HTTPS access and FNBAMD where the choice is arbitrary and no specific order is defined. As long as both certificates can validate the path, one will be used and there is no deterministic way to know which one. To send a specific chain, remove the conflicting one.

topics.title: After upgrade to FortiOS version 7.4.13, user receives error '400 Bad Request' when using proxy inspection and Deep Packet inspection
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to FortiOS version 7.4.13, a user may start receiving "Error 400: Bad Request" when accessing legitimate sites when the firewall policy is set to use Deep Packet Inspection and proxy-based inspection.ScopeFortiOS version 7.4.13.SolutionFollowing an upgrade to FortiOS version 7.4.13, users may start seeing the Error 400 Bad Request when accessing legitimate sites: This issue is present when the following settings are in place:strict-web-check is set to enable:config web-proxy global set strict-web-check enable endFirewall policy using proxy-mode inspection and a Deep Packet Inspection profile:config firewall policy edit 40 set name "Outbound Internet" ... set inspection-mode proxy set ssl-ssh-profile "custom-deep-inspection" ... next end FortiOS version 7.4.13 introduced a change that enables strict-web-check: Changes in default behavior.The reason the traffic is blocked is that enabling strict-web-check under config web-proxy global caused the proxy mode policy to block HTTP/2 requests that carry more than one Cookie header field. HTTP/2 (per RFC 7540 8.1.2.5) permits the Cookie header to be split into multiple separate header fields, but strict mode rejected such requests as malformed, returning a connection error to the client.With strict web checking enabled, WAD rejects malformed HTTP requests including requests carrying conflicting duplicate Content-Length headers with "400 Bad Request" instead of forwarding them to the origin server. This closes an HTTP request smuggling (CWE-444) desynchronization between WAD and the origin server that was reachable pre-authentication through the web proxy.Enhancements to allow split cookies while strict-web-check is enabled will be implemented in future FortiOS release 7.4.15.Solution:If legitimate web traffic is blocked after upgrade, the previous behavior can be restored with the following configuration option:config web-proxy global set strict-web-check disable endNote: If the FortiGate is managed by a FortiManager that is running versions 7.6.8 or 7.4.12, there is a chance this option may be unset on the next install. To prevent this, follow the "FortiManager may unexpectedly push unset strict-web-check when installing policies to FortiOS 7.4.13" portion of this document: Special Notices.

topics.title: FortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models show high memory consumption on firmware version 7.6 and 8.0
topics.summary: DescriptionThe reasons why FortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models run at high memory on firmware version 7.6 and 8.0.ScopeFortiSwitch models 108F and 1xxE.SolutionAfter upgrading FortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models to v7.6 firmware, the FortiSwitch runs at high memory even immediately after boot up and when no traffic is passing through the switch.get system performance status CPU states: 2% user 6% system 0% nice 92% idle Memory states: 72% useddiagnose sys top-mem pyfcgid (919): 23773kB zebra (924): 5695kB igmpsnoopingd (930): 5095kB newcli (2236): 4742kB cu_swtpd (1202): 3285kB Top-5 memory used: 42590kBFortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models running at high memory after an upgrade to firmware version 7.6 and 8.0 is expected behavior. These models are built with hardware that is limited to 256MB RAM. FortiSwitch OS 7.6's and 8.0's minimum requirement is 512MB RAM. These models will always boot up with high memory usage. The memory usage difference between firmware 7.6, 8.0 and firmware 7.2 or 7.4 is because more features are supported in 7.6 and 8.0, meaning more daemons are running and consume more memory.

topics.title: Information required for a FortiSwitch RMA request
topics.summary: DescriptionThe information and basic troubleshooting steps required when a FortiSwitch becomes completely unresponsive or does not power on. The collected information helps the Technical Support team perform an initial assessment of the issue.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionIf a FortiSwitch is completely unresponsive or does not power on, the Technical Support team may request the following information and troubleshooting results.Issue details:Note when the issue first occurred and for how long the FortiSwitch was on production or working.Note whether there was any power outage, power fluctuation, or power surge before the issue occurred.Note whether there were any new devices connected or configuration changes made to the FortiSwitch before the issue occurred.Hardware information:Provide the following details:FortiSwitch modelSerial numberFortiSwitchOS version (if known)LED and fan status:Connect the power cable and check the status of the LEDs on the FortiSwitch.Check whether the fans start spinning after power is connected. (If applicable based on the model).Record any unusual LED indications or fan behavior.Provide a photo or video showing the FortiSwitch during the power-up process.Test with a different power socket:Connect the FortiSwitch to a different power socket. Note: To verify that the test socket can power another device, preferably another FortiSwitch.Confirm whether the FortiSwitch powers on using the alternate socket.Test with a different power cable:Try a different compatible power cable. Note: To verify that the test cable can power another device, preferably another FortiSwitch.Confirm whether the FortiSwitch powers on using the alternate cable.Verify other devices at the site:Confirm whether other FortiSwitch units or devices at the same site are operating normally. Confirm whether other devices are using the same power source or a different power source.Check the power supply (Applicable if dual power supply is available).If the FortiSwitch has redundant power supplies, check the LED status of each power supply.If it is supported by the model, test each power supply independently.Record any abnormal LED indications.Disconnect external connections:Disconnect all network cables, transceivers and other external connections. Keep only the power cable and serial console connected. Attempt to power on the FortiSwitch. Check whether the LED or fan behavior changes.Collect serial console output:Connect a serial console cable to the affected FortiSwitch. Open a terminal application, such as PuTTY or Tera Term, using the following settings.Serial console settings:ParameterValueSpeed (default)115200Data bits8Stop bits1ParityNoneFlow ControlNoneAttempt to power on the FortiSwitch and check whether any output or error messages appear on the console. Save and share the console output with the Technical Support team, even if only a few lines are displayed.Note:Refer to the following article for instructions on saving a console session log using PuTTY: How to create a log file of a session using PuTTY.Perform a hardware reset: Important note: A hardware reset will restore factory-default settings and erase the existing configuration. It is best to perform this step only after confirming with the Technical Support team.Keep the serial console connected. Follow the model-specific instructions provided by the Technical Support team to perform a hardware reset using the reset button. Observe whether any output appears on the console during or after the reset process.Refer to the following documentation: Using the Reset button on FortiSwitch units.Physical inspection:Check the FortiSwitch chassis, power connectors, and externally accessible ports for visible physical damage.Check for burn marks, unusual smells, or other signs of physical damage.Share photos of any observed damage with the Technical Support team.Do not open the chassis or attempt hardware repairs.Note:All the above information and troubleshooting steps are intended for the initial assessment of a potentially faulty FortiSwitch. Based on the findings, the Technical Support team may request additional information or perform further troubleshooting before proceeding with the RMA evaluation. Refer to: How to create a ticket for Fortinet TACShare the collected information, photos, videos, and console logs with the Technical Support team for further investigation.

topics.title: 25G FortiLink Connection Does Not Establish Between FortiGate 901G and FortiSwitch 2048F
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to establish a 25G FortiLink connection between a FortiGate 901G and a FortiSwitch 2048F by configuring the interface speed, media type, and Forward Error Correction (FEC) settings.ScopeFortiGate 901G, FortiSwitch 2048F.SolutionTopology:Consider the topology shown above, where a FortiGate 901G is connected to a FortiSwitch 2048F using a 25G optical connection.The connection uses the following components:FortiGate: FortiGate 901G, ULL port x5.FortiSwitch: FortiSwitch 2048F, port47.Transceiver: 25G QSFP module (25GBASE-SR).Connection: 25G FortiLink.Symptoms: The 25G FortiLink connection between the FortiGate ULL port and the FortiSwitch port does not establish.Root Cause: The physical link fails to establish because the interface speed, media type, and Forward Error Correction (FEC) settings are not properly aligned between the FortiGate and FortiSwitch interfaces.Resolution: Manually configure the interface speed, media type, and FEC settings on both ends to ensure compatible link parameters.FortiGate configuration.The following example configures FortiGate ULL port x5:config system interface edit "x5" set speed 25000full set mediatype sr set forward-error-correction cl74-fc-fec next endFortiSwitch configuration (standalone CLI).Configure the corresponding FortiSwitch port (port47):config switch physical-port edit "port47" set speed 25000sr set fec-state cl74 next end FortiGate configuration to manage the FortiSwitch port.In a FortiLink deployment, the same FortiSwitch port settings should be pushed from FortiGate using the managed-switch configuration:config switch-controller managed-switch edit "FS2F48TVxxxxxxx8" config ports edit "port47" set speed 25000sr set fec-state cl74 next endNote: The FortiGate managed-switch configuration should be used to apply the settings centrally when the FortiSwitch is managed through FortiLink.After applying the configuration, verify that the physical link is established at 25 Gbps.Reference Documents:Configuring QSFP28 Port Splitting with 4×25G Breakout and Dual LAGs Using QSFP28-to-4×SFP28 DAC CablesMedia type for interfaces that support transceiver modulesConfiguring forward error correctionConfiguring FortiSwitch split ports (phy-mode) in FortiLink mode

topics.title: RADIUS administrative authentication fails after upgrading FortiGate to 7.4.13 due to IPsec synchronization issues
topics.summary: DescriptionAdministrative access via RADIUS authentication fails after upgrading FortiGate to version 7.4.13 due to IPsec tunnel synchronization issues.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManager.SolutionSymptomsAfter upgrading FortiGate, administrators cannot access the device using RADIUS authentication. The RADIUS server is located behind an IPsec VPN tunnel. While the FortiGate sends authentication traffic into the tunnel, the traffic is not received by the RADIUS server. Root causeThe firmware upgrade caused a synchronization issue with the IPsec VPN tunnel encryption keys. The FortiGate maintained multiple encryption keys (both old and new), while the remote peer only recognized the new key. This mismatch prevented traffic from successfully traversing the tunnel to the RADIUS server. ResolutionTo resolve the authentication failure, reset the IPsec VPN connection to synchronize the encryption keys between the FortiGate and the remote peer.Log in to the FortiGate using a local administrator account.Identify the affected IPsec tunnel used for RADIUS communication.Reset the VPN connection to clear stale encryption keys. You can do this via the GUI or the CLI.To reset the tunnel via CLI, run the following command:diagnose vpn tunnel reset After resetting the tunnel, verify that the RADIUS server is reachable and that administrative users can authenticate successfully.

topics.title: False alert warns of virtual-wire-pair removal during policy installation.
topics.summary: DescriptionA cosmetic alert indicates that system virtual-wire-pair configurations will be purged during a policy installation, even when the interfaces are used in active policies.ScopeFortiManager, FortiGate.SolutionWhen pushing firewall policies from FortiManager to a FortiGate, the following alert appears:The following policy types are going to be purged: 'system virtual-wire-pair' This alert occurs even if the virtual wire interfaces are correctly configured and used within the firewall policies. Root causeThis is a visual bug in FortiManager version 7.6.7. The alert is cosmetic and does not result in the actual removal of the virtual wire pair configuration from the FortiGate device. The install preview does not show any purge commands being executed. ResolutionSince this is a cosmetic issue, proceed with the policy push. The virtual wire pair configuration will not be deleted, and traffic will not be disrupted.This issue is resolved in the following versions: FortiManager 7.6.10 FortiManager 8.0.3

topics.title: High CPU usage by ffdb_reinit process on FortiGate FortiOS version 8.0.2
topics.summary: DescriptionHigh CPU utilization issue on the ffdb_reinit daemon on a FortiGate after upgrading to FortiOS version 8.0.2.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionThe FortiGate running FortiOS version 8.0.2 experiences High CPU usage for the ffdb_reinit process on a specific core.diagnose sys top 1 50 3 07:16:30 PM up 2 days, 10 hours and 47 minutes 14U, 11N, 10S, 62I, 0WA, 0HI, 3SI, 0ST; 3614T, 389F ffdb_reinit 27868 R N 90.3 10.4 3To solve the issue, apply the workaround below:Set the internet-service-database to mini to reduce the resource load.config system global set internet-service-database mini endChange the update frequency to weekly to prevent frequent updates.config system autoupdate schedule set status enable set frequency weekly set time 03:00 set day Sunday endTrigger a manual update to download new ISDB definitions into FortiGate.execute update-now diagnose autoupdate versionsAfter applying the changes, check the FortiGate CPU usage. The ffdb_reinit process no longer utilizes high CPU and overall CPU usage will reduce.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Migrate config to a different model FortiGate using FortiManager
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to migrate the config from a FortiGate model to a different model using FortiManager. Scope FortiManager. Solution Migrating config involves 2 parts: device settings (including all the templates) and policy package. Migration of Device Settings. In this article, copy over device-level settings by capturing the configuration in provisioning templates (this applies to System Settings, SDWAN, Static Routes, BGP, and IPSec Tunnels): Device Manager -> Provisioning Templates -> Select the template type -> More -> Import. Note: Another approach to migrate device settings is to use FortiConverter, as discussed in Technical Tip: How to replace FortiGate with a different model in FortiManager. This step will import all IPsec tunnels from the old device and save their configurations as a template. Then select the old device from the drop-down list: Any required changes, such as 'Outgoing Interface', can be applied before assigning the template to the new FortiGate. Same steps apply for other types of templates (i.e., BGP template, SD-WAN template, etc). Notes: Interfaces (VLANs, zones, ...) will not be imported by these templates; the interfaces must be manually created either in Device Manager GUI or via a script that runs against the Device Manager. Check any templates assigned to the old FortiGate that may be needed for the new and assign those. Policy & Objects. The Policy Package of the old FortiGate can be assigned to the new FortiGate by modifying the 'Installation Targets' in the Policy Package. Interfaces used in the Policies are the 'Normalized Interfaces' that need to be mapped to the physical interfaces. Below is an example of a Normalized interface 'Data', it needs to be mapped to the device interface on the new FortiGate via per-device mapping or per-platform mapping. Once all the templates and policy package are ready, perform the install in steps. Install only device settings first, so all the interfaces are created. Install Policy Package after confirming the normalized interface mappings are correct.

topics.title: HTTP 400 Bad Request error
topics.summary: DescriptionUsers encounter an HTTP 400 Bad Request error when launching secrets in FortiPAM version 7.0.0 after a passkey is registered and an Active Directory password change occurs.ScopeFortiPAM version 7.0.00.SolutionAfter upgrading FortiPAM to firmware version 7.0.0, users cannot launch secrets. The browser returns an HTTP 400 Bad Request error.This issue occurs even for users who do not have a registered passkey and authenticate with a standard username and password. Both native Remote Desktop and Web RDP launches are affected.Trigger condition:The issue is triggered when at least one user has a FIDO2 passkey registered in FortiPAM and a password change occurs for an Active Directory user. This combination causes the FortiPAM internal WAD process to reject launching requests by incorrectly identifying them as SSO launching requests that fail validation.WAD debug logs show the following error sequence:wad_pam_parse_parameters: Target only SSO launching username=xxx, 115:0 wad_pam_parse_parameters: Unexpected PAM launching request ..., err_code=5 wad_pam_token_alloc: fail to get security launcher!__wad_http_build_replmsg_resp: Generating replacement message. http request parse fail repmsg_id 0 Forward response from Internal: HTTP/1.1 400 Bad RequestThis is a known issue and currently under investigation.Workaround:To restore secret launching functionality:Remove all registered passkeys from all FortiPAM users.Instruct all users to log out of FortiPAM.Instruct all users to log back in to FortiPAM.After completing these steps, normal secret launching through the GUI is restored.

topics.title: FortiGate cannot obtain IPv6 address via DHCPv6
topics.summary: DescriptionA FortiGate interface fails to obtain or renew an IPv6 address from a DHCPv6 server despite receiving ADVERTISE packets.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionObserved behavior may include:The FortiGate sends a DHCPv6 Solicit.The upstream DHCPv6 server replies with an Advertise.The FortiGate does not complete the DHCPv6 process.No IPv6 address is assigned to the WAN interfaceRun the following command to check the current local-in policies for IPv6:show firewall local-in-policy6Create a local-in policy that allows traffic on UDP ports 546 and 547 from link-local addresses to ensure the FortiGate can process DHCPv6 ADVERTISE packets.config firewall service custom edit "DHCPv6" set udp-portrange 546-547 next end config firewall local-in-policy6 edit 1 set intf "port1" set srcaddr "ipv6-link-local" set dstaddr "all" set service "DHCPv6" set schedule "always" set action accept next end

If a policy route is configured with a destination of 0.0.0.0/0 (all destinations), it matches the traffic and is forwarded based on the path defined in the policy route, potentially bypassing the intended SD-WAN interface selection. topics.title: Layer 2 flooding on FortiSwitch
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiGate-managed FortiSwitch deployments, including MCLAG where present and "how-to" verification commands for availability on the installed FortiOS and FortiSwitchOS releases.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptom:A sudden increase in flooded traffic on an inter-switch link (ISL) or MCLAG inter-chassis link (ICL) can coincide with packet loss or high link utilization. An uplink spike shows where traffic propagated. A Layer 2 loop requires corroborating evidence.Basic checks:Classify and trace the traffic. Record the incident time. Compare ingress counter changes on the affected trunk members and adjacent ports. If the issue recurs, use port mirroring to capture the traffic and identify the frame type, VLAN, and source MAC. Check the MAC table when investigating unknown unicast.diagnose switch physical-ports port-stats list Check the forwarding topology. On the affected FortiSwitches, check STP port roles and states. Where MCLAG is in use, check ICL status and confirm STP is enabled on the ICL. Correlate unexpected forwarding paths or MAC moves with the incident.diagnose stp instance list diagnose switch mclag iclCheck the effective storm control policy. On the FortiGate, follow the ISL or ICL auto-config policy to its storm control policy and verify what was applied on the switch. A policy in disabled mode overrides the global threshold.show full-configuration switch-controller auto-config default show full-configuration switch-controller auto-config policy show full-configuration switch-controller storm-control-policy show switch-controller storm-controlCorrect the confirmed loop or unexpected forwarding path. For a confirmed broadcast storm, apply broadcast storm control at the identified ingress where practical. If the ISL also needs protection, pilot a dedicated broadcast-only override on one ISL. Set its packet rate above measured legitimate peaks, including failover. Keep storm control disabled on the ICL during the pilot.Verify that traffic rates return to baseline and that client traffic works during normal operation and failover. In NAT mode, FortiGate multicast-forward controls IP multicast forwarding through the firewall. FortiSwitch handles Layer 2 flooding separately.

topics.title: How to resolve HA out-of-sync issue due to port speed mismatch
topics.summary: DescriptionA FortiGate High Availability cluster remains out-of-sync because of a configuration mismatch in the managed-switch object regarding SFP port speed settings.ScopeFortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionA FortiGate High Availability (HA) cluster reports a synchronization status of "out-of-sync" on the secondary unit. The primary unit remains "in-sync".Specifically, the switch-controller.managed-switch object for a specific FortiSwitch differs between the primary and secondary units.The HA synchronization failure is caused by a mismatch in the port speed configuration of the managed FortiSwitch object.The primary unit has SFP ports configured as 1000full, while the secondary unit has them set to auto.When the secondary unit attempts to apply the 1000full setting during synchronization, the command is rejected with a parse error (Return code -61), preventing the objects from reaching a synchronized state.Resolution: If the cluster is out-of-sync due to a managed-switch object mismatch, the standard synchronization commands to resolve the issue might not work.The configuration on both devices will show:Primary:config switch-controller managed-switch edit "Switch1" set sn "S108FNTVXXXXXXXX" edit "port9" set port-owner '' set speed 1000full next edit "port10" set port-owner '' set speed 1000full nextSecondary:config switch-controller managed-switch edit "Switch1" set sn "S108FNTVXXXXXXXX" edit "port9" set port-owner '' set speed auto next edit "port10" set port-owner '' set speed auto nextIf trying to change the speed as auto manually, the option seems to not be available and returns an error:incomplete command in the end Command fail. Return code -160If the auto option cannot be configured due to the option missing, you can try and unset the speed on both ports, as below:edit "port10" set port-owner '' unset speedThis way, the default value will be used.The devices will now show the same values for all the ports and will be in-sync again.

topics.title: Using grep filter options in the FortiSwitch CLI
topics.summary: DescriptionThe options supported by the grep output filter in the FortiSwitchOS CLI and an explanation of how to use them to narrow down the output of show, get, diagnose, and execute commands, including when the switch is reached over SSH from a FortiGate.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionThe following are the supported options for the grep filter available on the FortiSwitch:Option Function -n Prefix each line with line_no: -c Print only the count of matching lines -o Print only the matching part of the line -v Print only non-matching lines -i Ignore case -w Whole-word match only -x Whole-line match only -F PATTERN is literal, not a regexp -E PATTERN is an extended regexp -m N Stop after N matches -A N N lines of trailing context -B N N lines of leading context -C N N lines before and after (-A N -B N) -e PTRN Extra pattern; repeatable for multiple patternsThe grep is applied as a pipe filter on any CLI command that produces output: | grep [options] PATTERNThe options can be grouped together and written as a single option cluster. For example, the -i and -c options can be combined into -ic instead of specifying them separately.show full | grep -ic trunkThe command above counts the number of lines containing the word trunk, regardless of whether it is written in uppercase or lowercase.Quick examples describing the functions:Filter MAC addresses learned on a specific port:diagnose switch mac-address list | grep port2Displays only the MAC addresses learned on port2.Display a specific port and the following lines:get switch physical-port | grep -i -A 4 port23 Displays the matching port23 line along with the next 4 lines. The -i option makes the search case-insensitive, and -A 4 displays 4 lines after the match.Count matching configuration lines:show full-config | grep -c native-vlan Counts and displays the number of lines containing native-vlan.Exclude specific matching lines:show full-config | grep -v native-vlanDisplays all configuration lines except those containing native-vlan. The -v option inverts the match.Search for multiple patterns using OR:show full-config | grep 'port1\|port2'Displays configuration lines containing either port1 or port2. The \| operator acts as an OR condition.Search for multiple patterns using -e:show full-config | grep -e port1 -e native-vlanDisplays configuration lines containing either port1 or native-vlan. The -e option allows multiple search patterns in a single command.Note: From a FortiGate, SSH to the switch and run the same commands there, since this article describes only the grep filter options available in the FortiSwitch:FGT # execute ssh admin@ FSW # show full | grep -ic trunkFor the available grep filter options in the FortiGate CLI, refer to the following KB article: options: The usage of "grep" filter command on the FortiGate CLI.

topics.title: Explaining the 'Auto reprovision users' setting in Sync Rules
topics.summary: Description'Auto reprovision users' setting in Sync Rules.ScopeFortiAuthenticator 8.0.4.SolutionThe behavior of expired FortiToken Mobile activations differs between FortiAuthenticator releases.FortiAuthenticator 6.6.9 and EarlierIf a user did not activate their FortiToken Mobile before the activation period expired, the account was automatically locked.An administrator had to manually unlock the account.FortiAuthenticator 6.6.10, 6.6.11, 8.0.2, and 8.0.3If token activation expired, the user account was locked.At the next synchronization, the account was automatically unlocked and a new activation period of FortiToken started.No administrator intervention was required.FortiAuthenticator 8.0.4 – New SettingRelease 8.0.4 introduces Auto reprovision users, which is enabled by default.Enabled: Expired token activations are automatically restarted during the next synchronization, and the user account is unlocked.Disabled: The user remains locked and is skipped during synchronization until an administrator manually unlocks the account.Summary:FortiAuthenticator 8.0.4 allows administrators to choose between automatic token reprovisioning and manual account unlocking.

topics.title: FortiGate 6k Chassis: Pre- and Post-Firmware Upgrade Health Check and Validation Guide
topics.summary: DescriptionA comprehensive pre- and post-firmware upgrade health-check procedure for the FortiGate 6k chassis, covering system performance, hardware health, FPC status, HA and configuration synchronization, DP channel connectivity, session statistics, and interface status to establish a baseline before the upgrade and validate chassis health after the upgrade.ScopeFortiGate 6k Chassis.SolutionObjectivesThis procedure is intended to establish a consistent operational baseline and confirm that the FortiGate 6000F chassis is healthy following a firmware upgrade.Verify overall firewall and chassis operational status.Review CPU and memory utilization.Validate FPC operation, hardware health, and redundancy.Confirm HA status and configuration synchronization, where applicable.Check blade checksums, DP channel connectivity, and base backplane communication.Record session, routing-table, and firewall-policy reference counts.Review DP channel statistics for potential packet discardsWhen to run the health checkPhaseWhenPurposePre-upgradeImmediately before starting the firmware upgrade.Capture the known-good baseline, identify existing faults and confirm the chassis is ready for the maintenance activity.Post-upgradeAfter the upgrade has completed and the chassis has returned to its intended operational state.Repeat the same checks and compare the results with the pre-upgrade baseline.Execution guidelinesRun the checks from the appropriate management access and on both chassis in an HA deployment, unless a command is specifically intended for one chassis or blade.Save the complete command output with a timestamp and identify the chassis, firmware version, and phase (PRE or POST).Use the same commands and collection method before and after the upgrade so that the results can be compared consistently.Do not treat a value as a failure solely because it differs from the baseline. Investigate unexpected changes and confirm whether they are expected for the upgraded software version or the current HA role.If a check reports an unexpected state, capture the output and investigate before declaring the chassis healthy.Detailed health checks4.1 System status and firmwareget system statusDisplays system and firmware information, including firmware/build details and HA mode.Health Check: Confirm that the running firmware/build is the expected version for the relevant phase. Record the output for pre/post comparison.4.2 CPU and memory utilizationget system performance statusDisplays overall system performance, including CPU and memory utilization.Health Check:Review the reported CPU and memory utilization and note any abnormal or unexpected resource usage.4.3 FPM/FPC load-balance statusdiagnose load-balance statusProvides information about which FPM/FPC is the master.Health Check:The status message should show Running.Note: If an error is present, the status may show messages such as 'waiting for data heartbeat' or 'waiting for configuration sync'. Investigate these conditions.4.4 HA status (where applicable)get sys ha statusDisplays HA master and slave information, including cluster synchronization state, VLAN ID, cluster uptime, and HA history.Health Check:HA Health Status should be OK. Review MONDEV statistics and confirm that the up/down state is the same on both chassis.Note: Record the HA role and history before and after the upgrade. A role change during the upgrade should be assessed in the context of the upgrade procedure.4.5 Configuration synchronizationdiagnose sys confsync statusChecks configuration synchronization across the blades.Health Check: All blades should report in_sync=1. A value of in_sync=0 indicates a configuration synchronization issue.4.6 HA group and heartbeat detailsdiagnose sys ha dump-by groupDisplays HA heartbeat-device selection, active worker information, uptime, and reset_cn.Health Check:best_hbdev should identify ha1 when communication is expected over the HA1 interface. best_hbdev active worker counts should be the same on both chassis. link_failure, pingsvr_failure, and active_worker should be the same. The master chassis flag should be 1, and the slave chassis flag should be 0.4.7 Configuration checksum consistencydiagnose sys confsync showcsum | grep "SN\|^all"Displays configuration checksums for the blades.Health Check:Each blade should print four checksum lines. The first and second checksum lines should match across all blades on both the master and slave chassis. The third and fourth lines should match within the same chassis.Note: Capture the full output from both chassis to allow a direct comparison.4.8 DP channel link statusdiagnose sys bcm_intf cli "ps xe1-xe24"Displays the link status of DP channel links. DP channel issues can affect communication between the ISF and FPC.Health Check: Review the status of all listed DP channel links and investigate any unexpected down state.4.9 Base switch and backplane healthdiagnose hardware deviceinfo nic base-mgmtChecks the base management interfa

topics.title: HTTP 500 error during OAuth authorization after upgrading FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.10
topics.summary: DescriptionUsers receive an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error at the /api/v1/oauth/authorize/ endpoint when authenticating through applications using FortiAuthenticator as an OAuth/OIDC provider.ScopeFortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10.SolutionAfter upgrading to FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10, users attempting to log in via OAuth/OIDC applications encounter an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.The error occurs specifically at the /api/v1/oauth/authorize/ endpoint.The system logs display the following traceback:Internal Server Error: /api/v1/oauth/authorize/ Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "./fac/fac/apps/oauth/views.py", line 282, in dispatch File "/lib/python3.11/site-packages/django/utils/functional.py", line 268, in inner return func(_wrapped, *args) AttributeError: 'RemoteLdapSessionUser' object has no attribute 'fac_groups' Root cause.This issue occurs when a non-imported remote user attempts to access an OAuth authorization page. In FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10, non-imported remote users cannot log in to OAuth portals, which leads to the AttributeError and the resulting HTTP 500 error.Resolution.The fix is available in the following versions:FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.12.FortiAuthenticator version 8.0.5.

topics.title: FortiPAM web launcher DNS error after upgrade to 1.9.2
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiPAM upgrades from version 1.9.1 to 1.9.2 may cause a 504 DNS lookup failed error when using web launchers with placeholders.ScopeFortiPAM.SolutionAfter upgrading FortiPAM from version 1.9.1 to 1.9.2, users may encounter a "504 DNS lookup failed" error when accessing a web launcher configured with placeholders. The launcher no longer displays a prompt for users to enter or modify the target FQDN, preventing successful access to the configured URL.This behavior is due to a change introduced in FortiPAM 1.9.2, where the web launcher no longer automatically prompts for the actual FQDN when placeholders are used in the configuration. As a result, placeholder values are not resolved at launch time, which can lead to DNS resolution failures.This issue is addressed by a fix in the FortiPAM 1.9.3 release train. The fix ensures that when launching a web session using a multiple-address secret with Login with Associated Credentials enabled, the web browser launcher correctly resolves the target URL and retrieves the associated credentials, preventing login failures caused by an empty target value.Related documents:Resolved Issues: Web browsing fails with multiple target address and associated secret credentialsCreating secret templates

topics.title: QUIC inspection mode unexpectedly changes when renaming an SSL/SSH profile in the GUI
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a known issue where the QUIC inspection mode in an SSL/SSH inspection profile is unexpectedly changed when the profile name is modified through the FortiGate GUI.ScopeFortiOS versions 7.4.13, 7.6.8 and 8.0.2.SolutionWhen an SSL/SSH inspection profile is renamed through the FortiGate GUI, the configured QUIC inspection mode is unexpectedly reset from inspect to bypass.As a result, the QUIC inspection configuration is not retained after renaming the profile through the GUI.This behavior has been confirmed in FortiOS versions 7.4.13, 7.6.8, and 8.0.2.Configuration before renaming through the GUI:The following configuration shows the original SSL/SSH inspection profile with QUIC inspection enabled:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "test-certificate-inspection" set comment "Read-only SSL handshake inspection profile." config https set ports 443 set status certificate-inspection set quic inspect set cert-probe-failure allow end next endConfiguration after renaming through the GUI:After changing the profile name through the GUI, the QUIC inspection mode is unexpectedly changed to bypass.config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "certificate-inspection_fqdn-test" set comment "Read-only SSL handshake inspection profile." config https set ports 443 set status certificate-inspection set quic bypass set cert-probe-failure allow end next endWorkaround:There are two available workarounds:Option 1: Rename the SSL/SSH inspection profile using the CLI.Use the CLI to change the profile name instead of renaming it through the GUI.Option 2: Manually reapply the QUIC inspection mode through the CLI.If the profile has already been renamed through the GUI, manually configure the correct QUIC inspection mode:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit " " config https set quic inspect end next endVerify the configuration after applying the change:show firewall ssl-ssh-profile " "Confirm that the QUIC inspection mode is set to inspect.The issue is currently scheduled to be fixed in FortiOS version 8.0.3.

topics.title: Understanding MTU Drops, ICMP Fragmentation Needed, and Silent Packet Black Holes
topics.summary: DescriptionHow Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) mismatches can lead to either expected ICMP error generation or silent packet drops within a network. A step-by-step breakdown of packet walks and diagnostic FortiOS commands is provided to help identify and resolve these connectivity issues.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionScenario 1: ICMP Fragmentation Needed (Layer-3 Egress Check)An ICMP Type 3, Code 4 ("Fragmentation Needed and DF Set") message is generated only when a packet successfully enters a FortiGate, is routed at Layer 3, and fails the MTU check as it tries to exit (Egress) an outbound interface.Ingress on FortiGate R2 port2 (MTU 1500) — PASSES Layer 2:The 1444-byte IP packet (plus 14-byte Ethernet header = 1458-byte frame) arrives at port2. The physical NIC/ASIC checks: Is 1444 <= 1500? Yes. The hardware accepts the frame, strips the Outer Ethernet Layer-2 header, and hands the 1444-byte IP packet up to FortiOS's Layer-3 routing engine.Egress on FortiGate R2 port1 (MTU 1200) — FAILS Layer 3:The routing engine looks up the destination IP and determines the packet must exit port1. Before transmission, FortiOS checks port1's configured IP MTU (1200): Is 1444 <= 1200? No. Because the Don't Fragment (DF=1) bit is set, the Layer-3 engine drops the packet.Result:Because the packet is inside the Layer-3 IP engine, FortiGate R2 generates an ICMP Type 3, Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed, Next-Hop MTU = 1200) packet back to the source (FortiGate R1).config system interface edit "port1" set mtu-override enable set mtu 1200 next enddiagnose sniffer packet any "host 192.168.23.2 and icmp" 6 0 lexecute ping-options df-bit yes execute ping-options data-size 1400 execute ping 192.168.23.2Packet capture:Scenario 2: Silent Packet Drops (Layer-2 Ingress Check / Mismatched Link MTU)A silent drop (zero ICMP messages) occurs when two directly connected interfaces on the same wire have mismatched MTUs, preventing the oversized packet from ever reaching a Layer-3 engine.Egress on FortiGate R2 port1 (MTU 1500) — PASSES Layer 3:FortiGate R2 checks its own port1 MTU (1500). Since 1444 <= 1500, FortiGate R2 assumes the link can handle 1444 bytes and transmits the frame straight onto the wire toward FortiGate R3. No ICMP message is generated.Ingress on FortiGate R3 port1 (MTU 1200) — SILENT LAYER-2 HARDWARE DROP:As the frame enters FortiGate R3's port1 Layer-1/Layer-2 MAC hardware buffer (sized for a 1200-byte payload maximum), the physical NIC/ASIC immediately aborts and discards the oversized frame at Layer 2.Result:The frame is destroyed inside the Layer-2 Ethernet MAC hardware on ingress and never reaches FortiGate R3's Layer-3 IP stack. Because the Layer-2 MAC chip does not parse IPv4 headers or generate ICMP error packets, the drop is completely silent, causing a packet black hole.R3 # diagnose netlink interface list port3 if=port3 family=00 type=1 index=5 mtu=1200 link=0 master=0 ref=11 state=start present fw_flags=400 flags=up broadcast run multicast Qdisc=pfifo_fast hw_addr=00:43:68:61:37:03 broadcast_addr=ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff stat: rxp=95 txp=10 rxb=6722 txb=1644 rxe=0 txe=0 rxd=0 txd=0 mc=0 collision=0 @ time=1794323917 re: rxl=0 rxo=0 rxc=0 rxf=0 rxfi=0 rxm=0 te: txa=0 txc=0 txfi=0 txh=0 txw=0 misc rxc=0 txc=0 input_type=0 state=3 arp_entry=0 refcnt=11R3 # fnsysctl ifconfig port3 port3 Link encap:Ethernet HWaddr 00:43:68:61:37:03 inet addr:192.168.23.2 Bcast:192.168.23.255 Mask:255.255.255.0 UP BROADCAST RUNNING MULTICAST MTU:1200 Metric:1 RX packets:104 errors:0 dropped:0 overruns:0 frame:0 TX packets:11 errors:0 dropped:0 overruns:0 carrier:0 collisions:0 txqueuelen:1000 RX bytes:7282 (7.1 KB) TX bytes:1820 (1.8 KB) Scenario 3: Silent Drop Across a Layer-2 SwitchIf a 1444-byte packet enters a Layer-2 switch port (FortiSwitch SW1 port1 with MTU 1500) and attempts to exit another Layer-2 switch port (port2 with MTU 1200), the drop is also completely silent.Even though the drop occurs on Egress (port2), the device forwarding the frame is operating as a Layer-2 Bridge/Switch, not a Layer-3 Router.A Layer-2 switch only reads the 14-byte Ethernet header (Destination MAC address). It has no Layer-3 IP routing engine on that transit VLAN and cannot generate an ICMP Type 3, Code 4 message back to the sender.Related articles:Technical Tip: MTU size and Interface related Errors on FortiGate

topics.title: FortiClient IPsec VPN Always Up option visibility
topics.summary: DescriptionThe Always Up option in FortiClient IPsec VPN settings is inconsistently visible. This occurs when specific configuration flags are enabled in the client configuration file.ScopeFortiClient, FortiGate.SolutionSymptoms.Users report that the 'Always Up' option is visible in the FortiClient IPsec VPN settings for some installations but not for others, despite using the same software version.The user also confirmed that the show_alwaysup option is set to '0' under the section of the XML file: 0 Root cause.The visibility of the 'Always Up' and 'Remember Password' options is controlled by specific keys within the FortiClient configuration file. topics.title: OCI HA: reserved management interface (ha-mgmt-status) has no internet access - blocks NTP/FortiToken Cloud, also suspect same root cause for SDN connector VIP failover not working
topics.summary: Environment: FortiGate-VM64-OPC on OCI, FortiOS 7.6.7, A-P unicast HA, ha-mgmt-status enabled on port1 (reserved management interface, config ha-mgmt-interfaces with its own gateway).Two related issues, same root cause suspected:1. FortiToken Cloud MFA fails when logging into a unit directly via its own management IP - works on one unit, fails on the other. Traced to: the unit whose management interface needs to reach FortiGuard/FortiToken Cloud for validation has no outbound path. Confirmed via execute ping-options source + ping 8.8.8.8 -> 100% loss, on both HA members (tested independently, not just the HA secondary).2. topics.title: High CPU consumption on FortiGate-VM When enabling security profiles
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue of high CPU utilization on a FortiGate-VM running FortiOS version 8.0 when enabling security profiles on firewall policies.ScopeFortiGate-VM, Proxmox.SolutionA FortiGate-VM running on Proxmox has CPU utilization increase to approximately 99% when enabling security profiles, even when little or no traffic is passing through the firewall. Disabling the security profiles returns CPU utilization to normal levels.The FortiGate-VM was configured with the KVM64 virtual CPU model.This CPU model does not expose the SSE4.2 instruction set required by Hyperscan, resulting in high CPU consumption when security inspection features are enabled.To solve the issue, change the virtual CPU type in Proxmox to a model that supports SSE4.2.The recommended CPU models are:x86-64-v2-AES.x86-64-v3.x86-64-v4.host.For updating the CPU type on a FortiGate VM in Proxmox:Log in to the Proxmox web interface.Select the FortiGate VM from the resource tree.Select Hardware and then select Processors.Edit the Type field and select one of the supported types listed above (e.g., host).Save the changes.Restart the FortiGate VM for the changes to take effect.

topics.title: Upgrading a FortiGate High Availability cluster to version 8.0.1 may remove the ha-mgmt-interfaces configuration if the interface is set to dedicated-to management
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue where a FortiGate High Availability (HA) cluster loses ha-mgmt-interfaces entry configuration upon upgrading to FortiOS 8.0.1.ScopeFortiGate, FortiOS 8.0.1.SolutionAfter upgrading a FortiGate High Availability (HA) cluster to version 8.0.1 , the ha-mgmt-interfaces configuration is stripped from the HA settings.Check the config-error-log: diagnose debug config-error-log read >>> "set" "interface" "mgmt" @ global.system.ha.ha-mgmt-interfaces.1:value parse error (error -3) >>> "next" @ global.system.ha.ha-mgmt-interfaces.1:failed command (error -56)Configuration example before the upgrade:config system interface edit "mgmt" set vdom "root" set ip 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.240 set allowaccess ping https ssh snmp set type physical set dedicated-to management set snmp-index 1 next end config system ha set group-name "fortinet" set mode a-p set password FortinetPasswordMask set hbdev "ha" 0 set ha-mgmt-status enable config ha-mgmt-interfaces edit 1 set interface "mgmt" set gateway 192.168.1.2 next end set override disable endConfiguration change after the upgrade:config system interface edit "mgmt" set vdom "root" set ip 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.240 set allowaccess ping https ssh snmp set type physical set dedicated-to management set snmp-index 1 next end config system ha set group-name "fortinet" set mode a-p set password FortinetPasswordMask set hbdev "ha" 0 set ha-mgmt-status enable set override disable endWhen attempting to re-add the management interface via the Command Line Interface (CLI), the system returns the error "entry not found in datasource" and the interface does not appear in the list of available options.# config system ha (ha) # config ha-mgmt-interfaces (ha-mgmt-interfaces) # edit 1 new entry '1' added (1) # set interface port23 entry not found in datasource value parse error before 'port23' Command fail. Return code -3Starting from FortiOS 8.0.1, interfaces configured as ha-mgmt-interfaces are not permitted to be set as dedicated-to-management, hence the upgrade process removes the ha-mgmt-interfaces entry when the associated management interface is configured with the dedicated-to management setting.Manual fix: To restore the ability to configure the HA management interface, unset the dedicated-to management setting on the interface. Perform these steps on both cluster members:Access the CLI of the FortiGate unit:Run the following commands to unset the dedicated management setting:config system interface edit "mgmt" unset dedicated-to management next endRe-configure the HA management interface settings under the HA configuration:config system ha config ha-mgmt-interfaces edit 1 set interface "mgmt" set gateway 192.168.1.2 next end endFortiOS 8.0.3 will contain additional upgrade handling to removed dedicated-to management setting on interfaces already found to be configured for dedicated HA management.

topics.title: FortiAuthenticator SSO session failure with NT_STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED error
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue where users fail to establish a Single Sign-On session on FortiAuthenticator after Windows security updates, resulting in an NTLM authentication failure.ScopeFortiAuthenticator, Windows Server 2025. SolutionUsers may experience Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication failures when using the Fortinet Single Sign-On (FSSO) Mobility Agent with FortiAuthenticator following the installation of Microsoft security updates released on November 10, 2026 (KB5135557).The issue results in NTLM authentication failures, preventing users from establishing SSO sessions on FortiAuthenticator. The logs display the error NT_STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED.11/11/2026 13:23:24 2B4BE6C0] NTLM auth result: 114 NTLM auth failed:Username/dcname(dc_time=1794399804...);error:NT_STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED]The issue is related to changes in NTLM signing behavior introduced by Microsoft's November 10, 2026 security updates. Windows clients now offer NTLM signing by default, which appears to cause a compatibility issue with the FSSO Mobility Agent.An internal engineering ticket has been raised to investigate the compatibility issue.Temporary workaround:If NTLM authentication must remain enabled, temporarily allow unsigned NTLM authentication on the affected Windows clients by applying the registry configuration documented in Microsoft's KB5135557.For further details, refer to the following Microsoft documentation:KB5135557 – NTLM Signing Security Improvements

topics.title: Technical Tip: Configuring IPSec VPN tunnels on VDOMs that do not have a WAN connection
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to configure IPSec VPN tunnels on Inter-VDOM links to allow VDOMs with no WAN interface to communicate with remote peers through the root VDOM. Scope FortiGate. Solution Consider that FortiGate has only one WAN connection assigned to the root VDOM, and an IPSec VPN tunnel should be configured on VDOM1. Then, the root VDOM should NAT the IKE traffic originating from VDOM1, and send it to the remote peer. Here is the Step by Step guide: Site A VPN gateway. Create globally Inter-VDOM links on both VDOMs Config global Config system interface edit "VDOM-link0" set vdom "root" set ip 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.252 set type vdom-link set snmp-index 14 next edit "VDOM-link1" set vdom "VDOM1" set ip 10.0.0.2 255.255.255.252 set type vdom-link set snmp-index 15 next end On VDOM1, configure an IPSec tunnel over the 'VDOM-link1' interface config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "VPN-FGT-A" set interface "VDOM-link1" set proposal aes256-sha1 set dhgrp 5 set remote-gw 172.16.1.1 end config vpn ipsec phase2-interface edit "VPN-FGT-A" set phase1name "VPN-FGT-A" set proposal aes256-sha1 set dhgrp 5 set src-subnet 10.10.1.0 255.255.255.0 set dst-subnet 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 end Static routing. config router static edit 1 set device "VPN-FGT-A" set dstaddr "192.168.10.0-24" next edit 2 set distance 254 set blackhole enable set dstaddr "192.168.10.0-24" end Firewall policies. config firewall policy edit 1 set name "vpn_VPN-FGT_local" set srcintf "internal" set dstintf "VPN-FGT-A" set srcaddr "10.10.1.0-24" set dstaddr "192.168.10.0-24" set action accept set schedule "always" set service "ALL" next edit 2 set name "vpn_VPN-FGT_remote" set srcintf "VPN-FGT-A" set dstintf "internal" set srcaddr "192.168.10.0-24" set dstaddr "10.10.1.0-24" set action accept set schedule "always" set service "ALL" next end On root VDOM, configure an outgoing NAT policy from src: VDOM-link0 ---> dst:WAN interface with fixedport enabled to preserve the source ports (500/4500). config firewall policy edit 1 set name "outgoing" set srcintf "VDOM-link0" set dstintf "wan1" set srcaddr "10.0.0.2-IP" set dstaddr "172.16.1.1-IP" set action accept set schedule "always" set service "IKE" set fixedport enable set nat enable end Configure an incoming policy with VIP as a destination address from src:WAN interface ---> dst: VDOM-link0 config firewall vip edit " VIP-10.0.0.2" set extip X.X.X.X <- Site A Public IP. set extintf "wan1" set mappedip "10.0.0.2" next end config firewall policy edit 2 set name "incoming" set uuid 17e0cd48-bdf3-51e9-1ff5-3f7995b1c6d7 set srcintf "wan1" set dstintf "VDOM-link0" set srcaddr "172.16.1.1-IP" set dstaddr "VIP-10.0.0.2" set action accept set schedule "always" set service "IKE" next end Note: Before configuring IPsec VPN, make sure there is Internet access from the desired VDOM. Refer to this document for more information: Technical Tip: WAN connectivity using inter-VDOM link

topics.title: Bringing Cisco Meraki MX into FortiAnalyzer SOC: Third-Party Log Parsing with FortiGuard SOC Automation (plus a custom parser)
topics.summary: https://github.com/ibrugnolli/meraki-fortianalyzer-soc-integration Why this mattersMany SOC teams work in mixed-vendor environments. Branch offices often run Cisco Meraki MX appliances, while the security operations stack is built on the Fortinet Security Fabric. Without proper parsing, Meraki syslog messages arrive in FortiAnalyzer as raw text that analysts can't easily filter, correlate or report on.To close this gap, I put together an open-source integration guide plus a custom log parser. It's all on GitHub: https://github.com/ibrugnolli/meraki-fortianalyzer-soc-integrationWhat the project coversThe repository is a step-by-step deployment guide with screenshots for every stage. It covers three things:Enabling the FortiGuard third-party parser. It uses the FortiAnalyzer SOC Automation Service (the RHSP FortiGuard content pack) to install the Cisco Meraki Firewall Log Parser. Configuring the Meraki MX to send syslog to FortiAnalyzer. This includes turning on the security features that generate useful events. Deploying a custom JSON parser. It extends the FortiGuard baseline with deeper mapping of Meraki event_type messages from recent MX firmware.Tested environmentCisco Meraki MX67 running MX 26.2.3 FortiAnalyzer 8.0.2 (build 0198); 7.6.4 or later is required A valid FortiAnalyzer SOC Automation Service license, with the unit registered to FortiCare/FortiGuard The MX sends UDP syslog on port 514 from its WAN interface to the FortiAnalyzer IPPart 1: Preparing FortiAnalyzerCheck the firmware version and NTP/time sync. Confirm the FortiCare registration, the SOC Automation license and FortiGuard connectivity. Go to Incidents & Alerts > FortiGuard Services > SOC Automation to review the third-party parsers in the content pack. Under Incidents & Alerts > Log Parsers > Log Parsers > Uninstalled Log Parsers, install Cisco Meraki Firewall Log Parser. Move it to the top of the list and confirm that its Origin is FortiGuard. Best practice: create a dedicated Fabric ADOM (for example, MERAKI_INTEGRATION) with the correct timezone, and install the parser in that ADOM too. This keeps third-party logs separate from your FortiGate data.Part 2: Configuring the Meraki MXIn Network-Wide > General > Logging, add a syslog server using the FortiAnalyzer IP (default port and protocol) and select the roles you need. In Network-Wide > Alerts, enable the alerts you want logged. In Security & SD-WAN > Threat Protection, enable AMP and IDS/IPS so the security engines generate events. In Security & SD-WAN > Content Filtering, block a test category to produce content-filtering events. Generate test traffic. You can check events in the Meraki Event Log and Security Center, and use Network-Wide > Packet Capture to confirm that syslog packets are actually leaving toward FortiAnalyzer.Part 3: Authorizing the device and checking the parsingThe MX first shows up under Unauthorized Devices. Right-click it, choose Authorize and assign it to the Meraki ADOM. The status changes to UP once logs start arriving. After a few minutes, Incidents & Alerts > Log Parsers > Assigned Parsers should show an automatic assignment to the Cisco Meraki parser. This confirms that FortiAnalyzer recognizes and parses the messages. In Log View > Logs > All, filter on "Cisco" to see normalized Meraki logs side by side with the rest of your Fabric data.Part 4: Going further with the custom parserThe FortiGuard parser is a solid baseline. I wanted richer field mapping for SOC analysis, so the repository also includes scripts/custom_meraki_parser.json ("Cisco Meraki Custom Log Parser v2"). Its rule sets cover the main Meraki message types:Network flows and firewall: source and destination IP/port, NAT IP/port, protocol and direction, plus normalized allow/deny decisions taken from several Meraki formats (pattern:, decision=, flows allow|deny). URL logs: HTTP method, URL and user agent. Events: event subtypes and content-filtering fields. Security events: IDS alerts and AMP file scans, mapped to threat name, ID, severity and action, plus file hash. Air Marshal: SSID, BSSID and source/destination MACs. Timestamps: taken from the syslog header, or from the Meraki epoch if the header has none.In total, 32 FortiAnalyzer fields are populated. That makes Meraki events much more usable in Log View, event handlers, correlation rules and reports. To deploy it, go to Incidents & Alerts > Log Parsers > Log Parsers > Create New, paste in the JSON and click Apply.Credits and licenseThe custom parser was converted from the community project BenderScript/meraki_syslog_parser. My repository is released under the Apache 2.0 license.Feedback welcome!If you run Meraki alongside FortiAnalyzer, give it a try and let me know how it works in your environment. Issues, pull requests and suggestions for more event_type mappings are very welcome on GitHub. I'd also love to hear how others are bringing non-Fortinet devices into their FortiAnalyzer SOC workflows.

topics.title: Analytics database size or range reduced after upgrading FortiAnalyzer to version 7.6 (ClickHouse migration)
topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to verify whether analytics logs are complete after upgrading FortiAnalyzer from version 7.4 to 7.6, when the analytics database usage decreases significantly after the upgrade, and how to rebuild the analytics database from archive logs if data is missing.ScopeFortiAnalyzer version 7.6 (upgraded from version 7.4).SolutionSymptom.After upgrading FortiAnalyzer from version 7.4 to 7.6, the analytics database usage is much lower than before the upgrade (for example, from about 4 TB to less than 100 GB), although the data policy keeps analytics logs for 90 days. Log View, FortiView, or reports for older dates may show fewer logs than expected.Background.Starting in v7.6, FortiAnalyzer stores analytics logs in a ClickHouse database instead of PostgreSQL. During the upgrade, the existing analytics data is migrated to ClickHouse. This is different from a database rebuild: the migration reads the existing analytics database, while a rebuild (execute sql-local rebuild-db) recreates the analytics database from the archive (raw) logs.A lower disk usage after the upgrade is expected and is not, on its own, a sign of missing data. ClickHouse is a columnar database with high compression, and the previous database usage also included the FortiView/report cache (hcache), which is regenerated on demand. Data completeness must be validated by the date range and the number of logs per day, not by disk usage.Verification.Check the database status and size.diagnose sql status rebuild-db diagnose sql show db-sizeConfirm that no rebuild or migration is still in progress. If the database size is still increasing between runs, wait for the process to finish before drawing conclusions.Check the analytics date range.diagnose test application logfiled 4 Compare the oldest analytics date with the analytics retention configured in the ADOM data policy.Compare log volumes per day.In Log View, select the same device and filters and compare an older day with a recent day. If the number of logs is of the same order, the analytics data is complete. If the older days contain much fewer logs than the recent days, the analytics data for that period is incomplete.Check archive log availability and quotas.Confirm in the ADOM data policy and storage settings that:Archive logs are kept for at least the analytics retention period. A rebuild can only restore the periods that are still available in the archive logs.The analytics quota is large enough to hold the full retention period.If the analytics data is incomplete and the archive logs for the missing period are available, rebuild the analytics database from the archive logs.Plan a maintenance window and take a configuration backup (and a snapshot for VM deployments) before starting. The rebuild reboots FortiAnalyzer, purges the analytics database, and inserts the archive logs again. It is resource-intensive and can take from hours to days depending on the log volume. Log View, FortiView, and reports are incomplete until it finishes. Logs received during the rebuild are not lost.Starting in v7.6, the rebuild of a single ADOM is not available. The rebuild applies to all ADOMs.Set the start time of the rebuild according to the analytics retention period (for example, 90 days before the current date), then start the rebuild:config system sql set start-time end execute sql-local rebuild-dbMonitor the progress:diagnose sql status rebuild-db diagnose sql show db-sizeIf the status remains at 99% for a long time, check whether the database size is still increasing. Refer to the related article below.After the rebuild is completed, repeat the verification steps. The oldest analytics date must match the retention period, and the number of logs per day must be consistent between older and recent days. The database size will be smaller than in v7.4 for the same data because of the ClickHouse compression.If the rebuild is completed, the archive logs and retention settings are correct, and the analytics data is still incomplete, contact Fortinet Technical Support with the outputs above.

topics.title: FortiSwitch 1xx series IGMP snooping limit reduced in FortiSwitchOS 7.6.6
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue on FortiSwitch 100 Series switches running FortiSwitchOS 7.6.6, where native VLAN changes pushed from FortiGate/FortiManager fail to synchronize with the managed FortiSwitch.ScopeFortiSwitch-1XX series v7.6.6 and above.SolutionWhen attempting to push VLAN or port configuration changes from FortiGate/FortiManager, the FortiSwitch fails to apply the configuration updates.The synchronization status can be verified using the following command:execute switch-controller get-sync-status allThe following error message may be observed:"Enable IGMP Snooping not allowed, maximum 5 vlans have been enabled with IGMP Snooping"To resolve this issue:Reduce the number of VLANs with IGMP Snooping enabled to five or fewer.Review the VLAN configuration on the FortiSwitch.Identify the VLANs where IGMP Snooping is enabled.Disable IGMP Snooping on the VLANs where it is not required.Ensure that the total number of VLANs with IGMP Snooping enabled does not exceed five.Allow the FortiGate/FortiManager to synchronize the configuration with the FortiSwitch.After making the necessary changes, execute the following command on the FortiGate:execute switch-controller get-sync-status allReducing the number of IGMP Snooping-enabled VLANs to five or fewer allows the switch to accept the configuration updates and synchronize successfully with FortiGate/FortiManager.
