topics.title: Fragmented GTP-U delivered through an IPsec tunnel and throughput tuning with post-encapsulation fragmentation
topics.summary: DescriptionThe reasons why GTP-U traffic (UDP/2152) carried in an IPsec tunnel can be delivered to the downstream node (eNB or core) as IPv4 fragments, featuring an explanation of how to make sure the node receives complete GTP-U packets, along with which settings to review if throughput decreases after the change.ScopeFortiOS 7.4 (NP7 and NP7Lite platforms for the Host Protection Engine section).SolutionSymptomGTP-U packets leaving the IPsec tunnel are forwarded to the downstream node as two IPv4 fragments. Nodes that do not accept fragmented GTP-U drop the traffic or show degraded performance.The fragments can be seen with a sniffer on the interface facing the downstream node:diagnose sniffer packet 'udp port 2152 or (ip[6:2] & 0x1fff != 0)' 4 100 aFragments are shown as (frag : @ +).CauseThe phase1 is configured with ip-fragmentation pre-encapsulation. When a GTP-U packet is larger than the tunnel MTU, the sending FortiGate fragments the inner packet before encryption and sends each fragment as a separate ESP packet. The receiving FortiGate decrypts each ESP packet and forwards the inner fragments unchanged. Reassembly is left to the destination host. This is expected behaviour of pre-encapsulation fragmentation.Configure post-encapsulation fragmentation on both peers.With post-encapsulation (the default), the complete packet is encrypted first. If the ESP packet exceeds the underlay MTU, only the outer ESP packet is fragmented. The receiving FortiGate reassembles the ESP packet, decrypts it and forwards the complete GTP-U packet.The fragmentation method is applied by the encrypting side, so configure it on both peers to cover both directions:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit " " set ip-fragmentation post-encapsulation next endApply the change in a maintenance window. If the behavior does not change, re-establish the tunnel.Make sure the tunnel interface MTU is not lower than the largest GTP-U packet sent by the nodes. Packets larger than the tunnel interface MTU are fragmented before IPsec processing.config system interface edit " " set mtu-override enable set mtu next endReview the receiving side if throughput decreases.With post-encapsulation, each large packet crosses the underlay as two IP fragments. The receiving FortiGate processes and reassembles them in the CPU. At high rates, two mechanisms can drop them.NP7/NP7Lite Host Protection Engine (HPE). When enable-shaper is enabled, ESP packets and IP fragments sent to the CPU are rate limited in packets per second. Check the HPE_IPSEC_ESP and HPE_IP_FRAG counters during a throughput test (the command below is for NP7Lite platforms):diagnose npu np7lite dce-drop-allIf they increase, raise the limits above the expected peak with a safety margin:config system npu config hpe set esp-max set ip-frag-max end endAs a reference, 1484-byte packets need about 84 ESP packets per second per Mbps, and each ESP packet is sent as two fragments. For example, 200 Mbps is about 17,000 ESP packets per second and 34,000 fragments per second. Avoid extreme values, as they effectively disable CPU protection.Fragment reassembly memory. The default reassembly buffer is 32 MB. When it is exhausted, fragments are dropped and ReasmFails increases. Orphan fragments (where the second fragment was lost in transit) stay in the buffer until they time out, which makes this worse on lossy links.diagnose snmp ip frags fnsysctl cat /proc/net/sockstatIf required, increase the threshold. The range is 32-2047, available from v7.0.8 and v7.2.4. Size it according to the FRAG memory used at peak:config system global set ip-fragment-mem-thresholds endAdditional checks during the test:diagnose vpn tunnel list name diagnose sys mpstat 2Recommended: avoid fragmentation.Post-encapsulation delivers complete packets to the nodes, but the underlay still carries fragments. The most robust design is to set the GTP-U interface MTU of the radio and core nodes so that the ESP packet fits in the underlay MTU without fragmentation. For example, with AES-CBC/SHA256, no NAT-T and an underlay MTU of 1492, the SA MTU is 1422 bytes. AES-GCM reduces the ESP overhead.

topics.title: Wi-Fi EAP-TLS authentication fails due to IPsec packet fragmentation
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue where RADIUS packets carrying client certificates are dropped across an IPsec tunnel, preventing successful EAP-TLS authentication on FortiAuthenticator.ScopeFortiGate, FortiAuthenticator.SolutionUsers cannot connect to a Wi-Fi SSID using EAP-TLS authentication. Packet captures show that FortiAuthenticator receives the RADIUS Access-Request and responds with an Access-Challenge, but no subsequent reply is received. Further analysis reveals that client certificates are missing from the RADIUS packets arriving at the FortiAuthenticator.Root cause:Large RADIUS packets containing client certificates are dropped due to IPsec packet fragmentation across the data center tunnel. This prevents the full certificate information from reaching the FortiAuthenticator, causing the authentication process to fail.Resolution:Configure the IPsec tunnel to use post-encapsulation fragmentation. This ensures that large packets are fragmented after they are encrypted, allowing them to traverse the tunnel without being dropped.Access the Command Line Interface (CLI) of the FortiGate device.Modify the Phase 1 settings of the affected IPsec tunnel to set fragmentation to post-encapsulation.config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit set ip-fragmentation post-encapsulation set npu-offload disable next endVerify that the Wi-Fi endpoints can now successfully authenticate and connect to the SSID.Note: With post-encapsulation, FortiGate encrypts and encapsulates the original packet before any fragmentation decision is made. The packet is then sent to the data layer for transmission, where FortiGate compares the size of the encrypted packet against the MTU of the parent interface (e.g., the WAN interface) - not the tunnel MTU. If fragmentation is required and allowed, FortiGate fragments the encrypted ESP packet into multiple packets.

topics.title: FortiManager FDS connectivity checking when error message is “HTTP/1.0 503 Service Unavailable” or “HTTP/1.0 504 Gateway Timeout” and why the web proxy must be in tunnel mode for FortiManager 7.4 and above
topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to verify FortiGuard FDS (AV/IPS and firmware images) connectivity from FortiManager when a web proxy is on the path to FortiGuard Servers. It describes the case when the FortiManager is used by FortiGates as local FDS, e.g. in air-gapped environment, and this FortiManager connecting to FortiGuard through an intermediate web proxy.Features an explanation of how to determine whether the proxy is well configured in tunnel or proxy mode, and why tunnel mode must be used on FortiManager 7.4 and above, as proxy settings for all FortiGuard services were consolidated under config system web-proxy in 7.4.0.ScopeFortiManager 7.4.7 and above.Applies to FortiManager acting as an FDS client and to FortiManager acting as a local FDS server for managed FortiGates.SolutionWhat has to be reachable.FortiManager, by default, accesses FDS for antivirus and attack updates through TCP/SSL port 443; firmware image updates also use TCP/443 to https://fds1.fortinet.com, and DNS resolution uses UDP/53.If a proxy sits between FortiManager and FDS, FortiManager can use:tcp port 443 to communicate with the proxy server in tunnel mode by defaultOr, in proxy mode, it then uses tcp port 80.Note: Allow the FortiGuard FQDNs dynamically rather than by IP: .fortinet.net, .fortinet.com, *.fortiguard.com, or the ISDB entry fortinet-fortiguard on the FortiGate side. The AV-IPS/firmware-image hosts per region setting are fds1.fortinet.com, usfds1.fortinet.com, eufds1.fortinet.com (unicast) and globalupdate.fortinet.net, usupdate.fortinet.net, euupdate.fortinet.net (anycast).Confirm the service itself is enabled.Starting with FortiManager 7.2.12, 7.4.8, 7.6.5 and above, the AV/IPS service must be explicitly enabled, as no objects are otherwise ever downloaded:config fmupdate service set avips enable endGUI equivalent: FortiGuard -> Settings -> AV/IPS service enabled for the relevant products. Additionally, confirm the product families to download are selected in "config fmupdate fds-setting": a family that is not listed will never have packages available.Identify the current proxy mode.If the only way for the FortiManager to reach FortiGuard servers on Internet is to go through a proxy, it must be configured to use this web-proxy.The command depends on the release:Version 7.4.1 and above:get system web-proxyVersion 7.4.0 and below:get fmupdate av-ips web-proxyOutputMeaningActionset mode tunnelFortiManager issues a CONNECT and runs TLS to FDS end to end over TCP/443Correct — go to step 4set mode proxyFortiManager issues a cleartext HTTP forward request to origin TCP/80Change to tunnel (step 6)set status disable with a proxy still enforced in the networkTraffic is intercepted upstreamAlign FMG config with the actual egress pathGUI equivalent: System Settings -> Advanced -> Misc Settings -> Use Web Proxy (Tunnel is the default).Baseline before any change:diagnose fmupdate update-status fds diagnose fmupdate view-serverlist fds diagnose fmupdate view-configure fds diagnose fmupdate fds-update-info diagnose fmupdate view-service-info fds“update-status fds” is the quickest health check to run before any change: UpdatedDate, LastSuccessDate, UpullStat, UpullErr and TotalObjNum show whether a poll has ever completed."TotalObjNum=0" with an empty LastSuccessDate means no object was ever received."view-serverlist fds" shows the FDS list.Capture the actual failure:diagnose debug application fdssvrd -1 diagnose debug enable diagnose fmupdate updatenow fdsAfter waiting for a few minutes:diagnose debug disablefdssvrd is the FDS server daemon debug process. Useful historical equivalents:diagnose fmupdate view-linkd-log fds diagnose fmupdate fds-dump fds-logInterpretation of the three failure signatures: Log lineCauseFixTLSv1 read fatal alert: protocol version -> FCP_CONN error, event=4 -> failed_reason=1(Connect error)FortiManager is offering TLSv1.x while FortiGuard expects TLSv1.2 or higher 26]config fmupdate fds-setting -> set fds-clt-ssl-protocol tlsv1.2Using proxy server : then POST http://fds1.fortinet.com:80/fdsupdate HTTP/1.0, Host: fds1.fortinet.com:80, and a proxy-generated HTTP/1.0 503/504 before any TLS handshakeWeb proxy is in proxy mode; the FDS service is not served anymore over cleartext HTTP on port 80 for IPS/AV updates and firmware updatesSwitch to tunnel mode (step 6) and have the proxy allow CONNECTProxy-Authorization: basic Og== (decodes to ":")Empty credentials are being sent to an authenticating proxy — no username/password is configured: check if proxy needs authenticationConfigure the service account, or exempt the FortiManager source IP on the proxyA successful poll looks like this in the linkd log:"Response=200" followed by "FCP_CONN cleanup ... SUCCESS!".Resolution: switch to tunnel mode."set port " is 1080 by default."set username ' '" is only necessary if the proxy authenticates.config system web-proxy set status enable set mode tunnel set address set port set username " " set password " " endTunnel mode is the do

topics.title: FortiAuthenticator authentication fails when using Red Hat LDAP server with password and OTP
topics.summary: Description Authentication fails when using a Red Hat LDAP server and requiring both password and OTP factors, resulting in an invalid password error. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate. Solution By default, FortiAuthenticator stores the Distinguished Name (DN) of imported remote LDAP users and uses the stored DN directly during LDAP bind operations. In load-balanced Red Hat LDAP environments where user DNs are not consistent across directory servers, the bind operation may fail, resulting in authentication issues when password and OTP authentication are used together. Authentication fails when a user attempts to authenticate using a Red Hat LDAP server with both password and OTP factors enabled. The event logs show the following error message: msg="Remote LDAP user authentication from (null) with FortiToken failed: invalid password" Authentication succeeds if only the password factor is used. This issue is resolved in FortiAuthenticator 6.6.3 and later. Run the following command in the Command Line Interface (CLI) to force FortiAuthenticator to search the LDAP directory for the username before performing the LDAP bind, instead of relying on the saved DN: diagnose authentication radius-force-ldap-user-lookup enable For more information about the command, see New command to search the LDAP directory . topics.title: Unable to complete FIDO token Authorization because token retry is not supported
topics.summary: Description The message "Unable to complete FIDO token Authorization because token retry is not supported. Please start the login process from the beginning" is received after user inputs FIDO token while being authenticated via SAML where FortiAuthenticator acts as the SAML IDP. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution A user receives the following message after inputting the FIDO token which is preceded by the SAML user login credentials: The following log entry is generated under Logging -> Log Access -> Logs , indicating that FortiAuthenticator is expecting FIDO token input and waiting for the user to provide it. cat="Event" subcat="Authentication" level="information" nas="example.com" action="Authentication" status="Pending" msg="Remote LDAP user authentication partially done, expecting fido token" user="user" Workaround The "FIDO-only" option can be selected instead of the "Password and FIDO" combination in the Authentication section of the Service Provider settings in FortiAuthenticator. Note: This issue affects the FortiAuthenticator 6.6.x and 8.0.x release branches. For the 6.6.x branch, the issue is fixed in the upcoming release, 6.6.12. A special build for 6.6.11 is also available.

topics.title: OSPF router LSA larger than the interface MTU on FortiSwitchOS prevents or flaps the neighbor adjacency
topics.summary: DescriptionA FortiSwitch running OSPF with a very large number of interfaces and areas advertises a router LSA (type 1) that exceeds the MTU of the OSPF link. The neighbor cannot accept the LSA, so the adjacency fails to form or repeatedly flaps.ScopeFortiSwitchOS 7.4.4 and 7.6.2 with OSPF over large L2 fabrics (hundreds of SVIs, tens of areas) - reported with 560 router-LSA links and 28 areas.SolutionOn the FortiSwitch and on the FortiGate peer, dump the self-originated router LSA and read its length against the OSPF interface MTU (default 1500).get router info ospf database self-originate get router info ospf database brief get router info ospf database router lsaUpgrade FortiSwitch to version 7.6.8 and above.

topics.title: NTLM and Kerberos usage in FortiAuthenticator
topics.summary: DescriptionA summary of NTLM and Kerberos use cases in FortiAuthenticator, as well as some known issues and workarounds to it.ScopeFortiAuthenticator.SolutionFortiAuthenticator uses NTLM and Kerberos in a few different instances. As NTLM is being increasingly deprecated, this can lead to some unexpected errors.FortiAuthenticator uses only NTLMv2 by default. It supports RC4, but defaults to AES. The encryption algorithm selection is determined by the server, so NTLMv2 servers should be configured to use AES only.FortiAuthenticator uses NTLM and/or Kerberos for the following:Domain JoinFSSOProxying NTLM trafficDomain joinFortiAuthenticator can be joined to a Windows Domain to allow for MS-CHAPv2 RADIUS authentication with a remote LDAP (Windows AD) server, and allow users to change their password securely via self-service portal or during the login process.The domain join process utilizes winbind, and uses NTLM and Kerberos both during joining and communicating with the domain controller.If NTLM is disabled, then the domain join and/or MS-CHAPv2 authentication may fail. Alternatives include:Using LDAPS instead of (or in addition to) joining FortiAuthenticator to the domainUsing RADSEC and PAP for remote LDAP authentication:LDAP authentication requires a clear-text password, which means using PAP between the RADIUS client and FortiAuthenticator.Using EAP-TTLS instead of EAP-MSCHAPv2:EAP-TTLS transmits a clear-text password inside an encrypted channel, allowing FortiAuthenticator to use LDAP rather than domain join authenticationUsing SAML authentication instead of RADIUS:SAML authentication occurs on a webpage hosted by FortiAuthenticator itself, so it receives the password as entered by the user on a secure HTTPS page, rather than the password being transmitted by a client device like FortiGate.There is a known issue in FortiAuthenticator 6.6.2 where MS-CHAPv2 authentication will fail if NTLMv1 is disabled. This is resolved in higher firmware versions, but NTLMv2 is still required.FSSOFortiAuthenticator uses NTLM and Kerberos in a few different instances for FSSO. These are:EventLog PollingWorkstation VerficiationKerberos SSO PortalOptionally, FortiClient Mobility AgentBoth EventLog Polling and Workstation Verification utilize NTLM so FortiAuthenticator can authenticate itself with the configured service account and access the user login information.The Kerberos SSO Portal is a portal hosted on FortiAuthenticator that, when accessed by a user, triggers Kerberos authentication. If the authentication is successful, FortiAuthenticator generates an FSSO session from it. More information on it can be found here: FortiAuthenticator Admininstration Guide: FSSO Web Services.NTLM authentication for FortiClient Mobility Agent can be enabled to require the the mobility agent to periodically perform an NTLM authentication against a known domain controller, proxied via the FortiAuthenticator. This is intended to protect against spoofed clients and domain controllers, as outlined in the Administration Guide: FortiClient SSO Mobility Agent.The following issues may occur with FSSO if NTLM is disabled:Event Log Polling will fail with errors like "NT_STATUS_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED" and "NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED".Workstation verification will fail with errors like "unable to connect".The only workaround currently available for Event Log Polling is to switch to DC Agent mode instead. For Workstation Verification, there is no workaround, though the only impact is that logins may grow stale and users show up as logged in in FSSO after they have already logged out from their workstations.As an alternative, the standalone Collector Agent can be used, as that supports Kerberos rather than NTLM for both Event Log Polling and Workstation Verification, but this requires some changes on FortiGate as well, as it will in effect use a different Collector Agent.Some useful articles:FortiAuthenticator with DC AgentEnforcing Kerberos instead of NTLM on FSSO Collector AgentWindows Server 2025 in particular is affected by the NTLM-related FSSO issues.Proxying NTLM TrafficFortiGate can authenticate users via NTLM, usually as part of explicit or transparent proxy authentication. FortiGate can either communicate directly with a domain controller to verify the user credentials, or proxy the NTLM traffic via an FSSO Collector Agent. FortiAuthenticator can forward these proxied NTLM requests the exact same way as a standalone Collector Agent.FortiAuthenticator itself does not perform any NTLM authentication when acting as a proxy, it simply forwards the NTLM traffic from FortiGate to the domain controller.If NTLM is disabled, then FortiGate should be configured to authenticate users in a different manner, such as via Kerberos.

topics.title: DMI on a WST-QSFP+SRB-CF 40GBASE-SR4 QSFP+ module
topics.summary: DescriptionOn a FortiSwitch unit, the WST-QSFP+SRB-CF 40GBASE-SR4 QSFP+ module is correctly detected and inserted. However, the module does not provide Digital Diagnostic Monitoring Interface (DMI) information.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionWhen checking the module status, the following message is displayed for the port where the module is installed:Port(port1) Module does not support Diagnostic Monitoring Interface (DMI).The get switch modules summary command shows that the module is detected successfully, but DMI information is unavailable:Portname State Type DMI Transceiver RX Vendor Part Number Serial Number port1 INSERT QSFP+ N 40G-Base-SR4 N/A +Fortinet WST-QSFP+SRB-CF TB50B70512The module identity information, including the vendor, part number, and serial number, is read correctly. The module is also recognized as a 40GBASE-SR4 QSFP+ transceiver.The WST-QSFP+SRB-CF 40GBASE-SR4 QSFP+ module does not support DMI, which is consistent with the CLI output. The module is correctly detected and its identification information is available. The absence of DMI telemetry is therefore expected behavior.

topics.title: FortiGate 6000 Chassis GUI widgets and network interface pages fail to load after upgrading to FortiOS version 7.6.8
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue where certain GUI components fail to load on FortiGate 6000 Chassis devices after upgrading to FortiOS version 7.6.8 GA.ScopeFortiGate 6k Chassis.SolutionThe issue affects both Global and VDOM dashboards, where CPU, Memory, and Session widgets remain unloaded. Additionally, the Network Interface pages under both Global and VDOM views fail to load. On the Firewall Policy page, it loads fine, but interface names are incorrectly displayed as [object Object], [object Object] instead of their actual names.On the Firewall Policy page:Steps to reproduce the issue.Log in to the GUI of the FortiGate 6000F running FortiOS version 7.6.8 GA.Navigate to the dashboard (System -> Dashboard).Observe that the Session, CPU, and Memory widgets keep loading indefinitely and never render.Navigate to System -> Network Interface.Observe that the page keeps loading indefinitely and never renders.The same issue is observed even in VDOM.The solution is to enable CSF on the FortiGate to fix the issue.config system csf set status enable set group-name fortinet endRoot cause:Starting with FortiOS version 7.6.4 GA, the SLBC GUI aggregator uses csfToken-based authentication, which requires CSF to be enabled for the GUI to function correctly. In FortiOS versions 7.2 and 7.4, the SLBC GUI aggregator uses admin-session-based authentication and does not depend on CSF being enabled.Starting from version 8.0, CSF can be kept disabled, and the GUI still works, as the CSF dependency is removed in version 8.0.

topics.title: High iowait (99%) on multiple CPU cores due to eMMC I/O blocking, resulting in processes becoming stuck in D state
topics.summary: DescriptionAn eMMC driver issue causes high I/O wait times, leading to unresponsive GUI access, SSL VPN drops, and DHCP drops, causing multiple processes to be in D state.ScopeFortiGate version 7.4.SolutionSymptoms.The following symptoms may occur on a FortiGate 60F, 70F, 100F, 70G, 71G, 90G, 120G in version 7.4.x:Intermittent SSL VPN tunnel drops.The Graphical User Interface (GUI) becomes unresponsive.High I/O wait (iowait) observed on one or more CPU cores (e.g., CPU3 stuck at 99% iowait).Multiple system daemons such as sslvpnd, miglogd, forticron, and hasync enter the D state (uninterruptible sleep).Process state: Multiple daemons in D state (Uninterruptible sleep).From diagnose sys top on FortiGate (99WA — 99% Wait):| Process | PID | State | CPU% | Mem% | CPU Affinity | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | miglogd | 2018 | D | 0.0 | 0.5 | 0 | | forticron | 2007 | D | 0.0 | 0.4 | 2 | | sslvpnd | 2020 | D | 0.0 | 0.3 | 0 | | updated | 2154 | D | 0.3 | 3 | | hasync | 2029 | D | 0.3 | 1 |All these daemons are blocked waiting for disk I/O to complete. No single process is consuming CPU; the CPU is idle but waiting on I/O.Additionally, when executing multiple commands on the FortiGate, the CLI becomes unresponsive or gets stuck, preventing the complete command output from being displayed.Output that can be collected during issue time:Multiple times (e.g., 5 times, 10 seconds apart) when the issue happens.diagnose hardware sysinfo memory diagnose sys flash list fnsysctl df diagnose sys filesystem last-modified-files diagnose sys filesystem open-files /data diagnose sys filesystem open-files /data2 diagnose sys filesystem lsof Root cause.A software issue in the eMMC driver causes an I/O bottleneck at the storage layer. This blocks disk-dependent processes from completing their operations, which results in the CPU entering a high iowait state. Because the SSL VPN, DHCP, and GUI rely on disk I/O for session files and page resources, they become unresponsive or drop connections. Resolution.Reboot the device. A reboot clears transient file system inconsistencies and restores normal disk I/O operation. Permanent resolution.The eMMC driver timeout issue is resolved in FortiOS version 7.4.15 and 7.6.10 (yet to be released).

topics.title: ZTNA TCP forwarding reports UTM block when backend server is unreachable
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen using ZTNA TCP Forwarding for RDP access, FortiGate may generate UTM and SSL event logs when the backend RDP server is unavailable or down.ScopeFortiGateSolutionWhen using ZTNA TCP forwarding to access the RDP service, the ZTNA traffic log may report the session as UTM Blocked even when no UTM security profile is configured on the corresponding proxy policy.The issue can occur when the backend server does not respond to the TCP connection initiated by the FortiGate ZTNA proxy or if the backend server is down.From the traffic logs, it can be seen that the UTM action is set to block.date=2026-09-22 time=13:36:27 eventtime=1790048187399475658 tz="+1000" logid="0005000024" type="traffic" subtype="ztna" level="notice" vd="root" srcip=192.168.50.110 srcport=51207 srcintf="port1" srcintfrole="undefined" dstcountry="Reserved" srccountry="Reserved" dstip=10.17.32.18 dstport=3389 dstintf="port1" dstintfrole="undefined" sessionid=2850416 service="RDP" proxyapptype="ztna-proxy" proto=6 action="timeout" policyid=4 policytype="proxy-policy" poluuid="14785d90-8710-51f1-ab0b-e7cf6160543b" policyname="Allow-RDP" appcat="unscanned" duration=11 gatewayid=1 vip="ZTNA-Proxy" vipincomingip=10.22.26.42 accessproxy="ZTNA-Proxy" clientdeviceid="289879DC54ED417F8DC3DAB80B24C965" clientdevicemanageable="manageable" clientdeviceems="FCTEMS0000XXXX" clientdevicetags="all_registered_clients/Logged-in-Domain/ad/Windows-11/CLASS_Low" clientcert="yes" emsconnection="online" wanin=0 rcvdbyte=0 wanout=0 lanin=2160 sentbyte=2160 lanout=40476 fctuid="289879DC54ED417F8DC3DAB80B24C965" utmaction="block" countssl=1 utmref=65468-98At the same time, if the SSL event logs are checked (msg="Connection failure due to record overflow occurred in SSL negotiation.(length:65)")date=2026-09-22 time=13:36:27 eventtime=1790048187399388524 tz="+1000" logid="1700062308" type="utm" subtype="ssl" eventtype="ssl-anomaly" level="information" vd="root" action="info" policyid=4 poluuid="14785d90-8710-51f1-ab0b-e7cf6160543b" policytype="proxy-policy" sessionid=2850416 service="HTTPS" profile="no-inspection" srcip=192.168.50.110 srcport=51207 srccountry="Reserved" dstip=10.17.32.18 dstport=3389 dstcountry="Reserved" srcintf="port1" srcintfrole="undefined" dstintf="port1" dstintfrole="undefined" srcuuid="aa62fbb0-63bd-51f1-915d-9cdaa0ab08f6" dstuuid="31d883a4-b084-51f1-4600-20697ca58fcc" proto=6 eventsubtype="handshake-failure" msg="Connection failure due to record overflow occurred in SSL negotiation.(length:65)" hostname="rdp.fortinet.com"Root Cause:For ZTNA proxy, the connection between FortiClient and FortiGate is always deep-inspected while establishing the ZTNA tunnel, regardless of whether a security profile is attached to the policyWhen the target server is down, the client's tunnel setup fails, and during this failure the SSL layer may detect data that is not valid TLS on the client connection and report it as an informational SSL anomaly event. SSL event logs are also UTM logs, so the ZTNA traffic log correlates them with the utmaction field. This does not mean traffic was blocked by a security profile. The session action itself (e.g., timeout) reflects the real cause: the server is unreachable.SSL anomaly events on this connection are controlled by the ssl-anomaly-log option of the ssl-ssh-profile, which is enabled by default in all profiles, including the built-in "no-inspection" profile. That is why the logs appear even when no profile is attached.To disable these logs, apply a profile with ssl-anomaly-log disabled to the ZTNA proxy policy:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit set ssl-anomaly-log disable next endAfter this, the SSL event logs and the UTM action field are no longer generated for these sessions.Hence, those event logs are expected in terms of ZTNA TCP forwarding.

topics.title: DHCP relay not working in private network mode on FortiExtender 511G
topics.summary: DescriptionDHCP packets are dropped by the modem when using FortiExtender 511G in private network mode, which prevents DHCP relay from functioning correctly.ScopeFortiExtender.SolutionSymptoms.When using a FortiExtender 511G in private network mode, DHCP relay fails to function because DHCP packets are dropped by the modem.The BGP connection is established through the LTE interface using an LTE modem. The BGP session is stable, and the FortiExtender is successfully receiving the expected routing information from its BGP peer, but DHCP packets are being dropped by the LTE modem and are not reaching the next-hop device. Environment details.FortiExtender:Model: FortiExtender 511G.Firmware: v7.6.5 build 520 (GA).LTE Modem:Vendor: Sierra Wireless.Model: EM9291.Modem Firmware: FEM_20_EM9291-25-01-01-NAM.Modem Revision: SWIX65C_02.17.08.00.Packet capture findings.Packet captures on the FortiExtender confirm that DHCP packets are transmitted through the LTE interface, but these packets do not reach the next-hop device, indicating that they are being dropped somewhere along the LTE modem forwarding path.Root cause.A software issue in the FortiExtender firmware causes DHCP packets to be dropped when operating in private network mode. Resolution.Update the FortiExtender 511G to FortiExtender version 8.0.1 GA build to resolve the issue.

topics.title: FortiManager unable to configure Agentless ZTNA portal authentication rules
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiManager fails to import or manually configure authentication rules for Agentless ZTNA portals when using form-based or SAML authentication schemes.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManager.SolutionSymptoms.When importing a configuration from a FortiGate or attempting to manually configure an authentication rule for an Agentless ZTNA portal via FortiManager, the following error message appears:"authentication rule",FAIL,"(name=agentless-portal-rule, oid=3945, reason=invalid value - prop[n/a]: can only use http protocol.)"========FGT configuration============= FGT-HUB (ztna_portal-saml) # show config authentication rule edit "ztna_portal-saml" set protocol ztna-portal set active-auth-method "saml-ztna" next end FGT-HUB# show authentication scheme saml-ztna config authentication scheme edit "saml-ztna" set method saml set saml-server "saml-ztna" set user-database "ldap_server" next endThis error occurs even when the protocol is correctly set to ztna-portal. Root cause.A software bug in FortiManager version 7.6.7 prevents the validation of the ztna-portal protocol for authentication rules when the authentication scheme is configured for form-based or SAML methods. This causes the system to incorrectly require the http protocol, leading to import failures or configuration errors. Resolution.The fix is currently not available and is expected in an upcoming GA release.

topics.title: FortiManager ISDB Extension Configuration Incorrectly Pushed to Other Devices Within the Same ADOM while doing policy install
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue in FortiManager 7.6.8 where internet-service-extension configurations defined for a specific FortiGate are incorrectly included in policy installation previews and pushed to other FortiGate devices within the same ADOM, even when the configuration is not explicitly defined for those devices.This appears to indicate that the ISDB extension configuration is being incorrectly applied across multiple devices within the same ADOM, rather than being restricted to the intended FortiGate.ScopeFortiManager 7.6.8.SolutionSymptomsThe config is done on the FortiManager CLI configuration for the device 'FGT-A' within ADOM-A, and it is intended to push it only to 'FGT-A'. The ISDB extension configuration was not initially present in the CLI configuration of the other FortiGate devices within the same ADOM, but FortiManager continued to include it in their policy installation previews.The configuration and policy packages were confirmed to be in sync with FortiManager. Configuration retrieval was also performed before attempting the installation, but the ISDB extension configuration still appeared in the installation preview.After the installation was completed on the affected FortiGate devices, the ISDB extension configuration also became visible in their respective CLI configurations on FortiManager. ResolutionThis issue is scheduled to be resolved in an upcoming GA release.

topics.title: FortiManager global policy assignment fails with no write permission error
topics.summary: Description An issue where global header policies fail to install on FortiGate devices from the Global ADOM when using the Automatically Install Policies to ADOM Devices option, resulting in a "No write permission" error. Scope FortiManager, FortiGate. Solution Symptoms When pushing global header policies from the Global ADOM to multiple ADOMs, the process fails at the end with the following error message: rootp:Firewall_Header_Policy_ADOM2 - no write permission This issue occurs specifically when the Automatically Install Policies to ADOM Devices option is used in the Global DB assignment. Pushing policies individually from the ADOM works as expected. Root cause A software issue exists in FortiManager 7.6.8 where the automatic installation of global policies fails to obtain the necessary write permissions for the target devices when Workspace Mode is enabled. Resolution Use one of the following workarounds to resolve the issue: Workaround 1 : Lock both Global and Local ADOMs This method allows the use of the automatic installation feature while maintaining Workspace Mode. Lock the target Local ADOM. Lock the Global ADOM. Select "Global DB" and then select "Assignment". Select the target ADOM and select "Assign + Automatically Install to device". Workaround 2 : Manual policy reinstallation If locking ADOMs is not feasible, manually trigger the installation for the affected devices. Select multiple target devices within the ADOM. Click "Reinstall Policy" to push the configuration. Workaround 3 : Disable Workspace Mode Disable Workspace Mode temporarily to allow the automatic installation to function. Disable Workspace Mode in FortiManager. Select "Global DB" and then select "Assignment". Select "Assign + Automatically Install" from the Global ADOM. topics.title: ACME certificate renewal is not automatically updated in FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how FortiGate devices using an ACME certificate do not send updated certificate details to FortiManager after renewal, causing FortiManager's certificate mapping to continue referencing an expired certificate.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManager.SolutionSymptoms.When ACME certificate renewals are enabled on a FortiGate, the certificate updates correctly on the local device, but FortiManager continues to reference the previous expired certificate in its mapping.FortiGate ACME Certificate Auto-Renewal Does Not Automatically Synchronize Updated Certificate and Private Key Details with FortiManager Root cause.The FortiGate does not send the updated certificate details to FortiManager even when auto update is enabled. Workaround.Until a permanent fix is applied, perform the following steps to manually update the certificate mapping: Retrieve the configuration from the FortiGate device to FortiManager.The issue is currently under investigation by the engineering team.

topics.title: Windows Autopilot / Intune OOBE provisioning through a FortiGate explicit web proxy
topics.summary: DescriptionWindows 11 Autopilot provisioning may fail intermittently when devices access Microsoft Intune services through a FortiGate explicit web proxy.During the Out-of-Box Experience (OOBE), devices may not yet have an authenticated user identity or an appropriate client certificate. As a result, they need an unauthenticated proxy policy that permits access to the Microsoft endpoints required for device provisioning and enrolment.Administrators commonly address this requirement by creating destination FQDN objects and web filtering exceptions based on Microsoft's published Intune endpoint list. However, this approach introduces several challenges:Microsoft service endpoints and associated IP addresses can change dynamically.Azure Front Door and other Microsoft services use shared CDN infrastructure.Static FQDN-based objects may not consistently represent the destinations required throughout provisioning.Internet Service Database (ISDB) classification and proxy policy matching may vary depending on FortiOS version.These conditions can cause intermittent connectivity failures during Autopilot provisioning, which may appear as authentication or MDM enrolment errors.ScopeProduct: FortiGate with explicit web proxy enabled.FortiOS: 7.2 and later, subject to feature and version compatibility.Environment: Windows 11 Autopilot and Microsoft Intune provisioning.SolutionCreate a dedicated proxy policy:Group the Autopilot build machines under a source address object and configure an unauthenticated proxy policy above the existing authenticated policies. Restrict access to the required Microsoft services without affecting other proxy rules.Verify the Internet Service Database (ISDB):Ensure the ISDB is up to date and record its version:diagnose autoupdate versions | grep "Internet" -A 6Configure Internet Service matching:Use supported Internet Service objects in config firewall proxy-policy instead of maintaining extensive FQDN lists. Identify the relevant Microsoft/Azure services, including AzureFrontDoor.MicrosoftSecurity where applicable, and verify coverage against the required Intune endpoints. Confirm the supported internet-service parameters for the FortiOS version.Address missing services:Where predefined ISDB entries do not cover required endpoints, consider custom Internet Service objects using the appropriate IP ranges, protocols and ports. Since the predefined ISDB is maintained by FortiGuard, submit missing or incorrect service classifications through the FortiGuard ISDB contact form.Avoid overlapping ISDB entries:Overlaps between custom and predefined Internet Services can cause unexpected service classification and policy mismatches. Review service precedence and validate the actual matched Internet Service ID.Troubleshoot policy matching:If traffic is still denied, collect WAD debugging for an affected build machine to identify the resolved Internet Service ID and matched proxy policy:diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose wad filter src diagnose wad debug enable category all diagnose wad debug enable level verbose diagnose debug enableStop debugging after reproducing the issue:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug resetClear the WAD filter and review the output for unexpected Internet Service classification or proxy policy selection.Related articles:Technical Tip: Using custom internet service in policyTechnical Tip: Updating Firewall Configurations to Include New Intune Network EndpointsTechnical Tip: Issues with matching Custom Internet Service (ISDB) object in the policyTechnical Tip: Using the 'diagnose wad debug' command to troubleshoot Explicit Web Proxy related issues

incidents.solution: FortiManagement Cloud 26.4.0 was released in early November. sources.title: FortiAuthenticator authentication fails when using Red Hat LDAP server with password and OTP
sources.summary: Description Authentication fails when using a Red Hat LDAP server and requiring both password and OTP factors, resulting in an invalid password error. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate. Solution By default, FortiAuthenticator stores the Distinguished Name (DN) of imported remote LDAP users and uses the stored DN directly during LDAP bind operations. In load-balanced Red Hat LDAP environments where user DNs are not consistent across directory servers, the bind operation may fail, resulting in authentication issues when password and OTP authentication are used together. Authentication fails when a user attempts to authenticate using a Red Hat LDAP server with both password and OTP factors enabled. The event logs show the following error message: msg="Remote LDAP user authentication from (null) with FortiToken failed: invalid password" Authentication succeeds if only the password factor is used. This issue is resolved in FortiAuthenticator 6.6.3 and later. Run the following command in t
sources.symptom: Authentication fails when using a Red Hat LDAP server and requiring both password and OTP factors, resulting in an invalid password error
sources.solution: By default, FortiAuthenticator stores the Distinguished Name (DN) of imported remote LDAP users and uses the stored DN directly during LDAP bind operations. In load-balanced Red Hat LDAP environments where user DNs are not consistent across directory servers, the bind operation may fail, resulting in authentication issues when password and OTP authentication are used together. Authentication fails when a user attempts to authenticate using a Red Hat LDAP server with both password and OTP factors enabled. The event logs show the following error message: msg="Remote LDAP user authentication from (null) with FortiToken failed: invalid password" Authentication succeeds if only the password factor is used. This issue is resolved in FortiAuthenticator 6.6.3 and later. Run the following command in the Command Line Interface (CLI) to force FortiAuthenticator to search the LDAP directory for the username before performing the LDAP bind, instead of relying on the saved DN: diagnose authentication radius-force-ldap-user-lookup enable For more information about the command, see New command to search the LDAP directory . incidents.solution: Recognize the symptom.After the upgrade, both units boot and the cluster passes traffic normally, but the secondary unit remains out-of-sync. With this information, the issue is isolated within the FortiManager database instead of connectivity with the managed device:FGFMs( -6917-- ): fgfm_keepalive_handler: old chksum: 03 6d db 79 ce 12 aa b8 76 20 f1 9e 9e 57 e9 1d, auto_ret rieve_pending = 0. FGFMs( --6917- ): fgfm_keepalive_handler: new chksum: 03 6d db 79 ce 12 aa b8 76 20 f1 9e 9e 57 e9 1d FGFMs( --6917- ): server:send: reply 200 request=keepalive cur_tun_serial=Check the related database:diagnose dvm device listThe output should show an empty list with no devices, despite there being an FGFM tunnel.Perform rollback:The rollback should be performed using a VM snapshot. If a snapshot is not available, perform the rollback using the following guide:Downgrading to previous firmware versionsCheck the device database again:Since the rollback to the last known good version was performed, the list should show devices. If not, it is possible the database is already corrupted and needs to be restored to an older, last known good ver

incidents.title: Explicit proxy returns 400 Bad Request when accessing HTTP2 websites after upgrade to 7.4.13
incidents.summary: DescriptionAn explanation and fix for a "400 Bad request" error received while accessing HTTP2 websites after upgrade to version 7.4.13.ScopeFortiOS 7.4.13.SolutionWhen accessing the HTTP2 websites, users might see below error "400 Bad Request".This issue happens when Deep Packet Inspection is applied for outbound traffic.This occurs while accessing HTTP2 websites through an explicit proxy policy with SSL inspection (DPI) enabled, specifically when an upstream FortiGate has strict-web-check enabled and the request contains multiple cookie headers.
incidents.symptom: An explanation and fix for a "400 Bad request" error received while accessing HTTP2 websites after upgrade to version 7.4.13
incidents.solution: When accessing the HTTP2 websites, users might see below error "400 Bad Request".This issue happens when Deep Packet Inspection is applied for outbound traffic.This occurs while accessing HTTP2 websites through an explicit proxy policy with SSL inspection (DPI) enabled, specifically when an upstream FortiGate has strict-web-check enabled and the request contains multiple cookie headers. HTTP/2 (per RFC 7540 8.1.2.5) permits the Cookie header to be split into multiple separate header fields, but strict mode rejected such requests as malformed, returning a connection error to the client.Enhancements to allow split cookies while strict-web-check is enabled will be implemented in future FortiOS 7.4.15.To verify, collect the output of the following debug commands:diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose wad debug enable level verbose diagnose wad debug display pid enable diagnose wad debug enable category all diagnose wad filter src diagnose wad filter dst diagnose debug enableReplace: with the client/source IP address. with the destination/server IP address.Disable debugging:diagnose wad debug clear diagnose wad filter clear diagnose debug disableThe following error can be obse Contournement : 1: Disable strict web checking.config web-proxy global set strict-web-check disable endWorkaround 2: Downgrade HTTP/2 via Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) manipulation.config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit " " set supported-alpn http1-1 endOnce the changes are made, users will be able to access the websites

incidents.title: Windows updates fails with enabled Forticlient
incidents.summary: Since last week we experiencing a lot of problems with Windows updates (mostly Windows 11, but there was one Windows 10 among them as well), specifically KB5040442. On about 10% of our Windows clients the update would start and go until 96% and stay there for 10-60 minutes, and then after a restart Windows would tell us that something did go wrong and it would reverse the update. This would require multiple restarts and anything in the order of 2-10h.

sources.summary: Since last week we experiencing a lot of problems with Windows updates (mostly Windows 11, but there was one Windows 10 among them as well), specifically KB5040442. sources.title: FortiClient Split Tunnel Not working for Windows Updates
sources.summary: we are using forticlient v7.4.7, today our users brought down their latest updates. Our VPN users are coming back down the VPN tunnel to download their updates, this maxed out our 1GB line. We have Windows updates set in the forticlient to go direct instead of using the tunnel. We also have the .exe and microsoft domain set to got direct. We are still seeing all this traffic coming down the VPN tunnel and then using our web filtering policies on the Fortigate to go out. Can anyone help with this?

incidents.summary: DescriptionHow to resolve the CLI error The entry is used by other 1 entries (Command fail. Return code -23) when attempting to delete an incorrect local wildcard certificate from a FortiGate before uploading the correct certificate.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionWhen an incorrect wildcard certificate is uploaded to a FortiGate, uploading the replacement certificate can fail if the existing entry conflicts with it. FortiOS prevents deleting any certificate that is still referenced by another configuration object (such as an SSL/SSH inspection profile, admin…
incidents.symptom: How to resolve the CLI error The entry is used by other 1 entries (Command fail. Return code -23) when attempting to delete an incorrect local wildcard certificate from a FortiGate before uploading the correct certificate
incidents.solution: When an incorrect wildcard certificate is uploaded to a FortiGate, uploading the replacement certificate can fail if the existing entry conflicts with it. FortiOS prevents deleting any certificate that is still referenced by another configuration object (such as an SSL/SSH inspection profile, admin GUI settings, or SSL VPN).Note: Make sure that the certificate is not applied to the configurationExample in GUI:Navigate to Security Profiles -> SSL/SSH Inspection.Edit the referenced profile.Change the CA Certificate or Server Certificate away from the incorrect wildcard certificate and select OK.Commands to delete the certificate:config vpn certificate local delete " " endUpload the new certificate and it should be uploaded successfully

incidents.solution: Symptoms:A scheduled firmware upgrade is displayed in the FortiGate GUI under System -> Firmware & Registration, even though automatic firmware upgrade is disabled under FortiGuard settings.When checking the FortiGuard configuration, the following observations may be made:Automatic firmware upgrade is disabled under 'config system fortiguard'The FortiGate is not a member of Security FabricFederated upgrade is initialized with the source configured as forced-upgrade, similar to the following configuration example:config system federated-upgrade set status initialized set source forced-upgrade set upgrade-id 4 set ha-reboot-controller "FGTAWSXXXXXXXXXXXX" config known-ha-members edit "FGTAWSXXXXXXXXXXXX" next edit "FGTAWSXXXXXXXXXXXX" next end endAttempting to modify the federated-upgrade status directly results in the following error:Federated upgrade cannot be configured directly. Please use 'execute federated-upgrade ...' to configure. object set operator error, -39 discard the setting Command fail. Return code -39Additionally, executing the recommended cancellation command fails with the following error:The existing upgrades cannot be cancelled. Command fail. Return code 1Root ca

incidents.title: IPS error condition when handling high volumes of application traffic
incidents.summary: DescriptionAn error condition in the Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) engine occurs when processing high volumes of application traffic, leading to potential traffic impact.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptomsThe IPS engine may crash when the FortiGate handles high volumes of application traffic. This crash results in an impact on traffic inspection.Root CauseA bug (Bug ID 1273729) exists in FortiOS 8.0.0 that causes an error condition in the ipsengine during the processing of high volumes of application traffic.
incidents.symptom: An error condition in the Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) engine occurs when processing high volumes of application traffic, leading to potential traffic impact
incidents.solution: SymptomsThe IPS engine may crash when the FortiGate handles high volumes of application traffic. This crash results in an impact on traffic inspection.Root CauseA bug (Bug ID 1273729) exists in FortiOS 8.0.0 that causes an error condition in the ipsengine during the processing of high volumes of application traffic. This issue specifically affects environments using nturbo. It does not affect VM environments or configurations where only IPS is used without Application Control Contournement : To check the IPS crash logdiagnose debug crashlog readDisable cp-accel-mode and np-accel-mode in global IPS settings.config ips global set cp-accel-mode none set np-accel-mode none end Resolution Upgrade the FortiGate to FortiOS 7.4.12, 7.6.7, 8.0.1, or a later version to resolve this issue.Resolved Issues 8.0.1Resolved Issues 7.6.7Resolved Issues 7.4.12

incidents.title: Unable to bypass critical vulnerability alert in FortiGate GUI
incidents.summary: DescriptionA critical vulnerability warning screen in FortiOS 7.6.7 prevents users from accessing the FortiGate GUI. When clicking the Skip button, the action is not processed correctly, and instead of proceeding with the login, the user is logged out.ScopeFortiGateSolutionWhen accessing the FortiGate GUI on FortiOS 7.6.7, an alert screen appears displaying the message "Installed Firmware Contains a Critical Vulnerability."The screen provides the option "Skip upgrade & I understand the risk" to allow users to proceed with the login without upgrading…
incidents.symptom: A critical vulnerability warning screen in FortiOS 7.6.7 prevents users from accessing the FortiGate GUI. When clicking the Skip button, the action is not processed correctly, and instead of proceeding with the login, the user is logged out
incidents.solution: When accessing the FortiGate GUI on FortiOS 7.6.7, an alert screen appears displaying the message "Installed Firmware Contains a Critical Vulnerability."The screen provides the option "Skip upgrade & I understand the risk" to allow users to proceed with the login without upgrading the firmware.However, clicking this button does not proceed with the login as expected. Although the warning message instructs users to acknowledge and accept the risk with the following statement, "To continue logging in without upgrading, please acknowledge and be willing to accept the risk of doing so.", the acknowledgement is not properly processed, and the user is redirected back to the login screen instead of gaining access to the FortiGate GUI.The prompt blocks the GUI session in the following browsers where the defect appears , no login setting bypasses it.Tested across multiple browser sessions, and the button is unresponsive in all three:Google Chrome (standard mode)Google Chrome (Incognito mode)Microsoft EdgeCLI access via SSH is still working normally Contournement : Log in from Firefox. The acknowledgement is processed and the session reaches dashboard

incidents.title: FortiZTP provisioning of FortiGate-VM to FortiManager fails with S-Series and FortiFlex Flex-VM licenses because auto-join-forticloud is disabled
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiZTP depends on the auto-join feature, which requires auto-join-forticloud to be enabled and config system central-management set to type fortiguard for provisioning to function.On FortiOS installations using a FortiGate-VMUL-S (S-Series Subscription) license, and on Flex-VM licenses.ScopeFortigate.FortiZTP provisioning target: on-premises FortiManager.FortiGate-VM license families: FortiGate-VMUL-S (S-Series Subscription), FortiFlex Flex-VM.Hypervisor: VMware Workstation.
incidents.symptom: FortiZTP depends on the auto-join feature, which requires auto-join-forticloud to be enabled and config system central-management set to type fortiguard for provisioning to function.On FortiOS installations using a FortiGate-VMUL-S (S-Series Subscription) license, and on Flex-VM licenses
incidents.solution: BackgroundFortiZTP requires a FortiGate model or license that supports the zero-touch provisioning (autojoin) feature, and FortiOS 5.2.2 or later. A valid certificate with the serial number as CN, signed by Fortinet, is also required for FortiZTP to function.For non-zero-touch models, FortiZTP supports one-touch provisioning, and DHCP must be configured on the chosen port.A FG-VM01 or FG-VM01V license is recommended for FortiGate-VM deployments because the autojoin feature is enabled by default on those licenses.SymptomsOn a FortiOS installation with a FortiGate-VMUL-S license, the following defaults are present:config system fortiguard show auto-join-forticloud endconfig system central-management show endThe output shows auto-join-forticloud disabled and type set to none. The none option means no central management. With those two defaults, the device does not send traffic to FortiGate Cloud, so FortiZTP provisioning to FortiManager cannot proceed.Resolution 1: enable autojoin manually before provisioningRun the following so that the FortiGate-VM can reach FortiGate Cloud, then restart the device and confirm that it is sending traffic to FortiGate CloudEnable auto-join for FortiZT

incidents.title: FortiClient EMS Deployment Failure on macOS 27 – Unsupported Operating System Error
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiClient EMS may fail to deploy FortiClient to devices running macOS 27 and display an "Unsupported Operating System" error message.ScopeFortiClient/EMS.SolutionSymptomsWhen attempting to deploy FortiClient 7.4.8 to endpoints running macOS 27.2.1 (26B131), the FortiClient EMS console displays the error message "Unsupported Operating System". This prevents the automatic deployment of the software to the affected MacBooks.
incidents.symptom: FortiClient EMS may fail to deploy FortiClient to devices running macOS 27 and display an "Unsupported Operating System" error message
incidents.solution: SymptomsWhen attempting to deploy FortiClient 7.4.8 to endpoints running macOS 27.2.1 (26B131), the FortiClient EMS console displays the error message "Unsupported Operating System". This prevents the automatic deployment of the software to the affected MacBooks. Root causeFortiClient EMS does not have full support for macOS 27, which leads to the operating system being identified as unsupported during the deployment process. Resolution Contournement : If immediate deployment is required, perform a manual installation on the endpoint:Download the FortiClient .dmg installation file.Run the installer manually on the macOS 27 device. Permanent fixUpgrade FortiClient EMS to version 7.4.9 or higher. Support for macOS 27 is included in this release to resolve the deployment issue

incidents.symptom: How to solve FortiClient error code is 2502 during installation
incidents.solution: If you encounter the following error when installing FortiClient:"The installer has encountered an unexpected error installing this package. This may indicate a problem with this package. The error code is 2502"This issue occurs when installing, updating, or uninstalling the program because the system's temporary folder lacks write permissions.The two most common solutions are:Run the installer with administrator privileges (Quick fix):Since .msi files do not display a direct "Run as administrator" option, you can force the process via the console:Press the "Windows + X" keys and select Terminal (Administrator) or open the Command Prompt (as Administrator).Type msiexec /i (with a space at the end), drag the FortiClient installer file into the console window so that its full path is inserted, and press Enter.(If you are uninstalling, you can open Task Manager, end the explorer.exe process, go to File > Run new task, type explorer.exe, and check the box "Create this task with administrative privileges" before proceeding with the uninstallation.)Fix permissions for the "Temp" folder:If the previous method fails, the installer may still be blocked from writing temporary files in Window

incidents.title: Technical Tip: Authentication failure after migrating to FortiGate using FortiConverter
incidents.summary: Description This article describes an issue when it is not possible to login to FortiGate after restoring a converted configuration file from FortiConverter. Scope FortiGate. Solution The converted configuration file does not have the same administrator credentials. To find the new credentials, go to the FortiConverter ticket at https://service.forticonverter.com and select 'Instructions for the Converted Config file'.

incidents.symptom: FortiGate users may encounter authentication failures in IPsec IKEv2 remote access VPNs when combining the EMS trust store with specific peer group validation settings
incidents.solution: Symptoms.After upgrading to FortiOS version 7.6.7 or FortiOS version 7.6.8, FortiClient reports 'Authentication failed' during IPsec IKEv2 VPN connection attempts. The issue occurs when the following configuration is used:set cert-trust-store emsset peertype peergrpset peergrp Debug logs for fnbamd show the following error:__quick_check_peer-CA does not match. 'EMS_Client_Validator' check ret:badThis results in the failure message: 'certificate validation before eap failed'.Root cause.In FortiOS version 7.6.7 and above, IKE delegates peer certificate validation to fnbamd. When cert-trust-store ems is configured, the certificate chain is built from the EMS CA cache. These certificates have an empty cmdb_name. If mandatory-ca-verify is enabled in the peer object, fnbamd compares the local CMDB CA name against this empty name, causing a mismatch and authentication failure.Resolution.Allow the EMS trust store to handle certificate trust and remove the explicit user peer reference from the Phase 1 configuration.Enter the IPsec Phase 1 interface configuration:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit Change the peer type to any to remove the peer group restriction:set peertype anyEnsure the

incidents.title: Administrator SSO authentication fails after upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.8.SolutionAfter upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential. The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login…
incidents.symptom: After upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account
incidents.solution: After upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential. The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login for FortiGate administrators with Entra ID acting as SAML IdP.Security Fabric SSO with root FortiGate as IdP, for example see Configuring single-sign-on in the Security Fabric. Confirmed not affected:VPN user SSO authentication.Other FortiOS versions including FortiOS 7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2.Local administrator authentication.Remote administrator authentication using RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+.While access to the FortiGate from FortiManagement Cloud (FortiGate Cloud) is technically not affected, SSO authentication to the FortiGate is still not possible over this management path. Issue matching:To confirm the issue, check the FortiOS crashlog for a matching "FORTISM Violation" from the time of the access attempt. This can be done by accessing the FortiGate using a local administrator account and executing diagnose debug crashlog read | Contournement : At this time, the only available workaround is to use another administrator authentication method.If no suitable administrator account exists, console access to a physical device can be used to recover access, see Technical Tip: Boot the backup firmware and config via console.If the device is centrally managed by FortiManager or a valid FortiManagement Cloud subscription, an administrator can be added. See Recover access to FortiGate via FortiManagement Cloud. Resolution:A fix for this issue exists and is planned for inclusion in FortiOS 7.6.9, currently expected to release in late November 2026. FortiOS firmware release schedules are subject to change without notice. Related article:Create a "break glass" admin account on the FortiGate as a backup for remote authentication/MFA (Recommendation)

incidents.title: FortiGate logs show ICAP connection errors and client sessions are dropped during file uploads because the ICAP connection queue becomes full.
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiGate logs show ICAP connection errors and client sessions are dropped during file uploads because the ICAP connection queue becomes full.ScopeFortiGate, FortiProxy.SolutionSymptomsWhen downloading or uploading files through a FortiGate configured with an ICAP profile, the webpage may take a long time to load and eventually time out. The FortiGate logs display the following error message:msg="ICAP connection error.
incidents.symptom: FortiGate logs show ICAP connection errors and client sessions are dropped during file uploads because the ICAP connection queue becomes full
incidents.solution: SymptomsWhen downloading or uploading files through a FortiGate configured with an ICAP profile, the webpage may take a long time to load and eventually time out. The FortiGate logs display the following error message:msg="ICAP connection error. Client session dropped" reason="ICAP server disconnected"WAD debug logs may show the following warning:wad_icap_srv_conn_on_error :516 ICAP ..(nil):(:0->x.x.x.x:1344)... wad icap port cancel/error Root causeThe issue occurs when the ICAP connection queue becomes full. The max-connection limit is distributed across all WAD workers in a first-come, first-served pattern. If the ICAP server takes too long to respond or fails to send a response on time, connections remain occupied. Once the available connections for the workers are exhausted, subsequent requests are queued. If these requests exceed the queue timeout, the FortiGate terminates the session and logs a port cancel error.Additionally, we can observe that the source port is displayed as (nil) in the debug output, indicating that the source-side socket/connection reference is NULL in this error-handling context. Re solution Increase the maximum number of connections allowed for the ICAP

This occurs for requests such as CMDB and event-log reads.Example failed requests:GET /forticloudapi/v1/fgt/ /api/v2/cmdb/system/global?account_id= GET /forticloudapi/v1/fgt/…
incidents.symptom: FortiOS API requests proxied through FortiGate Cloud fail with a version not supported error when targeting devices running FortiOS version 8.0.0
incidents.solution: Symptoms.When using the FortiGate Cloud API to proxy requests to a FortiGate device running FortiOS version 8.0.0, the API returns an HTTP 500 error. This occurs for requests such as CMDB and event-log reads.Example failed requests:GET /forticloudapi/v1/fgt/ /api/v2/cmdb/system/global?account_id= GET /forticloudapi/v1/fgt/ /api/v2/log/forticloud/event/system?rows=1&account_id= The response body contains the following error:error=internal_error, error_code=-1, error_description="version not supported"Root cause.The FortiGate Cloud API proxy does not support the API versioning used by FortiOS version 8.0.0 devices. incidents.summary: DescriptionLDAP authentication over LDAPS (TCP 636) fails with certificate verification errors due to an incorrect Root CA certificate installed on the FortiGate.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptomsLDAP authentication over LDAPS (TCP 636) fails. You may see an error message on the GUI, and debug logs show the following error:[1686] __verify_cb-Cert error 20, unable to get local issuer certificate. Depth 0. Subject '/CN= ' [1374] __ldap_tcps_connect-tcps_connect( ) failed: ssl_connect() failed: 167772294 (error:0A000086:SSL routines::certificate verify…
incidents.symptom: LDAP authentication over LDAPS (TCP 636) fails with certificate verification errors due to an incorrect Root CA certificate installed on the FortiGate
incidents.solution: SymptomsLDAP authentication over LDAPS (TCP 636) fails. You may see an error message on the GUI, and debug logs show the following error:[1686] __verify_cb-Cert error 20, unable to get local issuer certificate. Depth 0. Subject '/CN= ' [1374] __ldap_tcps_connect-tcps_connect( ) failed: ssl_connect() failed: 167772294 (error:0A000086:SSL routines::certificate verify failed). Root causeThe issue occurs because the Root CA certificate installed on the FortiGate does not match the CA that signed the LDAP server certificate. Starting from FortiOS 7.4.4, the LDAPS/STARTTLS server certificate issuer is enforced, meaning the correct Root CA must be present in the certificate store to validate the server certificate.There can be more than one similar root CA certificate on the domain controller server with the same CN. In a scenario like this, a user might end up importing the wrong CA on the FortiGate. Re solution Verify that the Root CA certificate installed on the FortiGate is the exact issuer of the LDAP server certificate by comparing the Subject Key Identifier (SKI) and Authority Key Identifier (AKI). Verify certificate identifiersOpen the LDAP server certificate on the Domain Control

incidents.title: BGP not supported within VRF
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes FortiSwitch BGP support within a VRF.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionBased on the official Fortinet documentation for FortiSwitchOS, it is necessary to distinguish between general BGP support and BGP support within a VRF.Fortinet's Feature Matrix identifies both BGP and VRF as supported features on applicable FortiSwitch models. However, when examining routing protocol integration with VRF, Fortinet explicitly identifies OSPF VRF support as a supported capability.Fortinet's official Feature Matrix confirms that OSPF…
incidents.symptom: This article describes FortiSwitch BGP support within a VRF
incidents.solution: Based on the official Fortinet documentation for FortiSwitchOS, it is necessary to distinguish between general BGP support and BGP support within a VRF.Fortinet's Feature Matrix identifies both BGP and VRF as supported features on applicable FortiSwitch models. However, when examining routing protocol integration with VRF, Fortinet explicitly identifies OSPF VRF support as a supported capability.Fortinet's official Feature Matrix confirms that OSPF supports VRF.There is no equivalent documented BGP VRF support entry in the FortiSwitchOS Feature Matrix.Although BGP and VRF are individually supported features, the available official Fortinet documentation does not establish support for running BGP within a VRF on FortiSwitch.Therefore, BGP over VRF is not supported.Recommendation:If dynamic routing within a VRF is required, OSPF is the routing protocol explicitly documented by Fortinet for this functionality.Related document:FortiSwitch Feature Matrix

incidents.symptom: Users cannot access servers using hostnames following a FortiGate power failure and reboot, although access via IP address remains functional
incidents.solution: Symptoms:After a FortiGate power failure and subsequent reboot, users experience the following issues:Unable to access servers using hostnames.Servers remain accessible when using the IP address directly.The environment uses SD-WAN. Cause:The issue is typically caused by a failure in DNS resolution or the loss of DNS cache/settings following an unexpected power cycle, preventing the translation of hostnames to IP addresses. Solution:Verify and restore DNS functionality on the FortiGate to ensure hostnames resolve correctly.Verify that the FortiGate can resolve external and internal hostnames using the command line interface. This can be checked using the following:show system dns execute ping www.fortinet.com execute ping In case the first step does not work, perform a packet capture and check the query-response from the DNS server.diagnose sniffer packet any "port 53" 4 O lIf DNS over TLS (DOT) is configured, use:diagnose sniffer packet any "tcp port 853" 4 0 lCheck the DNS server configuration to ensure the correct DNS servers are assigned and reachable from FortiGate.If the DNS settings are incorrect, update them using the document Important DNS CLI commands.Clear the DNS cache

incidents.symptom: A local-in policy configured to restrict IPsec VPN access to authorized IP addresses may fail to block unauthorized traffic if an existing IKE cache entry forces session creation
incidents.solution: Symptoms.A local-in policy is configured to allow IKE traffic only from specific authorized IP addresses. Initially, the policy correctly drops traffic from unauthorized IPs. However, after some time, unauthorized IPs can successfully establish a VPN tunnel because the traffic is no longer evaluated against the local-in policy, as it matches an existing session. Root cause.The IKE cache of the VPN forces the FortiGate to create a session for the incoming traffic. When a session already exists in the session table or is cached, the device may bypass the local-in policy evaluation for subsequent packets of that flow, allowing the tunnel to establish despite the restriction policy. Resolution.To resolve this issue and ensure the local-in policy is strictly enforced, clear the existing VPN tunnels and the session list to remove the cached entries.Flush the IPsec tunnels to clear the IKE cache.Clear the session table to remove any active sessions associated with the unauthorized IP addresses.Run the following commands in the CLI to clear the sessions and tunnels. Execute the clear with filter to clear a specific VPN tunnel.diagnose vpn ike gateway cleardiagnose sys session clear

incidents.title: High memory usage in the IKE daemon with dial-up IKEv2 VPN in FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.summary: DescriptionIn FortiOS 7.6, the Internet Key Exchange daemon (iked) can exhibit continuous monotonic resident memory growth under dial-up IKEv2 VPN deployments using dynamic EAP authentication with certificate validation. Although dial-up users disconnect normally during non-business hours, resident memory occupied by the iked process does not decrease. Over multiple days of operation, memory usage can climb to several hundred megabytes, eventually consuming a significant percentage of system RAM and potentially contributing to memory conserve…
incidents.symptom: In FortiOS 7.6, the Internet Key Exchange daemon (iked) can exhibit continuous monotonic resident memory growth under dial-up IKEv2 VPN deployments using dynamic EAP authentication with certificate validation. Although dial-up users disconnect normally during non-business hours, resident memory occupied by the iked process does not decrease. Over multiple days of operation, memory usage can climb to several hundred megabytes, eventually consuming a significant percentage of system RAM and potentially contributing to memory conserve mode.This symptom occurs specifically in environments running pure IKEv2 where dynamic dial-up tunnels handle frequent user connection setups, re-authentications, and Phase 2 Security Association (SA) rekeys. Internal daemon metrics reveal an accumulation of certificate structures (cfg.cert), cryptographic memory allocations (crypto.mem), and message buffers (vmbuf) that remain allocated in the daemon heap
incidents.solution: When dial-up clients establish IKEv2 sessions using EAP and certificate authentication, the iked daemon dynamically allocates memory structures to validate certificates, store peer identifiers, negotiate child security associations, and track connection state.In FortiOS 7.6.8, certain de-allocation paths during session termination fail to decrement reference counts on certificate structures and cryptographic context blocks. As a result, even when active user sessions terminate and the number of connected tunnels drops, the allocated memory is retained within the daemon heap rather than returned to the operating system. Over time, high volumes of dynamic user logins, disconnections, and automatic Phase 2 SA re-keys cause steady memory accumulation.Diagnostic steps:To confirm whether your FortiGate is experiencing this specific condition, perform the following diagnostic checks from the CLI:Identify iked resident memory consumption:diagnose sys top-mem 20Review the output to locate /bin/iked. incidents.title: SD-WAN IPv6 health-check failure after dynamic DHCPv6 prefix change (lnkmtd errno 99)
incidents.summary: DescriptionOn a FortiGate configured with an SD-WAN IPv6 Performance SLA using automatic source selection (set source6 ::), the health-check may fail permanently (100% packet loss) after the WAN interface acquires a new IPv6 prefix via DHCPv6.While manual ICMPv6 pings from the CLI succeed and regular IPv6 traffic forwards normally over the new address, the link-monitor daemon (lnkmtd) continues attempting to bind probe sockets to the old, removed IPv6 address.
incidents.symptom: On a FortiGate configured with an SD-WAN IPv6 Performance SLA using automatic source selection (set source6 ::), the health-check may fail permanently (100% packet loss) after the WAN interface acquires a new IPv6 prefix via DHCPv6.While manual ICMPv6 pings from the CLI succeed and regular IPv6 traffic forwards normally over the new address, the link-monitor daemon (lnkmtd) continues attempting to bind probe sockets to the old, removed IPv6 address. This causes a local socket bind failure with Linux kernel errno 99 (EADDRNOTAVAIL), preventing health-check probes from being sent out the interface
incidents.solution: When an SD-WAN IPv6 health-check is set to automatic source selection (set source6 ::), lnkmtd binds an ICMPv6 raw socket to the interface's primary global IPv6 address.When an upstream ISP router or modem reboots and allocates a new IPv6 prefix via DHCPv6, the FortiGate updates the interface IP. However, lnkmtd does not dynamically update its cached socket binding upon receiving the address change. The daemon retains the previous address in its monitor structure and attempts to bind subsequent probe sockets to that address.Because the old address no longer exists on the interface, the kernel rejects the socket creation with "errno 99" (Cannot assign requested address). As a result, no ICMPv6 probes leave the FortiGate.To identify this condition, enable link-monitor debugging on the FortiGate CLI:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug application link-monitor -1 diagnose debug enableWhen the issue is present, the console outputs:lnkmtd::lnkmt_addr_mode_bind6(72): ---> lnkmtd: fails to bind source IP (2001:db8:1::2) to intf(wan), errno(99) lnkmtd::ping_create_socket(468): ---> Fail to create ping socket for monitor(Google_DNS_IPv6-2-VIRTUAL_WAN_L Contournement : Toggling the health-check (set probe-packets disable/enable) does not release the stale socket. Use one of the following methods to restore monitoring:Method 1: Restart lnkmtd (Recommended).fnsysctl killall lnkmtdThe daemon restarts in seconds, detects the current DHCPv6 interface address, binds new sockets, and restores the health-check immediately without dropping active traffic sessions.Method 2: Re-bind source address via CLI.Temporarily define the new source address explicitly in the health-check, then return it to automatic:config system sdwan config health-check edit " " set source6 next end endAfter the health-check recovers, unset the parameter:config system sdwan config health-check edit " " unset source6 next end endTo verify that the health-check link state returns to alive:diagnose sys sdwan health-check status
