sources.solution: When an SD-WAN IPv6 health-check is set to automatic source selection (set source6 ::), lnkmtd binds an ICMPv6 raw socket to the interface's primary global IPv6 address.When an upstream ISP router or modem reboots and allocates a new IPv6 prefix via DHCPv6, the FortiGate updates the interface IP. However, lnkmtd does not dynamically update its cached socket binding upon receiving the address change. The daemon retains the previous address in its monitor structure and attempts to bind subsequent probe sockets to that address.Because the old address no longer exists on the interface, the kernel rejects the socket creation with "errno 99" (Cannot assign requested address). As a result, no ICMPv6 probes leave the FortiGate.To identify this condition, enable link-monitor debugging on the FortiGate CLI:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug application link-monitor -1 diagnose debug enableWhen the issue is present, the console outputs:lnkmtd::lnkmt_addr_mode_bind6(72): ---> lnkmtd: fails to bind source IP (2001:db8:1::2) to intf(wan), errno(99) lnkmtd::ping_create_socket(468): ---> Fail to create ping socket for monitor(Google_DNS_IPv6-2-VIRTUAL_WAN_L Contournement : Toggling the health-check (set probe-packets disable/enable) does not release the stale socket. Use one of the following methods to restore monitoring:Method 1: Restart lnkmtd (Recommended).fnsysctl killall lnkmtdThe daemon restarts in seconds, detects the current DHCPv6 interface address, binds new sockets, and restores the health-check immediately without dropping active traffic sessions.Method 2: Re-bind source address via CLI.Temporarily define the new source address explicitly in the health-check, then return it to automatic:config system sdwan config health-check edit " " set source6 next end endAfter the health-check recovers, unset the parameter:config system sdwan config health-check edit " " unset source6 next end endTo verify that the health-check link state returns to alive:diagnose sys sdwan health-check status

incidents.title: Missing FortiSASE dynamic ZTNA tag IPs on FortiGate SPA Hub
incidents.summary: DescriptionOn a FortiGate configured with a FortiClient EMS connector using Share all FortiClients (share-all: enabled), such as an on-premises Secure Private Access (SPA) Hub terminating tunnels from FortiSASE, remote user IP addresses may intermittently disappear from dynamic firewall address objects (diagnose firewall dynamic list).Although the remote FortiClient endpoint remains connected, compliant, and correctly tagged on FortiClient EMS, the FortiGate removes the client's VPN IP from the dynamic ZTNA address table.
incidents.symptom: On a FortiGate configured with a FortiClient EMS connector using Share all FortiClients (share-all: enabled), such as an on-premises Secure Private Access (SPA) Hub terminating tunnels from FortiSASE, remote user IP addresses may intermittently disappear from dynamic firewall address objects (diagnose firewall dynamic list).Although the remote FortiClient endpoint remains connected, compliant, and correctly tagged on FortiClient EMS, the FortiGate removes the client's VPN IP from the dynamic ZTNA address table. As a result, firewall policies referencing the dynamic posture tag silently deny access to internal resources until the user disconnects and reconnects with a different IP address, or until the FortiClient NAC daemon (fcnacd) is restarted
incidents.solution: When FortiClient EMS is configured with Share all FortiClients enabled, the FortiGate receives endpoint records globally without interface bindings (VDOM -1 in shared memory). The FortiGate link and endpoint control daemon (fcnacd) stores these records in internal shared memory (ec-shm) and populates the dynamic address object tables used by the firewall.In environments where dynamic VPN IP addresses are frequently reassigned, such as remote users connecting through FortiSASE Secure Internet Access (SIA) PoPs, a new user can receive a VPN IP recently released by another endpoint. In FortiOS 7.6.8 and earlier, fcnacd does not track reverse IP-to-UID ownership for share-all endpoints. When a delayed offline or disconnect event from the previous IP leaseholder arrives, fcnacd processes the deletion and removes the IP mapping from the dynamic firewall address table, inadvertently evicting the active compliant user.To verify whether an IP address is missing from the dynamic table:Check the dynamic address list:diagnose firewall dynamic listLocate the EMS dynamic tag object (for example, EMS1_ZTNA_Corporate_Tag). Check whether the active client VPN IP (for example, 100.64.1.12) is absent Contournement : To restore missing IP mappings without rebooting the FortiGate or interrupting user traffic, restart the FortiClient NAC daemon:fnsysctl killall fcnacdRestarting fcnacd flushes the internal endpoint shared memory cache (ec-shm) and triggers an immediate resynchronization with FortiClient EMS. The daemon re-evaluates all active compliant endpoints and restores all missing IP addresses to the dynamic address table within seconds.Verify that compliant endpoint IP addresses have repopulated:diagnose firewall dynamic listNote: This behavior is resolved in FortiOS 8.0.3 and FortiOS 7.6.9. On earlier releases in environments with high IP churn, an Automation Stitch executing "fnsysctl killall fcnacd" on a periodic schedule (such as daily off-peak) can be used to prevent stale cache entries until the firmware is upgraded

incidents.title: DHCP relay failure in FortiOS 7.4.4 due to DHCP option 54 behavior change
incidents.summary: DescriptionDHCP relay requests fail to reach the DHCP server in FortiOS 7.4.4 due to a change in relay behavior regarding Option 54.ScopeFortiNAC, FortiGate.SolutionSymptomsDHCP clients are unable to obtain an IP address. Packet captures show that the DHCP server sends a DHCPOFFER and the client responds with a DHCPREQUEST, but the DHCPREQUEST packet never reaches the DHCP server. Root causeStarting from FortiOS 7.4.4, the DHCP relay behavior changed.
incidents.symptom: DHCP relay requests fail to reach the DHCP server in FortiOS 7.4.4 due to a change in relay behavior regarding Option 54
incidents.solution: SymptomsDHCP clients are unable to obtain an IP address. Packet captures show that the DHCP server sends a DHCPOFFER and the client responds with a DHCPREQUEST, but the DHCPREQUEST packet never reaches the DHCP server. Root causeStarting from FortiOS 7.4.4, the DHCP relay behavior changed. In versions prior to 7.4.4, the relay forwarded requests to all configured DHCP servers. In FortiOS 7.4.4 and later, the relay forwards requests only to the server IP address specified in the DHCP Server Identifier (Option 54). If Option 54 contains an incorrect IP address, the relay drops the packet with the error "can't find a matching server in the relay".For example, the packet capture shows the DHCP relay forwarding the DHCPDISCOVER packet to the DHCP server at 172.20.200.3. However, the DHCP server responds with 172.20.200.2 in the DHCP Server Identifier (Option 54).Since the IP address in Option 54 does not match the configured DHCP relay server address, the FortiGate drops the subsequent DHCPREQUEST packet instead of forwarding it to the DHCP server. Resolution Enable the dhcp-relay-request-all-server setting on all interfaces that relay DHCP requests. This forces the FortiGate to forward

aiReview.summary: Les requêtes de relais DHCP n'atteignent pas le serveur DHCP dans FortiOS 7.4.4 en raison d'un changement de comportement du relais concernant l'option 54.
aiReview.symptom: Les clients DHCP ne parviennent pas à obtenir d'adresse IP. Les captures de paquets montrent que le serveur DHCP envoie un DHCPOFFER et que le client répond par un DHCPREQUEST, mais ce dernier n'arrive jamais au serveur DHCP.
aiReview.solution: À partir de FortiOS 7.4.4, le relais ne transmet les requêtes qu'à l'adresse IP du serveur spécifiée dans l'identifiant du serveur DHCP (option 54). Si l'option 54 contient une adresse IP incorrecte, le relais supprime le paquet avec l'erreur « can't find a matching server in the relay ».

incidents.title: Input not as expected error when enabling Log application health metrics on Firewall policy
incidents.summary: DescriptionEnabling the Log application health metrics feature on a firewall policy via the GUI may result in an "Input not as expected" error due to a failure to automatically disable NPU offloading.ScopeFortiOS 8.0.0.SolutionWhen attempting to enable the "Log application health metrics" feature on a firewall policy through the graphical user interface (GUI), the system returns an "Input not as expected" error and fails to save the policy.The "Log application health metrics" feature requires NPU offloading to be disabled for the specific firewall…
incidents.symptom: Enabling the Log application health metrics feature on a firewall policy via the GUI may result in an "Input not as expected" error due to a failure to automatically disable NPU offloading
incidents.solution: When attempting to enable the "Log application health metrics" feature on a firewall policy through the graphical user interface (GUI), the system returns an "Input not as expected" error and fails to save the policy.The "Log application health metrics" feature requires NPU offloading to be disabled for the specific firewall policy. While configuring this feature via the command line interface (CLI) automatically disables NPU offloading, the GUI does not perform this action automatically, leading to a validation error. To resolve this issue, manually disable NPU offloading for the firewall policy using the CLI before enabling the health metrics feature on GUI, or configure the entire setting via the CLI:Run the following commands to disable NPU offloading for the affected policy:config firewall policy edit set auto-asic-offload disable next endAfter disabling the offload, enable the "Log application health metrics" in the GUI or continue via the CLI:config firewall policy edit set passive-wan-health-measurement enable next endThis is known GUI issue 1277938, which is resolved in FortiOS 8.0.1. See FortiOS 8.0.1 Resolved issues.For more information on this feature, refer to Graphica

incidents.title: FortiProxy HA split-brain after sequential upgrade on VMware
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiProxy VM clusters using unicast heartbeat may experience a split-brain scenario where both units become primary after a sequential firmware upgrade to version 7.6.ScopeFortiProxy.SolutionSymptomsDuring or after a sequential firmware upgrade to FortiProxy 7.6, the following symptoms may occur in an Active-Passive High Availability (HA) cluster on VMware using unicast heartbeat:The secondary unit reports "System upgrade failed" in the console after rebooting.Both the primary and secondary units assume the primary role simultaneously…
incidents.symptom: FortiProxy VM clusters using unicast heartbeat may experience a split-brain scenario where both units become primary after a sequential firmware upgrade to version 7.6
incidents.solution: SymptomsDuring or after a sequential firmware upgrade to FortiProxy 7.6, the following symptoms may occur in an Active-Passive High Availability (HA) cluster on VMware using unicast heartbeat:The secondary unit reports "System upgrade failed" in the console after rebooting.Both the primary and secondary units assume the primary role simultaneously (split-brain).The primary unit reports the peer as lost.The secondary unit reports the primary unit is lost.Intermittent blocking of web traffic occurs due to incomplete FortiGuard registration or connectivity issues. Root causeThis behavior is caused by bug ID 1323217. In FortiProxy 7.6, when a cluster member is rebooted, the secondary unit stops answering ARP requests on the heartbeat link. Because the primary unit cannot resolve the secondary unit via ARP, it reports the peer as lost and promotes itself to primary, while the secondary unit also assumes the primary role. Resolution Contournement : sIf the split-brain occurs, use one of the following workarounds:Reboot the secondary unit. This forces the unit to broadcast a Gratuitous ARP (GARP) upon boot, which allows the primary unit to resolve the secondary unit and restore the HA state.Manually add a static ARP entry on the primary unit for the secondary unit's heartbeat interface:diagnose ip arp add Note: The diagnose ip arp add command creates a runtime entry that is lost after a reboot. To make the ARP entry persistent, configure it under config system arp-table. Preventative measuresTo avoid this issue, consider the following options:Upgrade Firmware: Install FortiProxy 7.6.8 or later, which contains the fix (recorded against build 1675).Change Heartbeat Mode: Use multicast heartbeat instead of unicast. On VMware, ensure that promiscuous mode and MAC address changes are enabled on the heartbeat port group and the data interface. Multicast design does not rely on the ARP resolution that triggers this bug

incidents.title: The FortiManagement Cloud Web GUI provides an incorrect configuration revision file for download
incidents.summary: DescriptionAn issue where, when attempting to download a specific older configuration revision from the FortiManagement Cloud Web GUI, the downloaded file contains a newer firmware version and configuration than the one selected. ScopeFortiManagement Cloud, FortiGate. SolutionA bug in the FortiManagement Cloud Web GUI causes a mismatch between the selected configuration revision and the actual file delivered for download.
incidents.symptom: An issue where, when attempting to download a specific older configuration revision from the FortiManagement Cloud Web GUI, the downloaded file contains a newer firmware version and configuration than the one selected
incidents.solution: A bug in the FortiManagement Cloud Web GUI causes a mismatch between the selected configuration revision and the actual file delivered for download. This behavior may occur when the firmware version information displayed in the configuration revision history is not synchronized with the actual backup file, particularly after a firmware upgrade.To retrieve the correct configuration file, select an earlier configuration revision and verify whether the downloaded file contains the expected configuration.A fix for this issue is planned for an upcoming FortiManager Cloud release

incidents.title: FortiAP clients missing from FortiGate GUI and wireless runtime reporting after HA role change
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter a FortiGate High Availability (HA) role change, managed FortiAPs can remain online while their wireless clients stop appearing in the FortiGate GUI, even though the clients remain authenticated and continue passing traffic.This article describes how to confirm the condition and restore wireless client reporting.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.x and FortiAP 7.6.x.SolutionSymptoms:FortiAPs remain up in CWAS_RUN in the diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c wtp output, but only FortiAPs that rejoined after the role change report their clients.diagnose…
incidents.symptom: After a FortiGate High Availability (HA) role change, managed FortiAPs can remain online while their wireless clients stop appearing in the FortiGate GUI, even though the clients remain authenticated and continue passing traffic.This article describes how to confirm the condition and restore wireless client reporting
incidents.solution: Symptoms:FortiAPs remain up in CWAS_RUN in the diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c wtp output, but only FortiAPs that rejoined after the role change report their clients.diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c ws shows VAPs with BSSID 00:00:00:00:00:00 and state N/A. Some VAPs also report a configuration failure.A client is authenticated on the FortiAP with active traffic counters, and the FortiGate session table shows sessions in both directions. However, diagnose wireless-controller wlac -d sta returns no entry for the client.The FortiGate GUI client monitor does not list the client.Example output:401F-HA-2 (vdom1) # diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c ws -------------------------------WTP SESSION 1---------------------------- WTP session : 9-10.100.100.3:5246 MP07 CWAS_RUN,7087 11,12 Ctrl in_ifIdx : 88/fap-lan indev : 0/ Data in_ifIdx : 88/fap-lan indev : 0/ mesh uplink : ethernet id : PU431FTH20027288 mgmt_vlanid : 0 wtp_wanlan_mode : wan-only refcnt : 10 deleted : no plain_ctl : disabled wtp-mode : normal wtp-report-index : 1 data-chan-sec : clear-text ctl-msg-offload : ac=0bff/wtp_loc=0bff/wtp_rem=03ff/oper=03ff session_id : 5f4bed54114567f910ea290e324e5c46 ehapd cfg : ongoing Contournement : Restore wireless client reporting using one of the following methods.Note: These operations restart the affected FortiAPs or the wireless controller daemon and may temporarily interrupt wireless connectivity. Perform them during a maintenance window.Reset the affected FortiAPs.Reset the affected FortiAP to force it to rejoin the controller and repopulate its client information.To reset a specific FortiAP, run the following:execute wireless-controller reset-wtp To reset all managed FortiAPs:execute wireless-controller reset-wtp allTo limit the impact, reset a specific FortiAP group instead:execute wireless-controller reset-wtp Note:The all option restarts every managed FortiAP and disconnects all wireless clients.If a newer FortiAP firmware image is available on the FortiGate and image download is enabled, the FortiAP downloads and installs it when rejoining the controller.Configure a single client daemon.When multiple client daemons are configured, the wireless client information may not be synchronized across all daemons.Set acd-process-count to 0 as a mitigation:config wireless-controller global set acd-process-count 0 endVerify the accepted values for the running FortiOS release

Some VAPs also report a configuration failure.A client is authenticated on the FortiAP with active traffic counters, and the FortiGate session table shows sessions in both directions. However, diagnose wireless-controller wlac -d sta returns no entry for the client.The FortiGate GUI client monitor does not list the client.Example output:401F-HA-2 (vdom1) # diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c ws -------------------------------WTP SESSION 1---------------------------- WTP session : 9-10.100.100.3:5246 MP07 CWAS_RUN,7087 11,12 Ctrl in_ifIdx : 88/fap-lan indev : 0/ Data in_ifIdx : 88/fap-lan indev : 0/ mesh uplink : ethernet id : PU431FTH20027288 mgmt_vlanid : 0 wtp_wanlan_mode : wan-only refcnt : 10 deleted : no plain_ctl : disabled wtp-mode : normal wtp-report-index : 1 data-chan-sec : clear-text ctl-msg-offload : ac=0bff/wtp_loc=0bff/wtp_rem=03ff/oper=03ff session_id : 5f4bed54114567f910ea290e324e5c46 ehapd cfg : ongoing Contournement : Restore wireless client reporting using one of the following methods.Note: These operations restart the affected FortiAPs or the wireless controller daemon and may temporarily interrupt wireless connectivity. Perform them during a maintenance window.Reset the affected FortiAPs.Reset the affected FortiAP to force it to rejoin the controller and repopulate its client information.To reset a specific FortiAP, run the following:execute wireless-controller reset-wtp To reset all managed FortiAPs:execute wireless-controller reset-wtp allTo limit the impact, reset a specific FortiAP group instead:execute wireless-controller reset-wtp Note:The all option restarts every managed FortiAP and disconnects all wireless clients.If a newer FortiAP firmware image is available on the FortiGate and image download is enabled, the FortiAP downloads and installs it when rejoining the controller.Configure a single client daemon.When multiple client daemons are configured, the wireless client information may not be synchronized across all daemons.Set acd-process-count to 0 as a mitigation:config wireless-controller global set acd-process-count 0 endVerify the accepted values for the running FortiOS release

incidents.title: DNS Database Configuration Lost After Upgrading to FortiOS 8.0.1
incidents.summary: DescriptionAn issue where DNS database configurations are lost after upgrading a FortiGate from FortiOS 8.0.0 to FortiOS 8.0.1.The issue occurs when DNS database entries have names starting with a period ( . ). These entries may fail to load during the upgrade process, resulting in the DNS database configuration being removed.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionAfter upgrading to FortiOS 8.0.1, the DNS database configuration under config system dns-database is missing.The configuration error log displays the following error:>>> "edit" ".fortinet.me" @…
incidents.symptom: An issue where DNS database configurations are lost after upgrading a FortiGate from FortiOS 8.0.0 to FortiOS 8.0.1.The issue occurs when DNS database entries have names starting with a period ( . ). These entries may fail to load during the upgrade process, resulting in the DNS database configuration being removed
incidents.solution: After upgrading to FortiOS 8.0.1, the DNS database configuration under config system dns-database is missing.The configuration error log displays the following error:>>> "edit" ".fortinet.me" @ root.system.dns-database:failed command (error -2004)Attempting to configure a DNS database entry with a name starting with a period also produces the following error:LAB_FGT (dns-database) # edit ".fortinet.me" Table name '.fortinet.me' contains illegal character! Command fail. Return code -2004The issue appears to be related to DNS database entry names beginning with a period ( . ).In FortiOS 8.0.0, DNS database entries with names starting with a period are accepted. However, in FortiOS 8.0.1, these names are rejected during configuration parsing.As a result, when the FortiGate processes the existing configuration during the upgrade, the affected DNS database entries fail to load and are omitted from the running configuration. Solution Contournement : Before upgrading to FortiOS 8.0.1, review the existing DNS database configuration and rename any entries whose names begin with a period ( . ).Before upgrading, verify the existing DNS database configuration:show system dns-databaseIdentify DNS database entries with names starting with a period.For example:config system dns-database edit ".fortinet.me"Rename the affected DNS database entries to names that do not begin with a period.For example:config system dns-database edit "fortinet.me"Ensure that the corresponding DNS database settings and DNS entries are retained.Verify the updated configuration:show system dns-databaseOnce the configuration has been updated and verified, proceed with the FortiOS upgrade.After upgrading, verify that all DNS database entries are present:show system dns-databaseNote: Always back up the FortiGate configuration before performing a firmware upgrade

incidents.title: FortiManager unable to push device-level configuration to HA FortiGate VM in public cloud
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiManager cannot push certain device-level configuration changes, including VLAN and system interface configurations, to FortiGate VMs deployed as an HA cluster in public cloud environments. As a result, FortiManager may be unable to generate an install preview or install these configuration changes.ScopeFortiManager.FortiGate VM deployed in HA mode on the following public cloud platforms:Amazon Web Services (AWS).Microsoft Azure (AZ).Google Cloud Platform (GCP).SolutionWhen FortiManager manages a FortiGate HA cluster in a public cloud…
incidents.symptom: FortiManager cannot push certain device-level configuration changes, including VLAN and system interface configurations, to FortiGate VMs deployed as an HA cluster in public cloud environments. As a result, FortiManager may be unable to generate an install preview or install these configuration changes
incidents.solution: When FortiManager manages a FortiGate HA cluster in a public cloud environment, it cannot install certain device-level configuration changes.Examples include the following configuration areas:config system ha config system interface config system sdn-connector nic config system sdn-connector route-tableAlthough the FortiManager Administration Guide explicitly references AWS and Azure, the same limitation applies to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) deployments.Because these configuration objects are device-specific, FortiManager cannot push them to HA FortiGate virtual machines in public cloud environments Contournement : To modify VLANs, interfaces, or other affected device-level settings:Make the required configuration changes directly on each FortiGate cluster member using either the GUI or CLI.Verify the cluster members are in sync:get system ha status diagnose sys ha dump-by vclusterBoth members must show the same configuration before proceeding.After the changes have been applied successfully, retrieve the configuration from the FortiGate devices into FortiManager.Verify that the FortiManager Device Database is synchronized with the FortiGate configuration.Retrieving the configuration ensures that FortiManager reflects the running configuration on the managed devices and prevents database mismatches.Verifying FortiManager virtual machine resources.If FortiManager exhibits unexpected behavior during install previews, configuration retrievals, or installation operations, verify that the FortiManager virtual machine meets the minimum system requirements.When additional virtual disk space has been added, run the following commands:execute lvm extend diagnose sys fsck harddiskIf the FortiManager virtual machine was previously undersized, expand the virtual disk from the cloud or hypervisor platform
versionScopes: FortiManager.FortiGate VM deployed in HA mode on the following public cloud platforms:Amazon Web Services (AWS).Microsoft Azure (AZ).Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

incidents.title: FortiClient EMS connector authorization failure in security fabric due to Fortinet_Wifi_CA conflict
incidents.summary: DescriptionA downstream FortiGate in a Security Fabric fails to synchronize the FortiClient EMS verifying-ca certificate from the root FortiGate, resulting in an "EMS certificate not authorized" error in the GUI or CLI: "internal error finding verifying CA cert for EMS".ScopeFortiGate.SolutionRoot causeThe issue occurs when, in an existing Security Fabric setup, the root FortiGate uses an imported CA certificate (promoted to fabric-ca) signed by DigiCert Global G2 TLS RSA SHA256 2020 CA1.
incidents.symptom: A downstream FortiGate in a Security Fabric fails to synchronize the FortiClient EMS verifying-ca certificate from the root FortiGate, resulting in an "EMS certificate not authorized" error in the GUI or CLI: "internal error finding verifying CA cert for EMS"
incidents.solution: Root causeThe issue occurs when, in an existing Security Fabric setup, the root FortiGate uses an imported CA certificate (promoted to fabric-ca) signed by DigiCert Global G2 TLS RSA SHA256 2020 CA1. When the Security Fabric root attempts to synchronize the CA certificate with a newly added downstream FortiGate, the certificate import is rejected by the downstream device because the factory-installed Fortinet_Wifi_CA cannot be renamed.Consequently, the verifying-ca reference is dropped, and the GUI reports that the FortiClient EMS Cloud or FortiClient EMS is not authorized on the downstream.The following debug output is observed on the downstream FortiGate:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp en diagnose debug application csfd -1 diagnose debug enable 02 nstd_ca_rename()-32: Failed to rename CA Fortinet_Wifi_CA to CSF_CA_Cert_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx_n (rc=-61)To disable debug processes:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug resetThe Security Fabric root displays the CA certificate, but the downstream does not.Fabric root:config vpn certificate ca edit "CSF_CA_Cert_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx_n set range global set fabric-ca enable next endDownstream:execu

incidents.title: FortiAP firmware upgrade fails when uploading firmware over a VPN connection
incidents.summary: DescriptionA potential issue where manually upgrading FortiAP firmware through the FortiGate GUI fails or appears to stall when the administrator uploads the firmware image over a VPN connection.ScopeAll supported versions of FortiGate and FortiAP.SolutionWhen manually uploading a FortiAP firmware image (.out) through the FortiGate GUI, the firmware file is transferred from the administrator's workstation to the FortiGate before being delivered to the FortiAP.If the administrator is connected through a VPN client, additional VPN encapsulation…
incidents.symptom: A potential issue where manually upgrading FortiAP firmware through the FortiGate GUI fails or appears to stall when the administrator uploads the firmware image over a VPN connection
incidents.solution: When manually uploading a FortiAP firmware image (.out) through the FortiGate GUI, the firmware file is transferred from the administrator's workstation to the FortiGate before being delivered to the FortiAP.If the administrator is connected through a VPN client, additional VPN encapsulation overhead can reduce the effective Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU). Depending on the VPN configuration and network path, this may introduce fragmentation or Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) issues, potentially interfering with the firmware upload process.In this scenario, the following symptoms may be observed:The FortiAP firmware upgrade process appears to stall within the FortiGate GUI.The FortiAP may initially be reported as "Disconnected" in the FortiGate GUI, before the firmware upgrade eventually transitions to "Cancelled".The FortiAP does not reboot and continues running its existing firmware version, indicating that the firmware upgrade has not been applied.The FortiGate crash log may contain entries relating to the Scheduled Firmware Upgrade Daemon (sfupgraded):the killed daemon is /bin/sfupgraded: status=0x0When reviewing the sfupgraded debug output, the following message may also be observe Contournement : To avoid potential MTU or fragmentation issues introduced by the VPN connection, perform the firmware upgrade from a device with local network connectivity to the FortiGate.Connect to a jump server within the local network and perform the firmware upload through the FortiGate GUI.Alternatively, access the FortiGate GUI directly from a workstation connected to the LAN.Once the firmware upgrade has completed, navigate to WiFi & Switch Controller -> Managed FortiAPs and verify that the FortiAP is online and running the expected firmware version.Note: The symptoms and sfupgraded debug messages do not independently confirm an MTU or fragmentation issue. However, if the firmware upgrade succeeds when performed from the local network rather than over the VPN connection, this suggests that the remote management path may be contributing to the failure.The status=0x0 daemon termination entry alone does not confirm an abnormal daemon crash
versionScopes: All supported versions of FortiGate and FortiAP

incidents.title: Windows 10/11 endpoints fail to obtain IPv6 SLAAC address when connected to a FortiSwitch
incidents.summary: DescriptionWindows 10/11 endpoints may fail to obtain an IPv6 address through SLAAC when connected to a FortiSwitch access port. This occurs because the initial Router Solicitation (RS) packets are dropped during the STP port transition from discarding to forwarding.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionRoot cause:By default, a FortiSwitch access port takes approximately 3 seconds to transition from the STP discarding state to the forwarding state.
incidents.symptom: Windows 10/11 endpoints may fail to obtain an IPv6 address through SLAAC when connected to a FortiSwitch access port. This occurs because the initial Router Solicitation (RS) packets are dropped during the STP port transition from discarding to forwarding
incidents.solution: Root cause:By default, a FortiSwitch access port takes approximately 3 seconds to transition from the STP discarding state to the forwarding state. During this transition, the switch temporarily prevents traffic from being forwarded through the port.Windows 10/11 sends its initial three Router Solicitation (RS) packets at approximately 1-second intervals. As a result, all three RS packets may be transmitted while the FortiSwitch port is still in the STP discarding state and subsequently dropped.Since Windows does not re-transmit the initial RS packets at a sufficiently later interval in this scenario, the endpoint may not receive a Router Advertisement (RA) from the router. Consequently, it fails to obtain an IPv6 address through SLAAC and the associated default route.By comparison, macOS, Linux, and Android may re-transmit RS packets at approximately 4-second intervals. This allows a subsequent RS packet to reach the network after the FortiSwitch port has transitioned to the forwarding state, enabling the endpoint to receive an RA and successfully establish IPv6 connectivity Contournement : Before upgrading to a fixed release, consider disabling STP on dedicated end-device access ports:On FortiSwitch CLI:config switch interface edit set stp-state disabled next endUse this only on ports dedicated to end devices, not on uplinks or ports where switches may be connected.Resolution:The issue is fixed in FortiSwitchOS versions 7.6.9 and 8.0.1.These releases introduce the edge-port fast option, which immediately transitions the interface to forwarding without the approximately 3-second delay.In the FortiSwitch CLI:config switch interface edit set edge-port fast next end

Consequently, it fails to obtain an IPv6 address through SLAAC and the associated default route.By comparison, macOS, Linux, and Android may re-transmit RS packets at approximately 4-second intervals. This allows a subsequent RS packet to reach the network after the FortiSwitch port has transitioned to the forwarding state, enabling the endpoint to receive an RA and successfully establish IPv6 connectivity Contournement : Before upgrading to a fixed release, consider disabling STP on dedicated end-device access ports:On FortiSwitch CLI:config switch interface edit set stp-state disabled next endUse this only on ports dedicated to end devices, not on uplinks or ports where switches may be connected.Resolution:The issue is fixed in FortiSwitchOS versions 7.6.9 and 8.0.1.These releases introduce the edge-port fast option, which immediately transitions the interface to forwarding without the approximately 3-second delay.In the FortiSwitch CLI:config switch interface edit set edge-port fast next end

incidents.summary: DescriptionAutomatic ACME certificate renewal fails with HTTP 503 errors and httpsd process crashes in mod_md.so on FortiOS 7.4.12.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptomsThe following symptoms occur during the Let's Encrypt ACME certificate renewal process on FortiGate:The ACME renewal fails with the error "Error waiting on domain names to be validated".The Let's Encrypt server returns HTTP 503 responses or "urn:ietf:params:acme:error:rateLimited".The "httpsd" process crashes with a segmentation fault (signal 11) in the "mod_md.so" module.application httpsd…
incidents.symptom: Automatic ACME certificate renewal fails with HTTP 503 errors and httpsd process crashes in mod_md.so on FortiOS 7.4.12
incidents.solution: SymptomsThe following symptoms occur during the Let's Encrypt ACME certificate renewal process on FortiGate:The ACME renewal fails with the error "Error waiting on domain names to be validated".The Let's Encrypt server returns HTTP 503 responses or "urn:ietf:params:acme:error:rateLimited".The "httpsd" process crashes with a segmentation fault (signal 11) in the "mod_md.so" module.application httpsd *** signal 11 (Segmentation fault) received *** fault_address: 0000000000000000 Backtrace: => /usr/local/apache2/modules/mod_md.so => /usr/local/apache2/modules/mod_md.so => /usr/local/apache2/modules/mod_md.so => /usr/local/apache2/modules/mod_watchdog.so Root causeTwo distinct causes exist for this issue:Software Bug: A timing issue in FortiOS 7.4 causes the httpsd process to crash within the mod_md.so module during ACME certificate management.Network Filtering: Upstream firewalls or NAT devices may block TCP port 80 or filter traffic based on application signatures. If the upstream device does not explicitly allow the acme-protocol, the HTTP-01 challenge validation fails even if basic TCP connectivity exists. Re solution Step 1: Resolve httpsd crashesUpgrade FortiGate to FortiOS 7.4.1

incidents.title: FortiManager installation fails due to duplicate address group members on FortiGate
incidents.summary: DescriptionSteps to troubleshoot FortiManager installation failures caused by duplicated firewall address group members on FortiGate.In some cases, FortiManager reports an installation failure even though the configuration command is accepted by FortiGate.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManager.SolutionThis behavior can happen when a firewall address object referenced by an address group is renamed. Duplicate member references may remain in the FortiGate configuration, resulting in a mismatch between FortiManager and FortiGate.The duplicated members may be…
incidents.symptom: Steps to troubleshoot FortiManager installation failures caused by duplicated firewall address group members on FortiGate.In some cases, FortiManager reports an installation failure even though the configuration command is accepted by FortiGate
incidents.solution: This behavior can happen when a firewall address object referenced by an address group is renamed. Duplicate member references may remain in the FortiGate configuration, resulting in a mismatch between FortiManager and FortiGate.The duplicated members may be visible in the FortiGate CLI configuration but not in the GUI.Check the affected address group on FortiGate:show firewall addrgrp "example_group"Example of a group having a duplicated member:config firewall addrgrp edit "example_group" set member "address1" "address2" "address2" next endCheck the FortiManager installation logs.Compare the address group members in the 'remote original' and 'to be installed' configuration.FortiManager may attempt to install the correct member list, but the FortiGate retains the existing duplicate entries. As a result, the installation comparison fails.Remove the duplicated members from the affected group.Before making changes, save a configuration backup and record the correct address group members.Perform this action during a maintenance window if the address group is referenced by firewall policies, as the group will temporarily have no members.config firewall addrgrp edit "example_group" unset

incidents.title: Unable to import configuration file in FortiClient standalone version 7.4.7
incidents.summary: DescriptionSteps to import configuration files in FortiClient Standalone 7.4.7 using the CLI, as GUI-based restoration is not supported and FCConfig.exe may return the error "Backup requires a password" even when the correct password is provided.ScopeFortiClient standalone.SolutionTo import a FortiClient configuration file using Command Prompt, navigate to the FortiClient installation directory:cd "C:\Program Files\Fortinet\FortiClient"Run the following command to import the configuration:FCConfig.exe -f -o import -p See FortiClient Standalone…
incidents.symptom: Steps to import configuration files in FortiClient Standalone 7.4.7 using the CLI, as GUI-based restoration is not supported and FCConfig.exe may return the error "Backup requires a password" even when the correct password is provided
incidents.solution: To import a FortiClient configuration file using Command Prompt, navigate to the FortiClient installation directory:cd "C:\Program Files\Fortinet\FortiClient"Run the following command to import the configuration:FCConfig.exe -f -o import -p See FortiClient Standalone (Windows) CLI commands.If the following error appears even with a correct password:C:\Program Files\Fortinet\FortiClient>FCConfig.exe -f C:\Program Files\Fortinet\FortiClient\IPSEC.conf -o import -p fortinet Backup requires a password This issue occurs because the configuration file path contains spaces and is not enclosed in quotation marks.To resolve this issue, use either of the following methods:Option 1: Copy the configuration file to a temporary folder (e.g., C:\Temp) and run:FCConfig.exe -f C:\Temp\IPSEC.conf -o import -p fortinetOption 2: Keep the configuration file in its original location and enclose the complete file path in quotation marks:FCConfig.exe -f "C:\Program Files\Fortinet\FortiClient\IPSEC.conf" -o import -p fortinet

incidents.title: After upgrading the FortiOS to 7.6.7 FortiSwitch to 8.0.0, the topology disconnects
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading the FortiOS to 7.6.7 and FortiSwitch to 8.0.0 in the Topology view, the FortiLink connection between the FortiGate and the MC-LAG switches is displayed as Not Connected, as shown in the screenshot below.ScopeFortiSwitches managed by a FortiLink Core switch (1048E) Access (424E and 1xx series).FortLink in an MC-LAG setup.SolutionSymptoms:In the Topology view, the FortiLink connection between the FortiGate and the MC-LAG switches is displayed as Not Connected.On the switch CLI's trunk status, the CAPWAP tunnel will show as "up".
incidents.symptom: After upgrading the FortiOS to 7.6.7 and FortiSwitch to 8.0.0 in the Topology view, the FortiLink connection between the FortiGate and the MC-LAG switches is displayed as Not Connected, as shown in the screenshot below
incidents.solution: Symptoms:In the Topology view, the FortiLink connection between the FortiGate and the MC-LAG switches is displayed as Not Connected.On the switch CLI's trunk status, the CAPWAP tunnel will show as "up". The FortiGate switch connection status is Authorized/Up.Solution:The STP root bridge was an unknown device connected to port21 (PortChannel_105). This device was acting as the STP root bridge and belonged to a different MSTP region than the FortiSwitch. We made the MC-LAG switch as a root bridge.The LACP mode on the FortiLink trunk was configured as Static. The LACP mode was changed to LACP Active on the FortiLink trunk configuration on the FortiGate.Change the topology from a square topology to a full-mesh topology between the FortiGate HA pair and the core MC-LAG switches

The FortiGate switch connection status is Authorized/Up.Solution:The STP root bridge was an unknown device connected to port21 (PortChannel_105). This device was acting as the STP root bridge and belonged to a different MSTP region than the FortiSwitch. We made the MC-LAG switch as a root bridge.The LACP mode on the FortiLink trunk was configured as Static. The LACP mode was changed to LACP Active on the FortiLink trunk configuration on the FortiGate.Change the topology from a square topology to a full-mesh topology between the FortiGate HA pair and the core MC-LAG switches

incidents.title: A secondary member in a FortiGate High Availability cluster becomes invisible in the HA menu after a failover triggered by a monitored interface disconnection
incidents.summary: DescriptionAn issue regarding the secondary member in a FortiGate High Availability cluster becoming invisible in the HA menu after a failover triggered by a monitored interface disconnection.ScopeFortiGate HA Cluster.SolutionSymptomsAfter disconnecting a monitored interface cable to test High Availability (HA) failover, the new primary unit does not list the secondary member in the HA status menu. The execute ha manage command to the secondary unit also fails.
incidents.symptom: An issue regarding the secondary member in a FortiGate High Availability cluster becoming invisible in the HA menu after a failover triggered by a monitored interface disconnection
incidents.solution: SymptomsAfter disconnecting a monitored interface cable to test High Availability (HA) failover, the new primary unit does not list the secondary member in the HA status menu. The execute ha manage command to the secondary unit also fails. However, the issue does not occur during a manual role swap using:diagnose sys ha reset-uptime Root causeThe secondary unit enters a stuck state or maintains a high link-failure count after a monitored interface failure. This prevents the unit from being accepted back into the cluster or maintaining bidirectional heartbeat communication with the primary unit, even if heartbeat links are functional.Immediate recoveryReboot both units in the cluster one by one to clear the stuck state and restore visibility of the HA members.Diagnostics and verificationIf the issue occurs, perform the following steps to identify the cause:Run the following commands on the current primary unit to check HA status and history:get system ha status diagnose sys ha history read diagnose sys ha dump-by group diagnose sys ha dump-by vcluster diagnose sys ha checksum cluster Verify the physical status of the heartbeat interfaces:diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic a diagnose h

incidents.title: Technical Tip: How to resolve the issue when EMS upgrade fail due to max index row size exceeded in PostgreSQL
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an EMS migration issue where the max index row size was exceeded in PostgreSQL when upgrading EMS from version 7.4.7 to 7.4.8.ScopeFortiClient EMS.SolutionEMS version 7.4.7 failed to be upgraded to version 7.4.8 due to the max index row size in the PostgreSQL database.Upon checking the EMS migration log, the following error is shown in the log:sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (psycopg2.errors.ProgramLimitExceeded) index row size 3072 exceeds btree version 4 maximum 2704 for index…
incidents.symptom: This article describes an EMS migration issue where the max index row size was exceeded in PostgreSQL when upgrading EMS from version 7.4.7 to 7.4.8
incidents.solution: EMS version 7.4.7 failed to be upgraded to version 7.4.8 due to the max index row size in the PostgreSQL database.Upon checking the EMS migration log, the following error is shown in the log:sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (psycopg2.errors.ProgramLimitExceeded) index row size 3072 exceeds btree version 4 maximum 2704 for index "ix_vuln_details_severity_category_cve_list_reference" DETAIL: Index row references tuple (1609,13) in relation "vuln_details". HINT: Values larger than 1/3 of a buffer page cannot be indexed. Consider a function index of an MD5 hash of the value, or use full text indexing.To resolve this issue, run the following commands one by one in the EMS machine Linux shell:# sudo -i emscli # db # DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_vuln_details_severity_category_cve_list_reference; # CREATE INDEX ix_vuln_details_severity_category_cve_list_reference ON public.vuln_details USING btree (severity, category); # \qAfter the above, perform the migration again. If the upgrade issue still persists, then raise a TAC ticket (Support) and continue troubleshooting with a TAC engineer

incidents.title: Diagnosing TCP packet loss and retransmissions using iperf3, FortiGate sniffer, and Wireshark
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to troubleshoot TCP throughput degradation, identify packet loss, and correlate network performance metrics between iperf3, packet capture from the FortiGate, and Wireshark. Specifically, it it details how TCP sequence numbers can be leveraged to pinpoint packet loss.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionPreparation and recommended Practices:To ensure accurate sequence tracking and protocol decoding in Wireshark without truncation issues, always capture packets using an SSH client like PuTTY.Converting CLI capture to Wireshark…
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot TCP throughput degradation, identify packet loss, and correlate network performance metrics between iperf3, packet capture from the FortiGate, and Wireshark. Specifically, it it details how TCP sequence numbers can be leveraged to pinpoint packet loss
incidents.solution: Preparation and recommended Practices:To ensure accurate sequence tracking and protocol decoding in Wireshark without truncation issues, always capture packets using an SSH client like PuTTY.Converting CLI capture to Wireshark file:Run the FortiGate packet sniffer via SSH, ensure logging is enabled, and use the FGT2ETH tool to convert it. See this article for more info: How to import 'diagnose sniffer packet' data to WireShark.Ensuring Capture Integrity (Zero Dropped Packets):When stopping your CLI packet capture (using ^C), always verify that 0 packets were dropped by the kernel. This confirms that your FortiGate successfully captured every single packet without buffer exhaustion during high-speed traffic tests.^C 12336 packets received by filter 0 packets dropped by kernelDisable NPU offload:Disable NPU offload on the matching firewall policy to capture all the traffic. See this article for more info: Technical Tip: FortiGate Disable Hardware Acceleration.config firewall policy edit 2 set name "AllowInternet" set uuid 48410dd6-e04b-51f1-6869-a61baae82f55 set srcintf "port3" set dstintf "port1" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service

incidents.symptom: OSPF neighborship drops and fails to reach Full state when using aggregate IPsec tunnels due to incorrect load balancing algorithms
incidents.solution: Symptoms:OSPF neighbors fail to establish adjacency or frequently drop the connection. The system logs show the following error messages:H1 # diagnose ip router ospf all enable H1 # diagnose ip router ospf level info H1 # diagnose debug console timestamp enable H1 # diagnose debug enable 2026-11-12 09:44:29 OSPF: NFSM[Local-Agg:172.28.0.14-10.200.2.253]: neighbor addr or tun-id changed 2026-11-12 09:44:29 OSPF: NFSM[Local-Agg:172.28.0.14-10.200.2.253]: Status change Full -> Down 2026-11-12 09:44:29 id=20302 msg="OSPF: %OSPF-5-ADJCHANGE: neighbor Local Agg:172.28.0.14-10.200.2.253 Down " 2026-11-12 09:44:29 OSPF: NFSM[Local-Agg:172.28.0.14-0.0.0.0]: Start 2026-11-12 09:44:29 OSPF: NFSM[Local-Agg:172.28.0.14-10.200.2.253]: Down (HelloReceived) Root cause:The issue occurs when OSPF traffic is distributed across multiple members of an aggregate IPsec tunnel. If the aggregate tunnel algorithm is not set to the load balancing algorithm, OSPF packets may switch between different tunnel members. This causes the receiving FortiGate to detect a change in the neighbor address or tunnel ID, which forces the OSPF neighborship to drop.config system ipsec-aggregate edit "Local-Agg" set member "Tu

incidents.title: After upgrade to FortiOS version 7.4.13, user receives error '400 Bad Request' when using proxy inspection and Deep Packet inspection
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to FortiOS version 7.4.13, a user may start receiving "Error 400: Bad Request" when accessing legitimate sites when the firewall policy is set to use Deep Packet Inspection and proxy-based inspection.ScopeFortiOS version 7.4.13.SolutionFollowing an upgrade to FortiOS version 7.4.13, users may start seeing the Error 400 Bad Request when accessing legitimate sites: This issue is present when the following settings are in place:strict-web-check is set to enable:config web-proxy global set strict-web-check enable endFirewall…
incidents.symptom: After upgrading to FortiOS version 7.4.13, a user may start receiving "Error 400: Bad Request" when accessing legitimate sites when the firewall policy is set to use Deep Packet Inspection and proxy-based inspection
incidents.solution: Following an upgrade to FortiOS version 7.4.13, users may start seeing the Error 400 Bad Request when accessing legitimate sites: This issue is present when the following settings are in place:strict-web-check is set to enable:config web-proxy global set strict-web-check enable endFirewall policy using proxy-mode inspection and a Deep Packet Inspection profile:config firewall policy edit 40 set name "Outbound Internet" ... set inspection-mode proxy set ssl-ssh-profile "custom-deep-inspection" ... next end FortiOS version 7.4.13 introduced a change that enables strict-web-check: Changes in default behavior.The reason the traffic is blocked is that enabling strict-web-check under config web-proxy global caused the proxy mode policy to block HTTP/2 requests that carry more than one Cookie header field. HTTP/2 (per RFC 7540 8.1.2.5) permits the Cookie header to be split into multiple separate header fields, but strict mode rejected such requests as malformed, returning a connection error to the client.With strict web checking enabled, WAD rejects malformed HTTP requests including requests carrying conflicting duplicate Content-Length headers with "400 Bad Request" instead of forwarding

incidents.title: FortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models show high memory consumption on firmware version 7.6 and 8.0
incidents.summary: DescriptionThe reasons why FortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models run at high memory on firmware version 7.6 and 8.0.ScopeFortiSwitch models 108F and 1xxE.SolutionAfter upgrading FortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models to v7.6 firmware, the FortiSwitch runs at high memory even immediately after boot up and when no traffic is passing through the switch.get system performance status CPU states: 2% user 6% system 0% nice 92% idle Memory states: 72% useddiagnose sys top-mem pyfcgid (919): 23773kB zebra (924): 5695kB igmpsnoopingd (930): 5095kB newcli (2236): 4742kB…
incidents.symptom: The reasons why FortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models run at high memory on firmware version 7.6 and 8.0
incidents.solution: After upgrading FortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models to v7.6 firmware, the FortiSwitch runs at high memory even immediately after boot up and when no traffic is passing through the switch.get system performance status CPU states: 2% user 6% system 0% nice 92% idle Memory states: 72% useddiagnose sys top-mem pyfcgid (919): 23773kB zebra (924): 5695kB igmpsnoopingd (930): 5095kB newcli (2236): 4742kB cu_swtpd (1202): 3285kB Top-5 memory used: 42590kBFortiSwitch 108F and 1xxE models running at high memory after an upgrade to firmware version 7.6 and 8.0 is expected behavior. These models are built with hardware that is limited to 256MB RAM. FortiSwitch OS 7.6's and 8.0's minimum requirement is 512MB RAM. These models will always boot up with high memory usage. The memory usage difference between firmware 7.6, 8.0 and firmware 7.2 or 7.4 is because more features are supported in 7.6 and 8.0, meaning more daemons are running and consume more memory

incidents.title: RADIUS administrative authentication fails after upgrading FortiGate to 7.4.13 due to IPsec synchronization issues
incidents.summary: DescriptionAdministrative access via RADIUS authentication fails after upgrading FortiGate to version 7.4.13 due to IPsec tunnel synchronization issues.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManager.SolutionSymptomsAfter upgrading FortiGate, administrators cannot access the device using RADIUS authentication. The RADIUS server is located behind an IPsec VPN tunnel. While the FortiGate sends authentication traffic into the tunnel, the traffic is not received by the RADIUS server.
incidents.symptom: Administrative access via RADIUS authentication fails after upgrading FortiGate to version 7.4.13 due to IPsec tunnel synchronization issues
incidents.solution: SymptomsAfter upgrading FortiGate, administrators cannot access the device using RADIUS authentication. The RADIUS server is located behind an IPsec VPN tunnel. While the FortiGate sends authentication traffic into the tunnel, the traffic is not received by the RADIUS server. Root causeThe firmware upgrade caused a synchronization issue with the IPsec VPN tunnel encryption keys. The FortiGate maintained multiple encryption keys (both old and new), while the remote peer only recognized the new key. This mismatch prevented traffic from successfully traversing the tunnel to the RADIUS server. Re solution To resolve the authentication failure, reset the IPsec VPN connection to synchronize the encryption keys between the FortiGate and the remote peer.Log in to the FortiGate using a local administrator account.Identify the affected IPsec tunnel used for RADIUS communication.Reset the VPN connection to clear stale encryption keys. You can do this via the GUI or the CLI.To reset the tunnel via CLI, run the following command:diagnose vpn tunnel reset After resetting the tunnel, verify that the RADIUS server is reachable and that administrative users can authenticate successfully

incidents.summary: DescriptionA FortiGate interface fails to obtain or renew an IPv6 address from a DHCPv6 server despite receiving ADVERTISE packets.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionObserved behavior may include:The FortiGate sends a DHCPv6 Solicit.The upstream DHCPv6 server replies with an Advertise.The FortiGate does not complete the DHCPv6 process.No IPv6 address is assigned to the WAN interfaceRun the following command to check the current local-in policies for IPv6:show firewall local-in-policy6Create a local-in policy that allows traffic on UDP ports 546 and 547 from…
incidents.symptom: A FortiGate interface fails to obtain or renew an IPv6 address from a DHCPv6 server despite receiving ADVERTISE packets
incidents.solution: Observed behavior may include:The FortiGate sends a DHCPv6 Solicit.The upstream DHCPv6 server replies with an Advertise.The FortiGate does not complete the DHCPv6 process.No IPv6 address is assigned to the WAN interfaceRun the following command to check the current local-in policies for IPv6:show firewall local-in-policy6Create a local-in policy that allows traffic on UDP ports 546 and 547 from link-local addresses to ensure the FortiGate can process DHCPv6 ADVERTISE packets.config firewall service custom edit "DHCPv6" set udp-portrange 546-547 next end config firewall local-in-policy6 edit 1 set intf "port1" set srcaddr "ipv6-link-local" set dstaddr "all" set service "DHCPv6" set schedule "always" set action accept next end

aiReview.symptom: Le FortiGate envoie un message DHCPv6 Solicit, le serveur distant répond par un Advertise, mais le processus ne se finalise pas et aucune adresse IPv6 n'est attribuée à l'interface WAN.
aiReview.impact: L'interface FortiGate ne reçoit pas d'adresse IP IPv6 via DHCPv6.
aiReview.solution: Créer une politique locale (local-in policy) pour autoriser le trafic sur les ports UDP 546 et 547 à partir des adresses link-local, en configurant un service personnalisé et une règle d'acceptation (local-in-policy6).

incidents.title: Traffic fails to match with an SD-WAN rule when it overlaps with policy route with "Stop Policy Routing" action
incidents.summary: DescriptionThe reason why the SD-WAN rules are bypassed when a policy route is configured with an action configured to stop policy routing.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptomsRegular policy routes have precedence over SD-WAN rules, and they are processed before any SD-WAN rule. If a policy route is configured with a destination of 0.0.0.0/0 (all destinations), it matches the traffic and is forwarded based on the path defined in the policy route, potentially bypassing the intended SD-WAN interface selection.
incidents.symptom: The reason why the SD-WAN rules are bypassed when a policy route is configured with an action configured to stop policy routing
incidents.solution: SymptomsRegular policy routes have precedence over SD-WAN rules, and they are processed before any SD-WAN rule. If a policy route is configured with a destination of 0.0.0.0/0 (all destinations), it matches the traffic and is forwarded based on the path defined in the policy route, potentially bypassing the intended SD-WAN interface selection. If you add a specific policy route with action "Stop Policy Routing" to bypass the policy route evaluation, the traffic still will not match the intended SD-WAN rule.Test scenario:FortiGate has two WAN links (Port5 and Port6).A test PC is connected to Port 3 with IP Address 192.168.231.44 pinging 9.9.9.9.There are two policy routes and one SD-WAN rule configured for testing:Policy ID 1: With action "Stop Policy Routing" to bypass the policy route evaluation.Policy ID 2: To match all Traffic and forward to Port5.SD-WAN rule ID 1: To match the intended traffic and forward to Port6.config firewall address edit "SDWAN-Test" set subnet 192.168.231.44 255.255.255.255 next end config system sdwan config members edit 3 set interface "port5" set zone "Internet" set gateway 10.9.15.254 set priority 10 next edit 4 set interface "port6" set zone "Interne

incidents.title: HTTP 500 error during OAuth authorization after upgrading FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.10
incidents.summary: DescriptionUsers receive an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error at the /api/v1/oauth/authorize/ endpoint when authenticating through applications using FortiAuthenticator as an OAuth/OIDC provider.ScopeFortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10.SolutionAfter upgrading to FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10, users attempting to log in via OAuth/OIDC applications encounter an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.The error occurs specifically at the /api/v1/oauth/authorize/ endpoint.The system logs display the following traceback:Internal Server Error:…
incidents.symptom: Users receive an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error at the /api/v1/oauth/authorize/ endpoint when authenticating through applications using FortiAuthenticator as an OAuth/OIDC provider
incidents.solution: After upgrading to FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10, users attempting to log in via OAuth/OIDC applications encounter an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.The error occurs specifically at the /api/v1/oauth/authorize/ endpoint.The system logs display the following traceback:Internal Server Error: /api/v1/oauth/authorize/ Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "./fac/fac/apps/oauth/views.py", line 282, in dispatch File "/lib/python3.11/site-packages/django/utils/functional.py", line 268, in inner return func(_wrapped, *args) AttributeError: 'RemoteLdapSessionUser' object has no attribute 'fac_groups' Root cause.This issue occurs when a non-imported remote user attempts to access an OAuth authorization page. In FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10, non-imported remote users cannot log in to OAuth portals, which leads to the AttributeError and the resulting HTTP 500 error.Resolution.The fix is available in the following versions:FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.12.FortiAuthenticator version 8.0.5

incidents.title: QUIC inspection mode unexpectedly changes when renaming an SSL/SSH profile in the GUI
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a known issue where the QUIC inspection mode in an SSL/SSH inspection profile is unexpectedly changed when the profile name is modified through the FortiGate GUI.ScopeFortiOS versions 7.4.13, 7.6.8 and 8.0.2.SolutionWhen an SSL/SSH inspection profile is renamed through the FortiGate GUI, the configured QUIC inspection mode is unexpectedly reset from inspect to bypass.As a result, the QUIC inspection configuration is not retained after renaming the profile through the GUI.This behavior has been confirmed in FortiOS…
incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue where the QUIC inspection mode in an SSL/SSH inspection profile is unexpectedly changed when the profile name is modified through the FortiGate GUI
incidents.solution: When an SSL/SSH inspection profile is renamed through the FortiGate GUI, the configured QUIC inspection mode is unexpectedly reset from inspect to bypass.As a result, the QUIC inspection configuration is not retained after renaming the profile through the GUI.This behavior has been confirmed in FortiOS versions 7.4.13, 7.6.8, and 8.0.2.Configuration before renaming through the GUI:The following configuration shows the original SSL/SSH inspection profile with QUIC inspection enabled:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "test-certificate-inspection" set comment "Read-only SSL handshake inspection profile." config https set ports 443 set status certificate-inspection set quic inspect set cert-probe-failure allow end next endConfiguration after renaming through the GUI:After changing the profile name through the GUI, the QUIC inspection mode is unexpectedly changed to bypass.config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "certificate-inspection_fqdn-test" set comment "Read-only SSL handshake inspection profile." config https set ports 443 set status certificate-inspection set quic bypass set cert-probe-failure allow end next end Contournement : There are two available workarounds:Option 1: Rename the SSL/SSH inspection profile using the CLI.Use the CLI to change the profile name instead of renaming it through the GUI.Option 2: Manually reapply the QUIC inspection mode through the CLI.If the profile has already been renamed through the GUI, manually configure the correct QUIC inspection mode:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit " " config https set quic inspect end next endVerify the configuration after applying the change:show firewall ssl-ssh-profile " "Confirm that the QUIC inspection mode is set to inspect.The issue is currently scheduled to be fixed in FortiOS version 8.0.3

incidents.title: Understanding MTU Drops, ICMP Fragmentation Needed, and Silent Packet Black Holes
incidents.summary: DescriptionHow Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) mismatches can lead to either expected ICMP error generation or silent packet drops within a network. A step-by-step breakdown of packet walks and diagnostic FortiOS commands is provided to help identify and resolve these connectivity issues.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionScenario 1: ICMP Fragmentation Needed (Layer-3 Egress Check)An ICMP Type 3, Code 4 ("Fragmentation Needed and DF Set") message is generated only when a packet successfully enters a FortiGate, is routed at Layer 3, and fails the MTU check as it…
incidents.symptom: How Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) mismatches can lead to either expected ICMP error generation or silent packet drops within a network. A step-by-step breakdown of packet walks and diagnostic FortiOS commands is provided to help identify and resolve these connectivity issues
incidents.solution: Scenario 1: ICMP Fragmentation Needed (Layer-3 Egress Check)An ICMP Type 3, Code 4 ("Fragmentation Needed and DF Set") message is generated only when a packet successfully enters a FortiGate, is routed at Layer 3, and fails the MTU check as it tries to exit (Egress) an outbound interface.Ingress on FortiGate R2 port2 (MTU 1500) — PASSES Layer 2:The 1444-byte IP packet (plus 14-byte Ethernet header = 1458-byte frame) arrives at port2. The physical NIC/ASIC checks: Is 1444 <= 1500? Yes. The hardware accepts the frame, strips the Outer Ethernet Layer-2 header, and hands the 1444-byte IP packet up to FortiOS's Layer-3 routing engine.Egress on FortiGate R2 port1 (MTU 1200) — FAILS Layer 3:The routing engine looks up the destination IP and determines the packet must exit port1. Before transmission, FortiOS checks port1's configured IP MTU (1200): Is 1444 <= 1200? No. Because the Don't Fragment (DF=1) bit is set, the Layer-3 engine drops the packet.Result:Because the packet is inside the Layer-3 IP engine, FortiGate R2 generates an ICMP Type 3, Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed, Next-Hop MTU = 1200) packet back to the source (FortiGate R1).config system interface edit "port1" set mtu-override

incidents.title: Upgrading a FortiGate High Availability cluster to version 8.0.1 may remove the ha-mgmt-interfaces configuration if the interface is set to dedicated-to management

incidents.symptom: An issue where a FortiGate High Availability (HA) cluster loses ha-mgmt-interfaces entry configuration upon upgrading to FortiOS 8.0.1
incidents.solution: After upgrading a FortiGate High Availability (HA) cluster to version 8.0.1 , the ha-mgmt-interfaces configuration is stripped from the HA settings.Check the config-error-log: diagnose debug config-error-log read >>> "set" "interface" "mgmt" @ global.system.ha.ha-mgmt-interfaces.1:value parse error (error -3) >>> "next" @ global.system.ha.ha-mgmt-interfaces.1:failed command (error -56)Configuration example before the upgrade:config system interface edit "mgmt" set vdom "root" set ip 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.240 set allowaccess ping https ssh snmp set type physical set dedicated-to management set snmp-index 1 next end config system ha set group-name "fortinet" set mode a-p set password FortinetPasswordMask set hbdev "ha" 0 set ha-mgmt-status enable config ha-mgmt-interfaces edit 1 set interface "mgmt" set gateway 192.168.1.2 next end set override disable endConfiguration change after the upgrade:config system interface edit "mgmt" set vdom "root" set ip 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.240 set allowaccess ping https ssh snmp set type physical set dedicated-to management set snmp-index 1 next end config system ha set group-name "fortinet" set mode a-p set password FortinetPasswordMask set hbde

incidents.symptom: An issue where users fail to establish a Single Sign-On session on FortiAuthenticator after Windows security updates, resulting in an NTLM authentication failure
incidents.solution: Users may experience Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication failures when using the Fortinet Single Sign-On (FSSO) Mobility Agent with FortiAuthenticator following the installation of Microsoft security updates released on November 10, 2026 (KB5135557).The issue results in NTLM authentication failures, preventing users from establishing SSO sessions on FortiAuthenticator. The logs display the error NT_STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED.11/11/2026 13:23:24 2B4BE6C0] NTLM auth result: 114 NTLM auth failed:Username/dcname(dc_time=1794399804...);error:NT_STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED]The issue is related to changes in NTLM signing behavior introduced by Microsoft's November 10, 2026 security updates. Windows clients now offer NTLM signing by default, which appears to cause a compatibility issue with the FSSO Mobility Agent.An internal engineering ticket has been raised to investigate the compatibility issue.Temporary workaround:If NTLM authentication must remain enabled, temporarily allow unsigned NTLM authentication on the affected Windows clients by applying the registry configuration documented in Microsoft's KB5135557.For further details, refer to the following Microsoft documentation:

incidents.title: Wi-Fi EAP-TLS authentication fails due to IPsec packet fragmentation
incidents.summary: DescriptionAn issue where RADIUS packets carrying client certificates are dropped across an IPsec tunnel, preventing successful EAP-TLS authentication on FortiAuthenticator.ScopeFortiGate, FortiAuthenticator.SolutionUsers cannot connect to a Wi-Fi SSID using EAP-TLS authentication. Packet captures show that FortiAuthenticator receives the RADIUS Access-Request and responds with an Access-Challenge, but no subsequent reply is received.
incidents.symptom: An issue where RADIUS packets carrying client certificates are dropped across an IPsec tunnel, preventing successful EAP-TLS authentication on FortiAuthenticator
incidents.solution: Users cannot connect to a Wi-Fi SSID using EAP-TLS authentication. Packet captures show that FortiAuthenticator receives the RADIUS Access-Request and responds with an Access-Challenge, but no subsequent reply is received. Further analysis reveals that client certificates are missing from the RADIUS packets arriving at the FortiAuthenticator.Root cause:Large RADIUS packets containing client certificates are dropped due to IPsec packet fragmentation across the data center tunnel. This prevents the full certificate information from reaching the FortiAuthenticator, causing the authentication process to fail.Resolution:Configure the IPsec tunnel to use post-encapsulation fragmentation. This ensures that large packets are fragmented after they are encrypted, allowing them to traverse the tunnel without being dropped.Access the Command Line Interface (CLI) of the FortiGate device.Modify the Phase 1 settings of the affected IPsec tunnel to set fragmentation to post-encapsulation.config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit set ip-fragmentation post-encapsulation set npu-offload disable next endVerify that the Wi-Fi endpoints can now successfully authenticate and connect to the SSID.Note: With p

aiReview.summary: Échec de l'authentification Wi-Fi EAP-TLS sur FortiAuthenticator en raison de paquets RADIUS volumineux fragmentés lors de leur traversée d'un tunnel IPsec.
aiReview.symptom: Les utilisateurs ne peuvent pas se connecter à un SSID Wi-Fi avec l'authentification EAP-TLS. Les captures de paquets montrent que FortiAuthenticator reçoit la requête Access-Request et répond par Access-Challenge, sans réponse ultérieure, et les certificats clients sont manquants.
aiReview.solution: Configurer le tunnel IPsec pour utiliser la fragmentation post-encapsulation (post-encapsulation fragmentation) en modifiant les paramètres de la phase 1 dans l'interface de ligne de commande (CLI) du FortiGate.
aiReview.note: La solution mentionne la configuration de la fragmentation post-encapsulation via la CLI FortiGate, sans inclure l'intégralité des commandes CLI.

incidents.symptom: Steps to verify FortiGuard FDS (AV/IPS and firmware images) connectivity from FortiManager when a web proxy is on the path to FortiGuard Servers. It describes the case when the FortiManager is used by FortiGates as local FDS, e.g. in air-gapped environment, and this FortiManager connecting to FortiGuard through an intermediate web proxy.Features an explanation of how to determine whether the proxy is well configured in tunnel or proxy mode, and why tunnel mode must be used on FortiManager 7.4 and above, as proxy settings for all FortiGuard services were consolidated under config system web-proxy in 7.4.0
incidents.solution: What has to be reachable.FortiManager, by default, accesses FDS for antivirus and attack updates through TCP/SSL port 443; firmware image updates also use TCP/443 to https://fds1.fortinet.com, and DNS resolution uses UDP/53.If a proxy sits between FortiManager and FDS, FortiManager can use:tcp port 443 to communicate with the proxy server in tunnel mode by defaultOr, in proxy mode, it then uses tcp port 80.Note: Allow the FortiGuard FQDNs dynamically rather than by IP: .fortinet.net, .fortinet.com, *.fortiguard.com, or the ISDB entry fortinet-fortiguard on the FortiGate side. The AV-IPS/firmware-image hosts per region setting are fds1.fortinet.com, usfds1.fortinet.com, eufds1.fortinet.com (unicast) and globalupdate.fortinet.net, usupdate.fortinet.net, euupdate.fortinet.net (anycast).Confirm the service itself is enabled.Starting with FortiManager 7.2.12, 7.4.8, 7.6.5 and above, the AV/IPS service must be explicitly enabled, as no objects are otherwise ever downloaded:config fmupdate service set avips enable endGUI equivalent: FortiGuard -> Settings -> AV/IPS service enabled for the relevant products. incidents.symptom: The message "Unable to complete FIDO token Authorization because token retry is not supported. Please start the login process from the beginning" is received after user inputs FIDO token while being authenticated via SAML where FortiAuthenticator acts as the SAML IDP
incidents.solution: A user receives the following message after inputting the FIDO token which is preceded by the SAML user login credentials: The following log entry is generated under Logging -> Log Access -> Logs , indicating that FortiAuthenticator is expecting FIDO token input and waiting for the user to provide it. cat="Event" subcat="Authentication" level="information" nas="example.com" action="Authentication" status="Pending" msg="Remote LDAP user authentication partially done, expecting fido token" user="user" Contournement : The "FIDO-only" option can be selected instead of the "Password and FIDO" combination in the Authentication section of the Service Provider settings in FortiAuthenticator. Note: This issue affects the FortiAuthenticator 6.6.x and 8.0.x release branches. For the 6.6.x branch, the issue is fixed in the upcoming release, 6.6.12. A special build for 6.6.11 is also available

incidents.summary: DescriptionA summary of NTLM and Kerberos use cases in FortiAuthenticator, as well as some known issues and workarounds to it.ScopeFortiAuthenticator.SolutionFortiAuthenticator uses NTLM and Kerberos in a few different instances. As NTLM is being increasingly deprecated, this can lead to some unexpected errors.FortiAuthenticator uses only NTLMv2 by default. It supports RC4, but defaults to AES. incidents.symptom: A summary of NTLM and Kerberos use cases in FortiAuthenticator, as well as some known issues and workarounds to it
incidents.solution: FortiAuthenticator uses NTLM and Kerberos in a few different instances. As NTLM is being increasingly deprecated, this can lead to some unexpected errors.FortiAuthenticator uses only NTLMv2 by default. It supports RC4, but defaults to AES. The encryption algorithm selection is determined by the server, so NTLMv2 servers should be configured to use AES only.FortiAuthenticator uses NTLM and/or Kerberos for the following:Domain JoinFSSOProxying NTLM trafficDomain joinFortiAuthenticator can be joined to a Windows Domain to allow for MS-CHAPv2 RADIUS authentication with a remote LDAP (Windows AD) server, and allow users to change their password securely via self-service portal or during the login process.The domain join process utilizes winbind, and uses NTLM and Kerberos both during joining and communicating with the domain controller.If NTLM is disabled, then the domain join and/or MS-CHAPv2 authentication may fail. aiReview.symptom: Erreurs inattendues liées à la dépréciation progressive de NTLM.

incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue where certain GUI components fail to load on FortiGate 6000 Chassis devices after upgrading to FortiOS version 7.6.8 GA.ScopeFortiGate 6k Chassis.SolutionThe issue affects both Global and VDOM dashboards, where CPU, Memory, and Session widgets remain unloaded. Additionally, the Network Interface pages under both Global and VDOM views fail to load. On the Firewall Policy page, it loads fine, but interface names are incorrectly displayed as [object Object], [object Object] instead of their actual names.On the…
incidents.symptom: This article describes an issue where certain GUI components fail to load on FortiGate 6000 Chassis devices after upgrading to FortiOS version 7.6.8 GA
incidents.solution: The issue affects both Global and VDOM dashboards, where CPU, Memory, and Session widgets remain unloaded. Additionally, the Network Interface pages under both Global and VDOM views fail to load. On the Firewall Policy page, it loads fine, but interface names are incorrectly displayed as [object Object], [object Object] instead of their actual names.On the Firewall Policy page:Steps to reproduce the issue.Log in to the GUI of the FortiGate 6000F running FortiOS version 7.6.8 GA.Navigate to the dashboard (System -> Dashboard).Observe that the Session, CPU, and Memory widgets keep loading indefinitely and never render.Navigate to System -> Network Interface.Observe that the page keeps loading indefinitely and never renders.The same issue is observed even in VDOM.The solution is to enable CSF on the FortiGate to fix the issue.config system csf set status enable set group-name fortinet endRoot cause:Starting with FortiOS version 7.6.4 GA, the SLBC GUI aggregator uses csfToken-based authentication, which requires CSF to be enabled for the GUI to function correctly.
