incidents.symptom: FortiManager fails to import or manually configure authentication rules for Agentless ZTNA portals when using form-based or SAML authentication schemes
incidents.solution: Symptoms.When importing a configuration from a FortiGate or attempting to manually configure an authentication rule for an Agentless ZTNA portal via FortiManager, the following error message appears:"authentication rule",FAIL,"(name=agentless-portal-rule, oid=3945, reason=invalid value - prop[n/a]: can only use http protocol.)"========FGT configuration============= FGT-HUB (ztna_portal-saml) # show config authentication rule edit "ztna_portal-saml" set protocol ztna-portal set active-auth-method "saml-ztna" next end FGT-HUB# show authentication scheme saml-ztna config authentication scheme edit "saml-ztna" set method saml set saml-server "saml-ztna" set user-database "ldap_server" next endThis error occurs even when the protocol is correctly set to ztna-portal. Root cause.A software bug in FortiManager version 7.6.7 prevents the validation of the ztna-portal protocol for authentication rules when the authentication scheme is configured for form-based or SAML methods. This causes the system to incorrectly require the http protocol, leading to import failures or configuration errors. Resolution.The fix is currently not available and is expected in an upcoming GA release

incidents.title: FortiManager global policy assignment fails with no write permission error
incidents.summary: Description An issue where global header policies fail to install on FortiGate devices from the Global ADOM when using the Automatically Install Policies to ADOM Devices option, resulting in a "No write permission" error. Scope FortiManager, FortiGate. Solution Symptoms When pushing global header policies from the Global ADOM to multiple ADOMs, the process fails at the end with the following error message: rootp:Firewall_Header_Policy_ADOM2 - no write permission This issue occurs specifically when the Automatically Install Policies to ADOM Devices…
incidents.symptom: An issue where global header policies fail to install on FortiGate devices from the Global ADOM when using the Automatically Install Policies to ADOM Devices option, resulting in a "No write permission" error
incidents.solution: Symptoms When pushing global header policies from the Global ADOM to multiple ADOMs, the process fails at the end with the following error message: rootp:Firewall_Header_Policy_ADOM2 - no write permission This issue occurs specifically when the Automatically Install Policies to ADOM Devices option is used in the Global DB assignment. Pushing policies individually from the ADOM works as expected. Root cause A software issue exists in FortiManager 7.6.8 where the automatic installation of global policies fails to obtain the necessary write permissions for the target devices when Workspace Mode is enabled. Resolution Use one of the following workarounds to resolve the issue Contournement : 1 : Lock both Global and Local ADOMs This method allows the use of the automatic installation feature while maintaining Workspace Mode. Lock the target Local ADOM. Lock the Global ADOM. Select "Global DB" and then select "Assignment". Select the target ADOM and select "Assign + Automatically Install to device". Workaround 2 : Manual policy reinstallation If locking ADOMs is not feasible, manually trigger the installation for the affected devices. Select multiple target devices within the ADOM. Click "Reinstall Policy" to push the configuration. Workaround 3 : Disable Workspace Mode Disable Workspace Mode temporarily to allow the automatic installation to function. Disable Workspace Mode in FortiManager. Select "Global DB" and then select "Assignment". Select "Assign + Automatically Install" from the Global ADOM. Resolution Use one of the following workarounds to resolve the issue Contournement : 1 : Lock both Global and Local ADOMs This method allows the use of the automatic installation feature while maintaining Workspace Mode. Lock the target Local ADOM. Lock the Global ADOM. Select "Global DB" and then select "Assignment". Select the target ADOM and select "Assign + Automatically Install to device". Workaround 2 : Manual policy reinstallation If locking ADOMs is not feasible, manually trigger the installation for the affected devices. Select multiple target devices within the ADOM. Click "Reinstall Policy" to push the configuration. Workaround 3 : Disable Workspace Mode Disable Workspace Mode temporarily to allow the automatic installation to function. Disable Workspace Mode in FortiManager. Select "Global DB" and then select "Assignment". Select "Assign + Automatically Install" from the Global ADOM.
